paper.title: Normal and pathogenic variation of RFC1 repeat expansions: implications for clinical diagnosis

persona.role: Rare-disease repeat-expansion researcher or laboratory scientist
persona.context: Research interpretation after an adult-onset ataxia workup

nonDiagnosticBoundary: This workflow uses a population reference to ask whether a comparable represented state occurs. It does not classify an individual's allele or make a diagnosis.

startingState.trigger: An externally characterized RFC1 repeat result with motif, approximate size, zygosity, and assay limitations.
inputs: Compatible research phenotype and RFC1 locus
GRCh38 coordinates, or a documented mapping to GRCh38
RP-PCR, Southern blot, OGM, or targeted long-read result
Motif, approximate size, interruptions, second allele, tissue, and uncertainty
startingState.question: Does this release contain comparable size, sequence-configuration, and local-haplotype states with adequate callability?
startingState.stopRule: If only a positive RP-PCR result is known and allele structure is missing, stop: the population browser cannot reconstruct it.

before: Record assay, tissue, build, motif spelling, total repeat units, interruptions, second allele, and uncertainty.
Normalize to the browser locus while retaining the original notation; do not turn paper observations into a universal size threshold.
inside: Open the RFC1 region with HGSVC/HPRC haplotypes and confirm GRCh38/Y1 provenance.
Inspect all alleles from one source event rather than treating normalized insertions as independent loci.
Compare length, exact sequence or motif decomposition, interruptions, global and stratum AC/AN, and carrier chromosome copies; treat the paper's 66 kb haplotype as a separate comparison.
after: Record the matching rule, callable denominator, missingness, release, run, and browser state.
Hand allele-level evidence to the research team for segregation, orthogonal sizing, phenotype review, and interpretation outside the browser.

branches.condition: An equivalent represented state is observed
branches.action: Report the exact matching rule and AC/AN; this supports population occurrence only.

branches.condition: The state is not observed but motif, long-allele, or callability data are incomplete
branches.action: Report unanswerable/data-blocked rather than zero.

branches.condition: The state is not observed in representation-complete callable data
branches.action: Report an upper-bound reference observation, never proof of pathogenicity.

story.given: a GRCh38 RFC1 allele characterized externally as an approximately 700-repeat AAAGG-containing expansion with an AAGGG allele on the other chromosome
story.when: the researcher opens the RFC1 event, selects all ALT alleles from that event, inspects full-cohort length plus exact motif/interruption structure, and filters carrying haplotypes
story.then: the browser returns exact or motif-similar reference observations with global and stratum callable AC/AN, release provenance, and an explicit not observed, not callable, or representation mismatch outcome, supporting only whether a comparable state is represented in this reference release

capabilities.step: Navigate to a bounded GRCh38 locus
capabilities.evidence: The checked region route returned HTTP 200; source limits Haplotype View to 100 kb.

capabilities.step: See reference allele lengths and carrier haplotypes
capabilities.evidence: The API returned 487 variants; one event has fragmented normalized alleles and AN values from 2 to 582.

capabilities.step: Compare complete motif and interruption structures
capabilities.evidence: Checked event records had empty motif fields; the repeat-count plot is not a sequence-structure distribution.

capabilities.step: Use denominator and provenance safely
capabilities.evidence: Global/population AC/AN and accepted provenance exist, but the CSV omits per-population AN and provenance.

capabilities.step: Reproduce and share the analysis
capabilities.evidence: The URL retains region/cohort/haplotype/search state, but not every filter, grouping, threshold, or provenance field.

acceptanceTest.fixture: One source event with a common short AAAGG allele, a long interrupted AAAGG allele, and a no-call chromosome copy.
acceptanceTest.actions: Open the event, inspect sequence decomposition and counts, search the long allele, and export the result.
acceptanceTest.expected: One event with three states; exact decomposition; allele/sample counts; global and stratum AC/AN; no-call count; release/run; identical exported values; and the carrying chromosome copy filtered.
acceptanceTest.forbidden: The result must not label either allele benign or pathogenic.

evidence.claim: The paper screened 893 adult-onset ataxia cases and 8,107 non-neurological controls using orthogonal repeat assays and selected targeted long reads.
evidence.citation: PDF pp. 3–5

evidence.claim: Selected affected AAAGG alleles were at least 600 repeats, while selected controls averaged 238; the paper did not establish a universal cutoff.
evidence.citation: PDF pp. 5–8, Fig. 2B

evidence.claim: A faithful replay starts with an externally characterized allele and asks about represented reference states rather than searching for affected individuals.
evidence.citation: Analyst reconstruction; requires workflow review

evidence.claim: The live API returned 487 variants in the checked region and highly variable AN among records at one RFC1 event.

paper.title: Father-to-offspring transmission of extremely long NOTCH2NLC repeat expansions with contractions: genetic and epigenetic profiling with long-read sequencing

persona.role: Neurogenetics or epigenetics researcher
persona.context: Researching why repeat length alone does not explain a family result

nonDiagnosticBoundary: A joint repeat/methylation reference observation can prioritize validation and characterize diversity. It cannot establish protection, penetrance, disease risk, or diagnosis.

startingState.trigger: A targeted long-read result or paper allele with repeat size/structure and an allele-specific methylation hypothesis.
inputs: Total GGC/GGA units and interruption pattern
Sample and tissue
Methylation assay/caller and coverage
Family phase and whether measurements are same-molecule or phase-linked
Reference build
startingState.question: Does a joint long-repeat and shifted-methylation state occur on one reference chromosome copy, and can that join be reproduced?
startingState.stopRule: If only sample-total methylation or no confirmed phase link is available, stop before assigning methylation to an allele.

before: Record repeat assay, exact units, tissue, methylation caller, family phase, build, and measurement-linkage semantics.
inside: Open the NOTCH2NLC region and verify primary, haplotype, and methylation provenance.
Select the TR event and inspect full allele-length and exact sequence/motif states.
Use Diploid view and confirmed per-copy methylation to compare copy A and B across chr1:149390115–149391841; A/B is not maternal/paternal.
Preserve copy-level points, CpG coverage, confidence, missingness, and mapping/orientation receipt.
after: Export copy rows, CpGs/coverage, repeat state, source identity/orientation receipt, URL settings, and caveats for collaborator review.

branches.condition: A same-copy joint state is supported
branches.action: Report a reference observation that requires orthogonal, locus-specific validation.

branches.condition: Only sample-total methylation or no phase linkage is available
branches.action: Do not attribute the profile to either allele.

branches.condition: No long allele is shown
branches.action: Do not claim absence unless caller range and no-call denominator are explicit.

story.given: an externally resolved NOTCH2NLC GGC expansion and an allele-specific methylation hypothesis
story.when: the researcher selects the NOTCH2NLC TR event, enters Diploid view, enables confirmed per-copy methylation, and compares repeat structure with CpGs across chr1:149390115–149391841 on copy A and copy B
story.then: the browser either displays a same-copy joint state with coverage and mapping provenance or explicitly reports that the measurements cannot be joined, supporting only prioritization of a reference configuration for follow-up

capabilities.step: Browse repeat and population length states
capabilities.evidence: The API returned 89 TRV alleles, but motif fields were empty and event reconciliation with the paper locus is required.

capabilities.step: View sample-total methylation
capabilities.evidence: The API returned 146 CpGs in the paper interval; source explicitly labels totals as non-allele-specific.

capabilities.step: Join methylation to chromosome copies
capabilities.evidence: The API reports AVAILABLE_CONFIRMED and source renders A/B with an orientation receipt, but phase_set was null in checked records.

capabilities.step: Compare exact repeat structure and methylation on one copy
capabilities.evidence: No tested contract proves that exact TR sequence and CpGs are jointly linked at this locus; motifs were empty.

capabilities.step: Interpret the state as protection or pathogenicity
capabilities.evidence: The paper includes four ascertained families, blood/LCL context, mosaicism, and no penetrance threshold.

capabilities.step: Export a reproducible multimodal result
capabilities.evidence: Current CSV is variant-only and omits CpGs, mapping receipt, tissue/caller provenance, and UI settings.

acceptanceTest.fixture: Two chromosome copies with different GGC lengths and CpG profiles plus one unassigned read set; also a sample-total-only fixture.
acceptanceTest.actions: Enable per-copy methylation, inspect copy mapping, export, swap the orientation receipt, and load the total-only fixture.
acceptanceTest.expected: Each profile appears only under its confirmed copy; unassigned data remains separate; coverage and mapping/phase receipt are exported; a swapped receipt fails closed; total-only data disables same-copy wording.
acceptanceTest.forbidden: The result must not call copy A/B maternal/paternal or infer protection, penetrance, pathogenicity, or diagnosis.

evidence.claim: Four ascertained trios were studied; affected-offspring median repeats were 93–162 and paternal medians were approximately 390–650.
evidence.citation: PDF pp. 1–5, Fig. 1

evidence.claim: Fathers' long alleles showed a roughly 2.2 kb gain-of-methylation, while affected alleles were predominantly unmethylated, with epigenetic mosaicism.
evidence.citation: PDF pp. 4, 6–7, Fig. 4

evidence.claim: The browser operation must join repeat and methylation states on the same chromosome copy; sample totals cannot answer the question.
evidence.citation: Analyst reconstruction; requires workflow review

evidence.claim: The checked API exposed summary and joined methylation, AVAILABLE_CONFIRMED capability, a 100 kb limit, and a chromosome-wide orientation receipt.
evidence.citation: Read-only browser/API capability check, 2026-08-11

paper.title: High clinical utility of long-read sequencing for precise diagnosis of congenital adrenal hyperplasia in 322 probands

persona.role: Molecular genetics researcher or laboratory scientist
persona.context: Research review of discordance among phenotype, locus-specific sequencing, MLPA, and family data

nonDiagnosticBoundary: The browser can ask whether a comparable copy-resolved population structure is represented. It cannot diagnose CAH or assign pathogenicity from population presence.

startingState.trigger: A copy-number/marker result such as a deletion chimera on one chromosome and duplicated marker-bearing CYP21-related copies on the other.
inputs: MLPA dosage and locus-specific sequence calls
Pedigree and phase
Phenotype context for research handoff
Genome build and assay copy-specificity
Ordered RCCX modules, copy identities, markers, and uncertainty
startingState.question: Is a comparable ordered, copy-assigned RCCX configuration represented, and can each marker be assigned to functional gene, pseudogene, or chimera?
startingState.stopRule: A generic DEL/DUP overlap is only a candidate structural call; stop before naming a chimera or duplicated haplotype.

before: Decompose the result by chromosome into ordered RCCX modules, CYP21 copy identity, variants, phase, and uncertainty while retaining original notation.
inside: Open the 85 kb region, verify genes/build, and remember GRCh38 is one haplotype rather than a universal module order.
Search exact markers and junction intervals; inspect summary CNVs with global/stratum AC/AN and callability.
Compare both chromosome copies in Diploid view, requiring copy labels, module order, conversion tract, breakpoint interval, and supporting records.
after: Export a two-chromosome structural diagram and machine-readable module, junction, marker, denominator, and provenance receipt for review and orthogonal validation.

branches.condition: Only a generic DEL/DUP overlaps
branches.action: Report candidate overlap and do not infer a chimera or module structure.

branches.condition: A copy-resolved structure matches
branches.action: Report occurrence and callable denominator without transferring the paper's affected-cohort proportion or clinical effect.

branches.condition: A marker appears only in a pseudogene or extra copy
branches.action: Report its copy context; do not label it a disease allele.

story.given: a P54-like research result with aggregate MLPA dosage and two sequence markers
story.when: the researcher opens the RCCX locus, searches the markers and breakpoint interval, and compares both chromosome copies in Diploid view
story.then: the browser distinguishes functional CYP21A2, CYP21A1P, and recombinant or duplicated copies, places each marker and junction with confidence, and reports callable-copy AC/AN, supporting only whether a comparable population structure is represented and whether locus-specific validation is warranted

capabilities.step: Navigate, search variants, and compare phased carriers
capabilities.evidence: The API returned 1,686 records; source supports ID/position/REF>ALT search, Diploid view, carriers, and CSV.

capabilities.step: See candidate large DEL/DUP calls
capabilities.evidence: Large generic events are visible, but they do not identify an RCCX configuration.

capabilities.step: Make prevalence or frequency comparisons
capabilities.evidence: Some complex records show AF 0.5 with AN of only 2 or 6; structure-specific callable denominators are absent.

capabilities.step: Assign modules, copy identity, chimera, and markers
capabilities.evidence: No first-class module count/order, copy identity, conversion tract, or chimera subtype is present.

capabilities.step: Reproduce P54 copy-number cancellation logic
capabilities.evidence: No upload or copy-specific dosage schematic joins opposite-chromosome structures.

capabilities.step: Export a reviewable structural result
capabilities.evidence: Variant CSV omits modules, per-population AN, callability, provenance, and UI settings.

acceptanceTest.actions: Open both chromosome copies, place markers and junctions, inspect uncertainty and denominators, then export.

acceptanceTest.forbidden: The result must not diagnose CAH, infer a chimera from generic overlap, or treat affected-cohort proportions as population frequency.

evidence.claim: The paper clinically ascertained 322 probands and 240 relatives and used 7.0–8.5 kb locus-specific PacBio CCS products.

paper.title: Long-read sequencing identifies a common transposition haplotype predisposing for CLCNKB deletions

locus: CLCNKA/CLCNKB · chr1:16,000,000–16,077,660 (GRCh38 overview; event remap required)

persona.role: Structural-variation researcher or laboratory scientist
persona.context: Research follow-up after a whole-gene CLCNKB deletion or apparently hemizygous small variant

nonDiagnosticBoundary: This workflow separates a common reference background from a linked deletion architecture. Population occurrence cannot prove predisposition, benignity, pathogenicity, or diagnosis.

startingState.trigger: An MLPA/WES CNV or small CLCNKB variant plus paper hg19 junction intervals and family phase.
inputs: Original hg19 paper coordinates
Classification as background junction, deletion junction, small variant, or hybrid-gene join
Validated event-aware remap to GRCh38 with sequence context
Family phase and assay limitations
startingState.question: Is the common transposition background or a comparable linked deletion architecture represented in reference haplotypes?
startingState.stopRule: If event-aware remapping is ambiguous in paralogous sequence, do not place a precise GRCh38 overlay.

before: Retain hg19 paper coordinates and classify every item as background, deletion, small variant, or hybrid join.
Obtain a validated event-aware GRCh38 remap with source/target sequence context; stop if ambiguous.
inside: Open a ≤100 kb overview and inspect CLCNKA/B orientation and homologous blocks.
Search the common transposition and each linked deletion junction as one architecture; compare exact versus overlap matches, source records, copies, and AC/AN.
after: Export paper build/coordinates, remap receipt, matching rule, linked junctions, carrier/callable denominators, release provenance, and browser state.

branches.condition: Only the common transposition is represented
branches.action: Report common reference background; do not call a CLCNKB deletion.

branches.condition: Only a generic approximately 23 kb DEL/DUP overlaps
branches.action: Report candidate overlap; do not assign paper architecture A–H.

branches.condition: A linked architecture is resolved
branches.action: Report reference occurrence/callability separately from the affected paper cohort; predisposition remains a hypothesis.

story.given: an hg19 CLCNKB deletion architecture and a small variant suspected to be in trans
story.when: the researcher supplies a validated GRCh38 remap, searches the common transposition and deletion junctions as linked events, and compares both chromosome copies
story.then: the browser distinguishes common background only, candidate generic CNV, and resolved linked deletion architecture, with callable AC/AN and provenance, supporting only whether comparable reference structures are represented

capabilities.step: Reach a bounded locus and inspect variants/haplotypes
capabilities.evidence: The API returned 2,439 records in the overview; the existing paper card's smaller region remains approximate.

capabilities.step: See candidate large structural calls
capabilities.evidence: Twenty-six large/duplication candidates were returned, including approximately 22–23 kb generic calls with sparse AN.

capabilities.step: Distinguish background from A–H architecture
capabilities.evidence: There is no first-class transposition-background or linked-junction A–H annotation.

capabilities.step: Map paper events safely across builds
capabilities.evidence: No event-aware literature remap and sequence-context receipt exists in the browser.

capabilities.step: Estimate recurrence, founder effect, or predisposition
capabilities.evidence: Reference N and structure callability are insufficient; the paper itself does not establish prospective risk.

capabilities.step: Export linked evidence
capabilities.evidence: Variant CSV cannot preserve linked junctions, remap provenance, callability, or full analysis state.

acceptanceTest.actions: Try an hg19 overlay without and then with a remap receipt, compare linked events and copies, and export.
acceptanceTest.expected: Three distinct labels; an hg19 overlay without receipt is rejected; exact/overlap matching and global/stratum callable denominators are shown; linked identities export.
acceptanceTest.forbidden: The result must not call any fixture pathogenic, infer A–H from generic overlap, or establish predisposition.

paper.title: Optimized testing strategy for the diagnosis of GAA- FGF14 ataxia

persona.role: Repeat-expansion researcher or laboratory scientist
persona.context: Research comparison after an externally performed FGF14 sizing and sequence assay

nonDiagnosticBoundary: This workflow asks whether a comparable sequence-resolved reference allele is represented and with what callable denominator. It cannot diagnose an individual, classify an allele, transfer the paper's threshold or calibration, or infer pathogenicity or benignity from population occurrence or absence.

startingState.trigger: An external FGF14 result with an allele pair, assay-specific size estimate, and preferably bidirectional motif or sequence information.
inputs: Original assay and laboratory: fLR-PCR/capillary electrophoresis, gel sizing, bidirectional RP-PCR, Sanger sequencing, nanopore sequencing, or another declared method
Raw allele-size estimate and any locally calibrated estimate, kept as separate values with control/calibration provenance
Both alleles, cyclic motif spelling, 5′ and 3′ interruption or polymorphism information, tissue, and uncertainty
Reference build and a documented mapping to GRCh38 chr13:102161575–102161726
A predeclared matching rule: exact ALT sequence, sequence-decomposed repeat count and interruption pattern, or length-only similarity
Browser release, cohort, source event, global and stratum AC/AN, and missingness/callability fields
startingState.question: Does this release contain an exact-sequence or explicitly weaker length/composition match to the externally characterized FGF14 allele, after keeping assay-specific sizing uncertainty separate?
startingState.stopRule: Stop exact comparison if the build, assay basis, allele pair, or sequence/motif evidence is missing; do not convert an uncalibrated capillary estimate with the paper's cohort-specific regression or use the paper's clinical threshold in the browser.

before: Record both alleles, original motif notation, assay, tissue, raw size, locally calibrated size, controls, sequence coverage, interruptions, and uncertainty without replacing the original measurement.

Normalize the locus to GRCh38 chr13:102161575–102161726 while retaining the source coordinates; bridge it to source event chr13-102161564-TRV-280 rather than treating the event's 281 bp reference span as the repeat tract.
Choose and label the matching rule before looking at population data: exact sequence is strongest; length-only similarity must remain a weaker result.
inside: Open chr13:102111564–102211564 with HGSVC/HPRC and verify dataset, cohort, reference build, accepted Y1 source, run, and chromosome scope.
Select all ALT records sharing source_variant_id chr13-102161564-TRV-280; do not interpret its normalized alleles as independent loci.

Compare the external allele to exact ALT sequence and event-level base-pair difference only on the declared basis; never silently equate event length with GAA repeat count or apply the paper's fLR-PCR correction.
For any candidate match, retain global and ancestry/sex-stratum AC/AN and the exact allele ID; distinguish an exact sequence match from same-length but structurally unresolved alleles.

Inspect motif, interruption, purity, full-cohort repeat-count distribution, and chromosome-copy linkage availability. If fields are empty or unavailable, report the corresponding comparison as data-blocked rather than absent.
after: Return one bounded outcome: exact-sequence represented, length-only represented, not observed in representation-complete callable data, or representation/data blocked.

Record the matching rule, external assay basis, raw and locally calibrated values, source event and allele ID, AC/AN by reported stratum, missingness, release/run, evidence date, and browser/API query state.
Hand the reference observation to the research or laboratory team for orthogonal sizing, segregation, phenotype review, and interpretation outside the browser.

branches.condition: Build, assay basis, second allele, or motif/sequence evidence is missing
branches.action: Stop exact comparison and request the missing source result; do not reconstruct an allele from a positive RP-PCR or a single size number.

branches.condition: Only an uncalibrated fLR-PCR/capillary size is available
branches.action: Preserve it as assay-specific and uncertain; do not apply the paper's regression or threshold as a universal conversion.

branches.condition: An exact ALT sequence match is represented with explicit AC/AN
branches.action: Report the allele ID, matching rule, AC/AN, strata, and provenance as population-reference occurrence only.

branches.condition: Only event-level length is similar while motif, purity, or interruptions are unresolved
branches.action: Report length-only similarity and mark structural equivalence data-blocked; do not call the alleles comparable in sequence.

branches.condition: No candidate match is returned but sequence representation, distribution, or callability is incomplete
branches.action: Report unanswerable/data-blocked rather than zero or absent.

branches.condition: No candidate match is observed in representation-complete callable data
branches.action: Report not observed with the exact denominator and release; this is not evidence of pathogenicity.

story.given: an externally characterized FGF14 allele pair, such as the paper's 266/417 example, with assay-labeled sizes, locally controlled calibration if used, bidirectional motif evidence, and sequence uncertainty
story.when: the researcher opens the corrected GRCh38 window, selects every ALT from source event chr13-102161564-TRV-280, compares exact sequence before length-only similarity, and checks AC/AN, motif, distribution, and callability provenance
story.then: the browser returns an exact-sequence represented, length-only represented, not observed in callable representation-complete data, or representation/data-blocked outcome with allele ID, global and stratum AC/AN, release/run, and limitations, supporting only whether a comparable state is represented in this reference release

capabilities.step: Open the corrected GRCh38 FGF14 window and resolve the source event
capabilities.evidence: On 2026-08-11 the deployed region and exact-allele routes returned HTTP 200, and the live API resolved source event chr13-102161564-TRV-280 at chr13:102161564–102161844.

capabilities.step: Inspect the complete event allelic series with global and stratum AC/AN
capabilities.evidence: The live API returned 139 ALT rows (indices 1–139), each with AN 584, per-stratum AC/AN, and exact ALT sequence; current source groups these as a TR Allelic Series, but the operation starts from one allele-specific page and event-level length differences.

capabilities.step: Compare an external repeat count on a declared assay basis
capabilities.evidence: The API reports exact ALT and event-level base-pair difference (-121 to +1791 bp), not an assay-aware FGF14 tract repeat count; there is no field for fLR-PCR, gel, nanopore, controls, calibration, or sizing uncertainty.

capabilities.step: Compare motif order, interruptions, and purity
capabilities.evidence: Exact ALT sequences are available, but all 139 event rows had empty motifs and null main_reference_region; no first-class decomposition or purity/interruption comparison is exposed.

capabilities.step: Use full-cohort repeat-count and genotype distributions at this event
capabilities.evidence: The exact live API query returned no allele-size groups, no genotype groups, and null max_repunits for chr13-102161564-TRV-280~139.

capabilities.step: Follow a candidate allele onto a confirmed chromosome copy
capabilities.evidence: A haplotype route and current-source haplotype components exist, but the bounded live exact-position haplotype_groups query returned null; copy linkage for this event was not independently demonstrated.

capabilities.step: Apply the paper's threshold or regression to classify an individual
capabilities.evidence: The paper's threshold and correction were assay- and cohort-specific, and the preprint itself says it should not guide clinical practice; population occurrence or absence cannot diagnose or classify an allele.

capabilities.step: Reproduce and export the complete comparison
capabilities.evidence: The region URL preserves dataset/cohort/haplotype state and the API is reproducible, but no single export joins external assay/calibration, exact sequence matching, missingness, accepted Y1 run provenance, and all UI settings.

acceptanceTest.fixture: One FGF14 source event containing an exact sequence match, a same-length interrupted allele, a distinct long pure-repeat allele, and one uncallable chromosome copy, plus an external result with separate raw and locally calibrated assay values.
acceptanceTest.actions: Open the corrected window, select the source event, compare exact sequence before length, inspect motif/purity/interruptions and global/stratum denominators, search the carrying copy, and export the result.
acceptanceTest.expected: One event with distinct allele states; exact sequence and tract-level repeat decomposition; raw versus calibrated assay values kept separate; allele and callable/no-call counts; global and stratum AC/AN; accepted release/run; explicit exact, length-only, not observed, or data-blocked outcome; and an export that reproduces those values.
acceptanceTest.forbidden: The result must not diagnose GAA-FGF14 ataxia, label an allele benign or pathogenic, apply the paper's 250-repeat threshold or calibration universally, equate event-level length with GAA count, or turn incomplete data into absence.

evidence.claim: The paper evaluated a three-step strategy using fLR-PCR, bidirectional 5′/3′ RP-PCR, then gel electrophoresis and/or Sanger sequencing, comparing 28 French Canadian participants (22 patients and six controls) with targeted nanopore data and validating in 53 French index patients.
evidence.citation: PDF pp. 3–6; Fig. 1 legend, p. 17

evidence.claim: Uncorrected capillary fLR-PCR systematically undersized expanded alleles versus nanopore and gel (slopes 0.87 and 0.84; biases -8.54% and -10.91%) and produced four false-negative classifications among 28 comparison participants; alleles above 400 repeats exceeded capillary sizing range.
evidence.citation: PDF pp. 3, 7; Fig. 3 legend, pp. 17–18

evidence.claim: Correction derived from four internally characterized alleles made fLR-PCR estimates comparable to nanopore and gel in this study, with slopes 0.98 and 0.94; this is paper-specific calibration evidence, not a transferable browser conversion.
evidence.citation: PDF pp. 7–8; Fig. 3E–H legend, pp. 17–18

evidence.claim: The proposed assay stops after two alleles below the paper's threshold; a single capillary-detected allele triggers gel sizing because a second very large allele may be missed; flat or atypical RP-PCR profiles trigger sequence resolution.
evidence.citation: PDF pp. 5–9; Fig. 1, p. 19

evidence.claim: Figure examples include 9/280, 9/510, 17/319, 43/370, 58/300, and compound 266/417 allele pairs; the larger 417 allele in the compound example was missed by fLR-PCR capillary detection.
evidence.citation: PDF pp. 9, 17–18; Figs. 2D–E and 4A–B

evidence.claim: The compound 266/417 sample had distinct 5′ polymorphic structures, reported as (GAA)(GAAA)(GGA)(GAA)n and (GAA)(GAAA)(GAAA)(GAA)n; combined forward/reverse Sanger covered alleles up to about 500 repeats in this study.
evidence.citation: PDF p. 9; Fig. 4C–D legend, p. 18

evidence.claim: Maternal transmission of a 467-repeat allele yielded 492- and 510-repeat alleles in two meiotic events in one family.
evidence.citation: PDF pp. 10, 12; Fig. 4A legend, p. 18

evidence.claim: A population-browser replay must begin with an externally measured allele, preserve assay uncertainty, and ask about represented reference states rather than reenact the paper's diagnostic decision tree.
evidence.citation: Analyst reconstruction from PDF pp. 5–11; requires workflow review

evidence.claim: Exact ALT sequence, length-only similarity, no observation in callable complete data, and data/representation blocked must be separate outcomes because same length does not establish the same interruption structure.
evidence.citation: Analyst reconstruction; requires data-semantics and product review

evidence.claim: The corrected GRCh38 target interval chr13:102161575–102161726 is 152 bp of cyclic AAG/GAA repeat sequence and lies inside the 281 bp current source event chr13:102161564–102161844.
evidence.citation: Ensembl GRCh38 sequence REST check and live API event check, 2026-08-11

paper.title: Simultaneous measurement of the size and methylation of chromosome 4qA-D4Z4 repeats in facioscapulohumeral muscular dystrophy by long-read sequencing

locus: 4qA-D4Z4, 4qB-D4Z4, and 10q-D4Z4 · custom-reference/homology mapping; no validated linear GRCh38 interval

persona.role: Repeat-expansion or epigenetics researcher
persona.context: Population-reference follow-up after an external assay has jointly measured D4Z4 array length and native-DNA methylation

nonDiagnosticBoundary: This workflow can support only a technically qualified, locus- and length-conditioned population-reference observation once a validated D4Z4 data model exists. It cannot diagnose FSHD, classify an array, or infer pathogenicity, benignity, penetrance, or risk.

startingState.trigger: An externally resolved D4Z4 chromosome copy, or a research question about the reference distribution of D4Z4 repeat count and distal-array methylation.
inputs: Original locus-assignment evidence, including proximal p13E-11 and distal 4qA-versus-10q discriminating anchors
Full-length molecule or phase-linked array record with D4Z4 repeat-unit count and orientation
Native-DNA methylation calls with CpG/read coverage and a stable molecule or chromosome-copy identifier
Tissue, extraction, enrichment, sequencing, caller, batch, and reference provenance
Explicit missing/no-output records for every roster sample and candidate chromosome copy
startingState.question: Among reference individuals not ascertained for FSHD, do confidently locus- and chromosome-copy-resolved D4Z4 arrays show comparable joint repeat-count and distal-array methylation states after conditioning on 4qA/4qB/10q identity, full-length coverage, missingness, tissue, and assay provenance?
startingState.stopRule: Stop before region navigation if only custom-reference-relative coordinates are available; do not invent a GRCh38 interval. Stop before locus-specific comparison if 4qA, 4qB, and 10q assignment is absent or ambiguous. Stop before same-copy wording if repeat count and methylation lack a stable molecule/chromosome-copy join. Stop before an absence claim if full-array callability and no-output denominators are unavailable.

before: Record original assay, sample/person identity, tissue, extraction, native-versus-bisulfite measurement, caller, batch, reference, locus anchors, full-length criterion, RU count, and uncertainty without translating custom coordinates.
Require proximal and distal anchor evidence to classify each full-length array as 4qA, 4qB, 10q, or unresolved; retain anchor-level QC and do not infer 4qB from non-4qA status.
Check for a validated, versioned D4Z4 locus model that maps custom array coordinates to GRCh38 while preserving 4qA/4qB/10q identity and homology ambiguity.
inside: For each resolved full-length chromosome copy, show RU count, molecule/read support, array completeness, orientation from proximal to distal RU1, and structural exceptions such as the 1.3 kb proximal-RU deletion.
Display CpG methylation and coverage for each chromosome copy without assigning parental identity; preserve HAP1/HAP2-to-GT1/GT2 orientation receipt and explicit unavailable samples.

Join methylation to the same resolved array and present molecule traces or copy-level summaries by RU ordinal from proximal to distal, separating RU1 promoter from RU1 gene body and showing uncovered intervals.

Compare distal-array methylation only among callable arrays matched by locus (4qA, 4qB, or 10q), RU count band, tissue/assay, coverage, and technical batch; keep external paper cases separate from reference participants.
after: Export a reviewable receipt containing custom and validated reference identities, locus anchors, array/RU structure, CpG and molecule coverage, tissue/assay/batch, all callable and missing denominators, orientation receipt, release/run identity, filters, and safety wording.

paper.title: Accurate long-read sequencing identified GBA1 as major risk factor in the Luxembourgish Parkinson’s study

locus: GBA1/GBA1LP (GBAP1) · GBA1 chr1:155,234,452–155,244,699; GBA1LP chr1:155,213,821–155,227,574 (GRCh38, pinned browser annotation)

persona.role: Neurogenetics researcher or molecular laboratory scientist
persona.context: Research review of a GBA1 call or recombinant-like marker set at a locus where the pseudogene and complex structures can confound copy assignment

nonDiagnosticBoundary: This population-reference workflow can ask whether a comparable copy-assigned sequence or structural state is represented. It cannot diagnose Parkinson’s or Gaucher disease, classify an allele, or transfer the paper’s Parkinson’s disease odds ratios to HGSVC/HPRC participants.

startingState.trigger: An externally normalized GBA1/GBAP1 variant set, conversion-like tract, hybrid, or duplication hypothesis with assay and phase evidence.
inputs: Original HGVS/protein notation, transcript, reference build, strand, and normalization receipt; retain the paper’s GRCh37/NM_001005742 notation separately from GRCh38 browser coordinates
Assay type and blind spots, including primer coordinates, amplification specificity, coverage, allele dropout, size-selection limits, and whether GBAP1 was sequenced
Per-chromosome sequence or assembly path spanning unique flanks, all GBA-related copies, and the inter-copy interval
Pinned GBA1 and GBAP1/GBA1LP reference sequences plus a versioned panel of paralog-diagnostic markers
Copy number, order, orientation, breakpoint intervals, phased small variants, unresolved bases, and confidence
startingState.question: Can each observed variant or donor-like tract be assigned to a specific GBA1, GBAP1, hybrid, duplicated, or unresolved physical copy on one chromosome, and is a comparable callable structural haplotype represented in this release?
startingState.stopRule: If evidence consists only of the paper’s GBA1-specific amplicon, a flat SNV list, or a generic DEL/INS/DUP overlap without unique-flank anchors and a diagnostic-marker path, stop before assigning GBAP1, conversion boundaries, hybrid identity, copy order, or duplication origin.

before: Preserve the source assay result exactly, then normalize each small variant and breakpoint to GRCh38 while retaining original build/transcript notation and a mapping receipt; protein labels alone are not browser queries.

Pin locus annotation and reference sequences. The checked browser annotation is GBA1 ENSG00000177628.16 at chr1:155234452–155244699 and GBA1LP ENSG00000160766.15, gencode symbol GBAP1, at chr1:155213821–155227574; both are on the minus strand.

Build a chromosome-level evidence object from unique left/right flanks through every GBA-related segment. Record physical copy count, order, orientation, gaps, local assembly/read support, and a versioned set of GBA1-versus-GBAP1 diagnostic markers.

Predeclare matching levels: exact sequence-and-path match; same copy class with different tract boundary; marker-similar only; generic interval overlap; unresolved. Do not let generic overlap satisfy a copy-identity match.
inside: Open chr1:155200000–155300000 with HGSVC/HPRC haplotypes and confirm GRCh38/Y1 provenance, the pinned gene models, cohort, run, and chromosome-wide source identity.

Select one sample strand at a time and require unique-flank anchors before interpreting the linear variant rows. Compare its sequence simultaneously against the pinned GBA1 and GBAP1 references rather than assigning origin from genomic overlap alone.

Lay out every physical segment in chromosome order and orientation. Label a canonical GBA1 or GBAP1 copy only when its flanks and diagnostic-marker majority agree; retain conflicting or uncovered segments as unresolved.

Call a conversion-like tract only on an anchored recipient copy when a contiguous run of donor-paralog diagnostic markers is bounded on both sides by recipient markers. Report the tract as an interval between the nearest informative markers, with marker count, conflicts, coverage, and uncertainty; do not convert it into an exact breakpoint.

Call a hybrid candidate only when one physical copy has a supported transition in backbone/paralog identity with a junction interval. Call a duplication only when the chromosome path contains an extra physical copy; assign that copy’s GBA1-like, GBAP1-like, hybrid, or unresolved origin independently and preserve copy order.

Assign small variants only after copy identity. A RecNciI-like marker pattern requires p.L483P, p.A495P, and p.V499V in cis on the same GBA1-assigned copy after build/transcript normalization. The three markers alone do not establish conversion boundaries, a reciprocal product, or a locus-spanning structural mechanism.

Group copies into structural classes only after representation reconciliation. For each class show exact-match count, callable chromosome-haplotype denominator, unresolved/no-call count, participants represented, sampling-group strata, release/run, matching rule, and query receipt.
after: Export a machine-readable per-chromosome path: participant, sample strand, unique-flank anchors, ordered segments, copy labels, orientation, diagnostic markers, tract/junction intervals, linked variants, confidence, unresolved sequence, matching level, and provenance.

Use orthogonal locus-specific sequencing, breakpoint validation, or assembly review for candidate hybrids, duplications, and conversion tracts; use segregation, phenotype, and expert interpretation outside the population browser.

Report only observed, not observed in callable copies, representation mismatch, or data-blocked. Keep the paper’s 77/637 versus 34/675 and OR 2.6 (1.6–4.1) confined to its filtered clinical case-control cohort.

branches.condition: Unique flanks and diagnostic markers support one canonical GBA1 and one canonical GBAP1 copy
branches.action: Assign small variants to the supported physical copy and report the two-copy chromosome path with callable-copy evidence.

branches.condition: An anchored recipient copy contains a bounded contiguous donor-like marker run
branches.action: Report a conversion-like tract with informative-marker bounds and uncertainty; keep the recipient copy identity explicit.

branches.condition: A physical copy changes paralog backbone across a supported junction
branches.action: Report a hybrid candidate and its ordered segment path; do not infer a reciprocal product unless independently observed.

branches.condition: An extra physical GBA-related copy is supported
branches.action: Report duplication and copy order, then assign each copy’s origin independently; use unresolved when marker or flank support is insufficient.

branches.condition: Only flat variant rows or generic approximately 20.6–61.8 kb events with sparse AN are available
branches.action: Report candidate overlap/representation blocked; do not name a conversion, hybrid, duplication origin, or RecNciI mechanism.

branches.condition: No comparable state is observed but structure-specific callability is incomplete
branches.action: Report data-blocked rather than zero or absent.

branches.condition: No comparable state is observed in representation-complete callable chromosome haplotypes
branches.action: Report a bounded reference non-observation with the callable denominator; do not infer pathogenicity or risk.

story.given: a GRCh38-normalized RecNciI-like three-marker set or conversion/hybrid hypothesis plus one chromosome-spanning sequence path, assay provenance, and a pinned GBA1/GBAP1 diagnostic-marker panel
story.when: the researcher opens chr1:155200000–155300000, selects the relevant sample strand, anchors unique flanks, orders every GBA-related segment, compares each segment simultaneously to GBA1 and GBAP1, bounds donor-like marker runs, and applies exact-versus-overlap matching with callable-copy accounting
story.then: the browser returns GBA1, GBAP1, conversion-like, hybrid, duplicated, or unresolved copy assignments with ordered segments, linked variants, marker and breakpoint uncertainty, exact/callable/no-call counts, and release/run/query provenance, supporting only whether a comparable population-reference state is represented

capabilities.evidence: The exact 100 kb route and REST request returned HTTP 200 on 2026-08-11. Live gene queries returned GBA1 chr1:155234452–155244699 and GBA1LP/GBAP1 chr1:155213821–155227574, both minus-strand GRCh38 models.

capabilities.evidence: The live payload returned 1,586 variant rows and 584 sample-strand rows for 292 diploid participants, with variant-level AC/AN and phase sidecars; 7,473 carrier-variant associations were ambiguous unphased.

capabilities.evidence: Position/ID/REF>ALT search and strand grouping exist, but paper protein labels require external build/transcript normalization and no first-class RecNciI allele object or diagnostic-marker receipt exists.

capabilities.evidence: The API/source variant model has linear position, alleles, type, length, frequencies, and sample strand, but no paralog-diagnostic marker panel, alternate-reference alignment, recipient/donor identity, or conversion-tract field.

capabilities.step: Resolve hybrid copies, duplications, and copy order/origin
capabilities.evidence: No first-class ordered segment path, physical-copy identifier, copy number/order/orientation, junction linkage, hybrid class, or duplicated-copy origin exists in the current LRVariant/carrier contract.

capabilities.evidence: The checked locus returned one approximately 20.6 kb deletion and approximately 20.6, 41.2, and 61.8 kb insertion/duplication-like rows, but each had AN=4 and none encoded a resolved GBA1/GBAP1 path.

capabilities.evidence: Variant-level AN ranged from 3 to 584; 487/1,586 rows had AN below 584. GBA1 rows had AN 386–584 and GBA1LP rows 4–584. No structure-specific callable chromosome-haplotype or physical-copy denominator exists.

capabilities.evidence: The paper’s ORs come from a filtered, clinically ascertained case-control cohort; HGSVC/HPRC has different ascertainment and no matching PD phenotype contract.

capabilities.step: Export a reproducible copy-identity result
capabilities.evidence: Current variant-oriented export cannot preserve ordered copies, origin evidence, conversion intervals, linked junctions, structure-specific no-calls, matching level, or complete browser state.

acceptanceTest.fixture: Five chromosome haplotypes: canonical GBA1+GBAP1; a GBA1-anchored copy with the three RecNciI-like markers and a bounded GBAP1-like tract; a supported GBA1/GBAP1 hybrid junction; an extra tandem copy whose origin is partly unresolved; and a generic overlapping 20.6 kb event with AN=4 but no segment path. Include one no-call marker interval and one sample in which the three markers are split across copies.
acceptanceTest.actions: Normalize build/transcript notation; open the 100 kb locus; verify pinned gene models and Y1 provenance; select each sample strand; anchor unique flanks; order segments; compare against both paralogs; bound donor-like runs; classify exact versus overlap; inspect global/stratum callable counts; and export/reload the receipt.
acceptanceTest.expected: Five distinct outcomes are retained. The RecNciI-like label appears only when all three normalized markers are cis on one GBA1-assigned copy; the tract has marker-bounded uncertainty; hybrid and duplication preserve junction/order and unresolved origin; split markers do not form RecNciI-like; the sparse generic event remains unresolved; every class shows matched/callable/no-call counts, participants, release/run/query and identical exported values.
acceptanceTest.forbidden: The result must not diagnose PD or Gaucher disease, transfer OR 2.6 or severe-allele OR 11.4 to reference participants, infer conversion from three markers alone, infer a hybrid or duplicated-copy origin from generic overlap, equate variant AN with structure callability, treat 292 people as 584 fully callable copies without evidence, or use non-observation as pathogenic evidence.

evidence.claim: GBAP1 is stated to lie 16 kb downstream and share 96% coding-region homology; the assay targeted only GBA1, and RecNciI is defined by p.L483P, p.A495P, and p.V499V.
evidence.citation: PDF p. 1, Introduction

evidence.claim: In 72 matched samples, targeted PacBio and WGS with Gauchian found six Sanger-confirmed carriers, while generic DRAGEN/GATK missed the RecNciI carrier.
evidence.citation: PDF pp. 2–3, Fig. 2a

For each event, compare both flanks, canonical full inserted sequence, length, orientation, LINE-1 family/subfamily segments, poly(A) and TSD. A shared site without identical complete sequence is a same-site different insertion, not an exact match.

Report ALT AC and AN by cohort and stratum together with explicit callable-reference and no-call chromosome-copy counts. If the site has no event-specific callable denominator, classify the result as no-call or data-blocked rather than absent.
after: Export the match definition, event grouping, all constituent records, callable denominator, no-call count, release/run, source identity, URL state and unresolved fields.

startingState.stopRule: Stop exact-event comparison if the source build or both breakpoints are unknown. evidence.claim: The study examined nine highly selected unresolved Werner syndrome participants from eight pedigrees, each with one previously identified heterozygous causal WRN allele; eight people had genomic targeted long-read sequencing and one affected sibling was resolved through the sequenced sibling/family workup.
evidence.citation: PDF pp. 1-3, abstract, Methods, and Table 1

evidence.claim: ReadFish adaptive sampling on ONT GridION targeted approximately 3 Mb around WRN plus two controls, used R9.4.1 flow cells for 72 hours, aimed for and averaged about 20x, aligned reads to GRCh38 with minimap2, phased SNV/indel calls with Medaka, and called SVs with Sniffles, SVIM, and cuteSV.
evidence.citation: PDF pp. 2-4, Targeted long-read sequencing and Data analysis

evidence.claim: For PD1010, the paper reports a heterozygous 338,715 bp/about 339 kb deletion beginning within WRN and including exons 25-35; junction PCR and Sanger sequencing confirmed GRCh38 chr8:g.31135822_31474535delinsTCT.
evidence.citation: PDF p. 2 Table 1; p. 4 Fig. 1B caption; p. 5 Results

evidence.claim: Long-read computational phasing predicted PD1010's known c.561A>G allele and newly detected deletion were on different haplotypes. Junction PCR/Sanger confirmed the deletion but did not independently establish trans; direct parental segregation was reported only for the BIA family, not PD1010.
evidence.citation: PDF pp. 4-5 and Table 1; prior WRN slide report, How in trans was established

evidence.claim: PD1010's LCL western blot showed no detectable WRN protein, and the known c.561A>G allele had prior evidence for cryptic splicing. The paper did not report a deletion-specific RNA assay; sample-level protein loss reflects the combined genotype and is not a population-browser observable.
evidence.citation: PDF pp. 2 and 4-5; Table 1

evidence.claim: The paper warns that ONT R9.4.1 has a higher single-read error rate than PacBio HiFi, especially in homopolymers; intronic splice predictions need laboratory confirmation; and one biologically compelling case remained molecularly unresolved despite DNA and RNA long reads.
evidence.citation: PDF pp. 5-6, Discussion

evidence.claim: The authors state all eight detected variants likely could also have been identified by focused short-read WGS analysis of WRN. The 8/9 result arose from an extremely ascertained, small, partly related cohort and is not an unselected diagnostic yield.
evidence.citation: PDF pp. 1-2 and 6; prior WRN slide report, Limitations

paper.title: Identification of a novel non-coding deletion in Allan-Herndon-Dudley syndrome by long-read HiFi genome sequencing

archetypes: A7 — Deep intronic and regulatory variants
locus: SLC16A2 intron 1 · chrX:74,455,691–74,468,566 display; paper deletion chrX:74,460,691–74,463,566 (GRCh38/hg38)

persona.role: Rare-disease structural-variation researcher or laboratory scientist
persona.context: Research follow-up after an externally validated noncoding SLC16A2 deletion

nonDiagnosticBoundary: This workflow can establish whether the same sequence-resolved deletion is represented in callable population-reference X-chromosome copies and can display separately pinned regulatory annotations. Population occurrence or absence cannot validate expression consequence, pathogenicity, benignity, penetrance, or diagnosis.

startingState.trigger: An externally characterized GRCh38 SLC16A2 intron-1 deletion with Sanger-supported junction sequence.
inputs: Original assembly and coordinate convention: paper hg38 deleted-base interval chrX:74,460,691–74,463,566, 2,876 bp
Breakpoint junction trace: AGACGGAGTCTGGCTCTGTCG|CCCAGGCTGGAGTGCAGTGGCA, manually transcribed from paper Fig. 2A
Orthogonal validation method, primers, amplicon identities, inheritance evidence, and uncertainty
Independently versioned JASPAR, GTEx eQTL, RegulomeDB, conservation, and transcript-annotation evidence
Cohort/release/run, X-ploidy model, event-callability rule, and callable/no-call chromosome-copy counts
startingState.question: Is the same deletion junction represented in callable reference X-chromosome copies, and which independently pinned regulatory annotations does that exact deleted interval overlap?
startingState.stopRule: Stop before claiming recurrence if the build, deleted-base/VCF conversion, retained flanks, or junction sequence cannot be reconciled; stop before claiming absence if exact-event callability and X-ploidy denominators are unavailable. Unpinned regulatory evidence is unavailable, not negative.

before: Retain the paper's hg38 one-based inclusive deleted-base interval and 2,876 bp length; pin the GRCh38 chrX accession before deriving any VCF representation.
Transcribe and independently review the Sanger junction plus left/right retained flanks. Record AluY1/AluY2 context so microhomology-equivalent VCF shifts are normalized to one event.
Define exact recurrence as the same retained-flank-to-retained-flank junction and deleted sequence, not generic overlap, similar length, or a shared left anchor.
Freeze annotation snapshots separately: assembly, release/version/date, track, stable feature ID, coordinates, alleles where applicable, tissue, effect direction/size, and source URL/checksum.
inside: Open chrX:74,455,691–74,468,566 in the HGSVC/HPRC Y1 view and verify GRCh38, cohort, accepted primary source, database, release, chromosome scope, and run.

Search normalized deletion representations at both paper breakpoints and require a junction-sequence match across the Alu-mediated join. Inspect every ALT from the source event; do not promote an overlapping DEL or an interval-only match to exact recurrence.

For an exact match, report global and XX/XY-stratified AC/AN, callable chromosome copies, no-call copies, participants, and the ploidy rule. XX contributes at most two non-PAR X copies and XY at most one; observed VCF AN is not a substitute for event callability.
If no exact row is found, inspect spanning-read/junction and breakpoint-flank callability for every eligible copy. Base-depth coverage alone cannot certify a 2.876 kb deletion as callable.

Render JASPAR TF predictions, rs1263181 GTEx eQTL evidence, RegulomeDB score, and conservation in a separate evidence layer with their own provenance and prediction/association labels; do not join them causally to population occurrence.
after: Export the paper interval, junction/flanks, normalization rule, exact/overlap outcome, AC/AN, callable/no-call X copies, sex/ploidy strata, release/run/database, query receipt, and pinned annotation receipts.

Hand population recurrence and regulatory annotations to external functional, segregation, transcript, and clinical review. Preserve the paper's negative blood RT-PCR and absence of direct functional validation.

branches.condition: The same junction and deleted sequence are observed in one or more callable reference X-chromosome copies
branches.action: Report exact population-reference occurrence with AC/AN, callable/no-call copies, XX/XY strata, and provenance; keep regulatory consequence unvalidated.

paper.title: Amplification-free long-read sequencing of TCF4 expanded trinucleotide repeats in Fuchs Endothelial Corneal Dystrophy

locus: TCF4 CTG18.1 · paper GRCh37 AGG flank chr18:53,253,349–53,253,384 and CAG/AGC repeat chr18:53,253,385–53,253,459; corrected GRCh38 paper segment chr18:55,586,117–55,586,228; current source event chr18:55,586,116–55,586,201

persona.role: Repeat-expansion researcher or laboratory scientist
persona.context: Population-reference follow-up after an externally characterized TCF4 CTG18.1 allele, with explicit interest in expanded configurations that occurred in affected and unaffected paper contexts

nonDiagnosticBoundary: This workflow asks whether a comparable sequence-resolved or explicitly weaker length-only TCF4 state is represented in a population-reference release. It cannot determine FECD status, penetrance, protection, pathogenicity, benignity, or diagnosis, and it must not transfer the paper's 40-repeat study designation to the browser.

startingState.trigger: An external TCF4 CTG18.1 result with both allele lengths and, when available, sequence across the adjacent AGG and CAG/AGC tracts.
inputs: Original assay, laboratory, tissue, molecule/read support, caller, sizing range, and uncertainty
Both allele measurements; raw STR, Southern, and long-read values retained separately rather than collapsed to one count
Exact sequence or motif decomposition across the AGG flank and CAG/AGC tract, including interruptions and strand/orientation
Original build and coordinates, plus a reviewed mapping to the corrected GRCh38 paper segment chr18:55,586,117–55,586,228
A predeclared matching rule: exact represented sequence, AGG-plus-CAG structural match, CAG-length-only similarity, or interruption-marker-only comparison
Browser cohort/release/run, source event and ALT identity, global and stratum AC/AN, expected chromosome roster, and missing/no-call accounting
startingState.question: Does HGSVC/HPRC contain an exact represented sequence state, or only a weaker length/flank/interruption similarity, and is non-observation interpretable after representation and callability checks?
startingState.stopRule: Stop exact comparison if build, orientation, assay basis, second allele, or sequence coverage is missing. Stop an absence claim if the paper's full AGG-plus-CAG segment is not represented, the event allelic series is incomplete, or callable/no-call counts are unavailable.

before: Record both alleles, original coordinates and motif orientation, assay, blood or other tissue, read distribution, flank sequence, interruptions, and uncertainty without replacing one assay's result with another.

Retain the paper's GRCh37 AGG and CAG/AGC intervals, then use the corrected GRCh38 paper segment chr18:55,586,117–55,586,228. Treat source event chr18-55586116-TRV-85 as a locus/representation bridge, not proof that its 86 bp reference span equals the full paper segment.

Choose the matching rule before viewing population data. Exact sequence across the same represented interval is strongest; equal signed length or a repeat count alone is weaker; rs143743309 alone is an interruption-marker observation, not an expanded-allele match.
Keep the four paper context groups as controls rather than outcomes: RE+/FECD+, RE+/FECD-, RE-/FECD-, and RE-/FECD+. Population participants have no corresponding FECD labels.
inside: Open chr18:55,576,116–55,596,201 in HGSVC/HPRC and verify GRCh38, accepted Y1 chr18 source, cohort, run, and chromosome scope.
Select all 52 ALT rows sharing source_variant_id chr18-55586116-TRV-85; compare one source event rather than treating normalized ALTs as independent loci.

Compare exact ALT sequence only over a declared common span. Separately report signed ALT-minus-REF length and, only if a validated decomposition exists, AGG count, CAG/AGC count, order, purity, and interruptions.

Use the paper's unaffected-expanded configurations as negative controls: 17/82, 12/67, 19/84, 18/92, and 12/103 by STR, while preserving their PacBio estimates and distributions. Do not infer a protective configuration from their occurrence.

Check the Sanger-verified expanded-allele AGG-flank variants separately: sample 337 had 17 AGGs; sample 554 had 12 AGGs, one CAG, then a thirteenth AGG. Also keep rs143743309 G>C/CAC as a short-allele marker that the paper found in four samples and not specific to FECD status.

For every observed ALT or SNP report exact matching rule, AC/AN, ancestry/sex stratum where used, explicit missing/no-call count or unavailable status, allele/event ID, and provenance. Do not equate a row's AN with repeat-sequence completeness.
after: Return one bounded result: exact represented sequence observed; AGG-plus-CAG structural match observed; length-only similarity observed; marker-only observation; not observed in representation-complete callable data; or representation/callability blocked.

Export the source and corrected coordinates, common comparison span, exact ALT or marker ID, matching rule, AC/AN and missing/no-call counts, filters, release/run, query date, and all paper-versus-browser limitations.

Hand the population-reference observation to the research team for phenotype review, corneal-tissue considerations, orthogonal sizing/sequence validation, segregation, and interpretation outside the browser.

branches.condition: Only one size number, an unknown assay, or no second allele is available
branches.action: Request the original assay result and stop exact or biallelic comparison; do not reconstruct sequence from length.

branches.condition: The source event and external allele do not cover the same AGG-plus-CAG interval
branches.action: Report representation mismatch; a matching signed length is not an exact-sequence match.

branches.condition: An exact ALT sequence matches over a predeclared common represented span with explicit AC/AN and callability
branches.action: Report population-reference occurrence with allele/event identity and provenance only; FECD phenotype and protection remain unknown.

branches.condition: Only total length or approximate CAG count is similar while AGG flank, interruptions, or purity are unresolved
branches.action: Report length-only similarity and label structural equivalence data-blocked.

branches.condition: rs143743309 or another interruption marker is observed without proven linkage to the compared expanded ALT
branches.action: Report marker occurrence separately and stop any expanded-haplotype or modifier inference.

branches.condition: No match is returned but exact sequence coverage, event representation, roster, or no-call accounting is incomplete
branches.action: Report representation/callability blocked, never absent or zero.

branches.condition: No match is observed in representation-complete callable data
branches.action: Report not observed with exact denominator, missing/no-call count, release, and matching rule; this is not evidence of pathogenicity or penetrance.

story.given: an externally characterized TCF4 allele pair with assay-labelled sizes and sequence across the AGG flank and CAG/AGC tract, such as an expanded allele configured like one of the paper's elderly RE+/FECD- samples
story.when: the researcher opens the corrected GRCh38 window, selects every ALT from chr18-55586116-TRV-85, compares exact common-span sequence before length-only similarity, inspects flank/interruption markers separately, and checks AC/AN plus missing/no-call and run provenance
story.then: the browser distinguishes exact represented sequence, weaker structural or length similarity, marker-only occurrence, not observed in callable representation-complete data, and representation/callability blocked, supporting only whether a comparable reference state is represented—not FECD classification or threshold-based interpretation

capabilities.evidence: HGSVC/HPRC has no FECD phenotype or corneal-endothelium comparator. The paper's five RE+/FECD- samples are methodological negative controls for a simple interruption explanation, not labels transferable to population participants.

capabilities.evidence: Current source has variant CSV and shareable region state, but no single export joins external assay/tissue, corrected and original coordinates, common sequence span, exact ALT, flank/interruption decomposition, event-level callability, and accepted-run receipt.

capabilities.step: Apply the paper's 40-repeat designation or infer penetrance/protection
capabilities.evidence: The study used a clinically defined RE threshold in 18 selected blood samples, observed elderly unaffected expansion carriers, could not assay corneal endothelium, and explicitly retained small-sample and tissue limitations. No threshold or phenotype inference transfers to HGSVC/HPRC.

acceptanceTest.fixture: One TCF4 source event with (a) an exact common-span match to an externally sequenced AGG-plus-CAG allele, (b) a same-length allele with a different AGG flank, (c) rs143743309 on an unlinked short allele, (d) one no-call chromosome copy, and (e) an external length-only result; include no FECD phenotype fields.
acceptanceTest.actions: Open the corrected region; verify accepted chr18 provenance; select all event ALTs; declare the common comparison span and matching rule; compare exact sequence before signed length; inspect flank and marker separately; check global/stratum AC/AN and no-call; export and reload the receipt.
acceptanceTest.expected: One grouped event; exact, same-length-different-structure, marker-only, no-call, and length-only states remain distinct; every observation has allele/event ID, matching rule, AC/AN, missing/no-call, release/run, and coordinate receipt; the external and exported values reproduce; non-observation fails closed when the full paper span is not represented.
acceptanceTest.forbidden: The result must not diagnose FECD, label an allele pathogenic, benign, protective, or penetrant, apply a 40-repeat threshold, treat an unaffected paper carrier as a population label, infer expanded-allele linkage from rs143743309 alone, equate signed event length with exact CAG count, or convert incomplete representation/callability into absence.

evidence.claim: The paper studied 18 blood-derived DNA samples in four groups: nine RE+/FECD+, five RE+/FECD-, two RE-/FECD-, and two RE-/FECD+; average on-target coverage was 582X, range 40X–2095X.
evidence.citation: PDF pp. 2, 5–7; Table 1

evidence.claim: The five elderly RE+/FECD- samples had STR allele pairs 17/82, 12/67, 19/84, 18/92, and 12/103; PacBio estimates for their expanded alleles were 83, 68, 85, 122, and 100–300 repeats respectively.
evidence.citation: PDF p. 7, Table 1

evidence.claim: No reproducible CAG interruption was found across all expanded reads from the five RE+/FECD- samples. Sample 337 instead had 17 AGGs on the expanded allele, and sample 554 had 12 AGGs followed by one CAG and a thirteenth AGG; both flank structures were Sanger confirmed.
evidence.citation: PDF pp. 9–12; Fig. 5

evidence.claim: The rs143743309 G>C change creates CAC in place of CAG and occurred in samples 001, 018, 180, and 663, always on an allele below 20 repeats in this sample set; it was not limited to either FECD+ or FECD- samples.
evidence.citation: PDF pp. 7–8; Fig. 3 and S2 Fig.

evidence.claim: STR and No-Amp estimates generally agreed within one triplet for smaller alleles, while alleles above roughly 85 repeats showed larger discrepancies, heterogeneity, and occasional automated-calling failure. Samples 4938, 4823, and 37 showed broad expanded distributions; Southern blot detected products up to about 8 kb in the latter two.
evidence.citation: PDF pp. 6–10; Table 1; Figs. 4–5

evidence.claim: The assay used amplification-free CRISPR-Cas9/SMRT enrichment on leukocyte DNA with 15 bp anchors allowing two mismatches and an indel-correction step. The authors could not assay corneal endothelium, did not systematically investigate coverage variability, had only five unaffected expansion carriers, and could not exclude interruptions in a subset of reads or individuals.
The paper coordinates are GRCh37: AGG flank chr18:53,253,349–53,253,384 and CAG/AGC tract chr18:53,253,385–53,253,459, with upstream and downstream 15 bp anchor sequences explicitly reported.
evidence.citation: PDF p. 4

evidence.claim: A faithful population-reference replay must preserve affected and unaffected paper configurations as comparison branches while withholding phenotype labels from HGSVC/HPRC; it must distinguish exact common-span sequence, flank structure, length-only similarity, and marker-only occurrence.
evidence.citation: Analyst reconstruction from PDF pp. 5–12; requires workflow and safety review

evidence.claim: The corrected paper segment and current source event are overlapping but not coordinate-identical representations; therefore the source event is a bridge to inspect, not proof of full AGG-plus-CAG equivalence.
evidence.citation: Analyst comparison of prior reviewed lift, manifest correction, paper p. 4, and live API; requires event/coordinate review

paper.title: Assessing the efficacy of target adaptive sampling long-read sequencing through hereditary cancer patient genomes

locus: EPM2AIP1/MLH1 promoter · paper Fig. 7 GRCh38 viewport chr3:36,991,000–36,995,350; TAS target chr3:36,983,349–37,060,846. The MLH1 workflow is A2; A4 describes separate APC SVA results in the same paper.

persona.role: Hereditary-cancer epigenetics researcher or molecular laboratory scientist
persona.context: Research follow-up after an external MLH1 promoter methylation result or an unresolved Lynch-syndrome workup

nonDiagnosticBoundary: This workflow can ask whether a comparable, provenance-matched methylation profile is represented on a reference chromosome copy and whether sequence and methylation evidence are genuinely linked. It cannot diagnose Lynch syndrome, establish an MLH1 epimutation, infer gene silencing, classify a sequence variant, or transfer tumor immunohistochemistry to HGSVC/HPRC participants.

startingState.trigger: An external MLH1 promoter methylation observation, ideally with per-read or chromosome-copy assignment, plus a question about comparable population-reference states.
inputs: Original reference build, interval, coordinate convention, assay, tissue, extraction, sequencing kit/flow cell, methylation caller/version, batch, and coverage
CpG-level methylated/unmethylated counts or likelihoods, exact tested interval/DMR if defined, and control-panel definition
Linkage class declared as sample-total, source-haplotype only, phase-linked chromosome copy, or same-read/same-molecule
For any claimed sequence association: exact SNV/indel/SV identity, phase set or molecule/read identifiers, and linkage evidence
Release/run, complete 292-person roster status, source-present/no-output/skip counts, and the hash-bound orientation receipt
startingState.question: Does a comparable MLH1 promoter methylation state occur on a callable reference chromosome copy, and is it linked to the same sequence state at the claimed evidence level rather than inferred from sample-total methylation?
startingState.stopRule: Stop allele-specific or same-copy interpretation if the methylation is sample-total, the copy mapping receipt is absent/stale, tissue/caller provenance is absent, or the claimed sequence state lacks phase or molecule linkage. The paper gives no exact DMR boundary and no MLH1 sequence variant, so neither may be invented.

before: Preserve the external result and its uncertainty. Record build, coordinate convention, assay, blood-versus-tumor tissue, native-DNA status, caller/version, CpG coverage, controls, DMR rule, and whether unassigned reads were retained.

Use GRCh38 and retain the paper's exact Fig. 7 viewport chr3:36991000–36995350. Do not use the index's approximate chr3:36987600–37056596 CTA: it is not the paper viewport and trims the paper's supplementary TAS target chr3:36983349–37060846.

Represent the paper finding accurately: S33 had an EPM2AIP1/MLH1 promoter-region allele-specific pattern, but the paper supplied no exact DMR endpoints and no linked MLH1 SNV, indel, or SV. Predeclare methylation-only unless independent sequence-linkage evidence is supplied.

Classify linkage strength before viewing reference data: sample-total < source-labelled HAP1/HAP2 < hash-receipted VCF-copy mapping < phase-set-linked < same-read/same-molecule. Never silently promote one level to another.
inside: Open chr3:36991000–36995350 with HGSVC/HPRC haplotypes and verify GRCh38, accepted chr3 primary run, methylation source run, full roster status, and orientation-receipt hash.
Show sample-total methylation in a separate lane or state. It may support a sample-level comparison but must not be duplicated into copy A and copy B or described as allele-specific.

Enable per-copy methylation only when the joined capability returns AVAILABLE_CONFIRMED for the exact chromosome, primary run, source run, roster, and expected orientation-receipt hash. Label A/B as chromosome copies, never maternal/paternal, and retain source HAP1/HAP2 plus VCF strand.

Preserve CpG position, methylation, coverage, source-row key, unassigned/no-output states, and linkage scope. A null phase_set and chromosome-wide operator assumption permit only receipt-qualified same-copy wording; they do not establish same-molecule linkage.

Inspect candidate sequence variants on the same VCF strand only after checking their own phase status and denominator. If the sequence and methylation records lack a shared phase set or molecule/read identifier, report co-display on a mapped chromosome copy, not molecular co-occurrence.

Compare profiles only after matching tissue, assay/caller, target interval, CpG callability, and control definition. The paper's ten-control thresholds are study-specific and cannot be applied to the current HGSVC/HPRC source without the same controls and provenance.
after: Return one bounded outcome: sample-total only; receipt-qualified same-copy profile; same-molecule linked state; not observed in callable provenance-matched data; or data/provenance blocked.

evidence.claim: The study applied target adaptive sampling long-read sequencing to 33 clinically suspected hereditary-cancer patients, including two with Lynch syndrome, targeting 147 cancer-predisposition genes.
evidence.citation: Local PDF pp. 1–3, Table 1 and Fig. 1

evidence.claim: The target used GENCODE Basic release 38 maximal transcript spans plus 10 kb margins; Supplementary Data 1 gives the exact MLH1 target as chr3:36,983,349–37,060,846, and alignment was to GRCh38.
evidence.citation: Local PDF p. 2 and p. 9; Supplementary Data 1 (MOESM3), MLH1 row

evidence.claim: Figure 7's exact displayed interval is chr3:36,991,000–36,995,350. It shows increased promoter-region methylation on S33 haplotype 2 across EPM2AIP1/MLH1, but neither the figure nor supplementary gene-level result defines exact DMR endpoints.
evidence.citation: Local PDF p. 8, Fig. 7a; high-resolution figure label

evidence.claim: Supplementary Data 5 reports S33 EPM2AIP1/MLH1 with 98 abnormal CpGs, 135 normal CpGs, abnormal ratio 0.42060086, and average -log10(p) 5.68454565.
evidence.citation: Supplementary Data 5 (MOESM7), S33 row

evidence.claim: S33 had tumor microsatellite instability and no germline mutation detected by prior multigene panel testing; the paper reports one MLH1 promoter allele as hypermethylated and separate tumor IHC loss of MLH1/PMS2, but names no linked MLH1 SNV, indel, or SV.
evidence.citation: Local PDF p. 8, Fig. 7 and Results; Table 1, p. 3

evidence.claim: Each native-DNA read was haplotagged with WhatsHap 1.4 from a GLIMPSE-phased common-SNP VCF; f5c 1.2 called per-read CpG methylation, outputs were split into haplotype 1, haplotype 2, and unclassified, and meth-freq computed per-CpG frequencies.
evidence.citation: Local PDF pp. 9–10, Methods; Fig. 1

evidence.claim: The study-specific detector used ten controls: CpGs at 0–0.2 in all controls were normally unmethylated and 0.8–1 normally methylated; target shifts required Fisher p≤0.05, and a gene was flagged if average -log10(p)≥4.5 or at least ten abnormal CpGs occurred within 2 kb upstream of its TSS.
evidence.citation: Local PDF p. 10, Allele-specific methylation analysis

evidence.claim: DNA was blood-derived after plasma isolation; libraries used SQK-LSK110/114, mostly R9.4.1 (29) and R10.4 (4), 72-hour adaptive sampling, Guppy 6.0.7, minimap2 2.22, and GRCh38. Median on-target depth was 21.9 and two samples below 10× compromised variant detection.
evidence.citation: Local PDF pp. 2 and 9, sequencing statistics and Methods

evidence.claim: The paper cautions that ONT indel calls were discordant with short reads, low depth reduced SNV recall, population-LD phasing has difficulty with rare variants, and somatic detection is limited by tumor impurity, subclones, and low allele fractions.
evidence.citation: Local PDF pp. 3 and 8–9, Results/Discussion

evidence.claim: The exact paper-supported browser CTA is the Fig. 7 viewport, not the approximate index window; the exact DMR and MLH1 sequence allele must remain unavailable unless separately supplied.
evidence.citation: Analyst reconstruction from Fig. 7, Supplementary Data 1/5, and GRCh38 validation

evidence.claim: Sample-total, receipt-qualified same-copy, phase-linked, and same-molecule evidence are different evidentiary states. Only the last directly joins sequence and methylation on one molecule.
evidence.citation: Analyst reconstruction for workflow and data-semantics review

evidence.claim: A faithful population-reference replay asks whether a provenance-matched state is represented and fails closed on missing linkage; it does not reenact the paper's clinical epimutation inference.
evidence.citation: Analyst reconstruction; requires paper, safety, and product review
