paper.title: Detecting PKD1 variants in polycystic kidney disease patients by single-molecule long-read sequencing

locus: PKD1 plus PKD1P1–PKD1P6 · PKD1 chr16:2,088,708–2,135,898; six remote pseudogenes chr16:14,911,551–18,401,940 (GRCh38 pinned browser gene models)

persona.role: Kidney-genetics researcher or molecular laboratory scientist
persona.context: Research review of a sequence difference in the duplicated PKD1 portion where one of six pseudogenes could be the true source

nonDiagnosticBoundary: This population-reference workflow can ask whether a sequence difference is origin-resolved to PKD1 or a named pseudogene, locally phased, and represented among callable reference chromosome copies. It cannot diagnose ADPKD, classify an allele, establish gene conversion, or convert the paper’s deliberately selected known-positive recovery fractions into diagnostic sensitivity, specificity, or yield.

startingState.trigger: An externally detected PKD1-region SNV, indel, local haplotype, or possible donor-like tract whose origin may be confounded by PKD1P1–PKD1P6.
inputs: Original genomic and transcript notation, GRCh37.p13 or other source build, reference/alternate sequence, strand, normalization method, and a retained build-conversion receipt

Assay identity and blind spots: targeted PCR or genome-wide, primer and unique-flank specificity, coverage, read/contig support, amplification cycles, allele dropout, chimera handling, and indel/homopolymer error model
Pinned GRCh38 references and gene models for PKD1 and PKD1P1–PKD1P6 plus a versioned homologous-block/exon-equivalence map
Per-locus sequence or assembly evidence spanning the candidate and enough unique or paralog-diagnostic context to assign origin
Local phase-set bounds and evidence; a chromosome-wide assembly/phasing receipt if cis is asserted across separate phase blocks or remote loci
Predeclared match level: exact sequence and origin; same local sequence with unresolved origin; homologous-position overlap; or unresolved
startingState.question: Does the evidence assign the sequence difference to PKD1 rather than a named pseudogene, what is the bounded local phase relationship, and is the same origin-resolved state represented among explicitly callable reference copies?
startingState.stopRule: If build normalization, homologous-coordinate mapping, unique/paralog-diagnostic anchors, local phase bounds, or origin-specific callability is missing, stop at unresolved or data-blocked; never infer PKD1 origin from linear overlap, one best alignment, VCF strand, or a population row alone.

before: Preserve the original GRCh37.p13 or source-build result and transcript notation. Normalize sequence and coordinates to GRCh38 with a receipt; do not treat a point liftover as complete indel normalization.
Pin all seven current GRCh38 gene models and a homologous-block map. Keep annotation liftover separate from current gene annotation because PKD1P4 and PKD1P5 model boundaries changed between builds.

Construct one evidence object per physical locus from unique flanks through the queried homologous block. Record coverage, read/assembly anchors, paralog-diagnostic markers, conflicts, unresolved bases, and assay artifacts.
Record each local phase block with start, stop, phase-set identifier, method, and confidence. Do not bridge the paper’s five separate PKD1 amplicons or browser phase blocks without spanning evidence.
Predeclare origin outcomes: PKD1-assigned, PKD1P1–PKD1P6-assigned, same-sequence/origin-unresolved, candidate donor-like tract, representation mismatch, or uncallable.
inside: Open the validated primary envelope chr16:2083989–2140617 and confirm GRCh38, HGSVC/HPRC, accepted chr16 run, PKD1 gene model, and query receipt.

Open synchronized paralog panes for PKD1P3, PKD1P6, PKD1P1/PKD1P2, and PKD1P4/PKD1P5. Align panes by versioned homologous/exon-equivalent coordinates and transcriptional orientation, not by genomic x-coordinate.

Compare the complete candidate sequence and local context simultaneously against PKD1 and all relevant pseudogene references. Require unique-flank or diagnostic-marker support on the same read/contig before assigning one source locus.
Assign a named origin only when locus anchors, diagnostic markers, mapping alternatives, and local coverage agree. Preserve conflicting, equally supported, or uncovered cases as origin-unresolved.

Call a donor-like or conversion-like candidate only when one PKD1-anchored molecule or assembly path changes to a contiguous pseudogene-like diagnostic-marker run and returns to PKD1 markers, with marker-bounded uncertainty. Do not infer a tract from a shared variant or one best alignment; the paper did not demonstrate gene conversion.

Phase variants only within the declared local phase block. Multiple differences may be called cis within one supported block; differences in separate amplicons, phase sets, or remote pseudogene panes remain unlinked unless a spanning assembly or validated chromosome-wide phasing receipt bridges them.

For population occurrence, count an exact PKD1-origin sequence state only among chromosome copies callable for the queried block and origin assignment. Report separate per-pseudogene denominators; retain uncallable and origin-unresolved copies rather than pooling seven loci or using variant AN as an origin denominator.
after: Return one bounded result: exact PKD1-origin state represented; named-pseudogene state represented; local-sequence match with unresolved origin; not observed among representation-complete origin-callable copies; or data/representation blocked.

Export original and normalized notation, all seven reference/model versions, homologous-coordinate map, locus anchors, diagnostic markers, local phase boundaries, exact matching rule, per-locus callable/matched/unresolved/no-call counts, strata, release/run, and query state.

Use locus-specific orthogonal sequencing, assembly/read review, breakpoint testing, segregation, phenotype review, and expert interpretation outside the population browser. Keep the paper’s 20/21 variants and 18/19 people as selected known-positive recovery counts only.

branches.condition: A PKD1-anchored sequence has concordant unique-flank and paralog-diagnostic support
branches.action: Report PKD1-assigned local sequence with its phase-block bounds, confidence, callable-copy AC/AN, unresolved/no-call counts, and provenance.

branches.condition: The same difference is supported on one named pseudogene-anchored sequence
branches.action: Report the named pseudogene origin and its own callable denominator; do not transfer it to PKD1.

branches.condition: Sequence matches but origin anchors are missing, conflicting, or equally supported
branches.action: Report same-sequence/origin-unresolved and stop before PKD1 assignment, recurrence frequency, or clinical interpretation.

branches.condition: A PKD1-anchored path contains a bounded contiguous pseudogene-like marker run
branches.action: Report a candidate donor-like tract with nearest-marker bounds, conflicts, coverage, and uncertainty; require orthogonal review and do not claim gene conversion as established.

branches.condition: Variants lie in different paper amplicons, phase sets, or unbridged local blocks
branches.action: Display them separately and stop before a cis, trans, whole-gene, or chromosome-wide haplotype claim.

branches.condition: No matching state is returned but any relevant locus, origin assignment, or representation is uncallable
branches.action: Report data-blocked rather than zero, absent, unique to the case, or pathogenic.

branches.condition: No matching state is observed in representation-complete origin-callable copies
branches.action: Report a bounded reference non-observation with exact callable and no-call counts; do not infer pathogenicity or diagnosis.

story.then: the browser returns PKD1-assigned, named-pseudogene-assigned, origin-unresolved, candidate donor-like tract, bounded non-observation, or data-blocked with local phase boundaries, exact/callable/unresolved/no-call counts, and release/run/query provenance, supporting only a population-reference origin and occurrence statement

acceptanceTest.fixture: Seven pinned GRCh38 locus references plus six chromosome-copy cases: a uniquely PKD1-anchored exact allele; the same base difference uniquely anchored to PKD1P3; a sequence shared by PKD1 and PKD1P2 with missing diagnostic anchors; a PKD1-anchored bounded pseudogene-like marker tract; two PKD1 variants in separate unbridged local phase blocks; and a non-observation case with one relevant pseudogene block uncallable. Include exact callable, unresolved, and no-call counts by locus and one generic overlapping VCF event.
acceptanceTest.actions: Normalize the source result; verify all model and homologous-map versions; open and synchronize primary/paralog panes by homologous orientation; compare complete sequence plus same-molecule anchors; inspect local phase bounds; apply exact-versus-overlap matching; inspect per-locus callable denominators; export and reload the receipt.
acceptanceTest.expected: The fixtures remain distinct: PKD1, PKD1P3, origin-unresolved, candidate donor-like tract, phase-unlinked, and data-blocked. A named origin requires same-read/contig anchor support; the tract retains nearest-marker bounds; no cis claim crosses an unbridged block; the generic event remains candidate overlap; each result shows matched/callable/unresolved/no-call counts and identical provenance after reload.
acceptanceTest.forbidden: The result must not diagnose ADPKD, label an allele benign or pathogenic, report 18/19 or 20/21 as prospective diagnostic performance, infer PKD1 origin or gene conversion from overlap/one-best-alignment alone, join separate amplicons or phase sets into a whole-gene haplotype, treat 292 people or 584 strands as fully origin-callable, or convert missing pseudogene/phase/callability data into absence.

evidence.claim: PKD1 screening is difficult because most of its sequence is homologous to six pseudogenes, with high GC content; the duplicated portion is exons 1–32 and exons 33–46 are nonduplicated in the diagnostic workflow.
evidence.citation: PDF pp. 1–2 (article pp. 870–871) and p. 4 (article p. 873)

evidence.claim: The cohort contained 19 deliberately selected, already genotyped ADPKD patients, each with at least one pathogenic mutation previously detected by Sanger or MLPA; peripheral-blood DNA was used.
evidence.citation: PDF p. 2 (article p. 871), Methods 2.1

evidence.claim: Five greater-than-4 kb PKD1 LR-PCR fragments covered coding exons and boundaries but intentionally excluded most of intron 1; products were 4.3–8.1 kb, amplified for 35 cycles plus five barcode cycles, and sequenced on five PacBio RSII SMRT cells with P6 chemistry and 360-minute movies.
evidence.citation: PDF p. 2 (article p. 871), Methods 2.2.1–2.2.2

evidence.claim: Reads were aligned to GRCh37.p13 with MAPQ at least 30; Quiver confidence below 40 was filtered, while a separate reference-free Long Amplicon Analysis reconstructed each amplicon from reads over 3 kb and removed 0.85% chimeric subreads.
evidence.citation: PDF pp. 3–4 (article pp. 872–873), Methods 2.2.3–2.2.4

evidence.claim: The experiment identified 5.6% residual off-target pseudogene reads and discriminated them by unique alignment; Figure 2A names PKD1P1, PKD1P5, and PKD1P6 as examples but does not provide all six pseudogene coordinates.
evidence.citation: PDF pp. 5 and 7 (article pp. 874 and 876), Fig. 2A and Discussion

evidence.claim: Consecutive amplicons with loss of heterozygosity were only an indirect deletion signal. Two MLPA-supported deletions were detected, but exact breakpoints could not be determined with either method.
evidence.citation: PDF pp. 3 and 6 (article pp. 872 and 875), Methods 2.2.5 and Results 4.3

evidence.claim: The descriptive known-positive recovery was 20/21 pathogenic PKD1 variants and 18/19 participants. The missed c.6223_6224insTT had 43.3% supporting fraction and depth 1,203; Table 1 assigns patient 15 while the Figure 3 caption says patient 16.
evidence.citation: PDF pp. 6–8 (article pp. 875–877), Results 4.4, Fig. 3, Table 1

evidence.claim: PacBio noise and homopolymer-associated artifacts were major limitations; the targeted PCR design retained amplification bias, and the limited sample size required larger future cohorts before diagnostic power could be established.
evidence.citation: PDF pp. 7 and 9 (article pp. 876 and 878), Discussion

evidence.claim: A faithful population-browser replay requires synchronized primary/paralog views aligned by homologous coordinates and same-read/contig origin anchors; seven unrelated linear windows cannot establish source locus.
evidence.citation: Analyst reconstruction for workflow and product review; not performed by Borràs et al.

evidence.claim: Phase must remain local to one supported amplicon or phase block unless a spanning assembly or validated chromosome-wide receipt bridges blocks; the paper’s five amplicons do not demonstrate one continuous PKD1 haplotype.
evidence.citation: Analyst reconstruction from the paper’s separate 4.3–8.1 kb amplicons and current phase semantics

evidence.claim: The safe frequency unit is one origin-callable chromosome copy for a queried homologous block, with separate per-pseudogene counts and explicit unresolved/no-call states; variant AN and participant count are not substitutes.
evidence.citation: Analyst reconstruction for data-semantics review

Ensembl assembly mapping exactly reproduces current spans for P1, P2, P3, and P6, differs by two bases at the PKD1 start, and maps broader historical P4/P5 spans than current gene models, so annotation version and assembly mapping must remain separate receipts.

paper.title: Optical genome mapping identifies a germline retrotransposon insertion in SMARCB1 in two siblings with atypical teratoid rhabdoid tumors

locus: SMARCB1 intron 2 SVA-E · paper GRCh37 chr22:24,134,114; independently remapped candidate GRCh38 junction chr22:23,791,927/23,791,928; locus-overview CTA remains remap-receipt gated

persona.role: Mobile-element/structural-variation researcher or molecular genetics laboratory scientist
persona.context: Research follow-up of an externally resolved intronic mobile-element insertion, asking whether the same structure or only ordinary nearby variation is represented in a population reference

nonDiagnosticBoundary: The browser cannot diagnose ATRT, classify pathogenicity or benignity, transfer maternal segregation or tumor evidence to a reference participant, call a nearby SNV/indel or generic insertion the paper event, infer mosaicism from low cohort AC/AF, or turn depth coverage alone into an event-level absence claim. Population-reference evidence only; not diagnostic and not a pathogenicity or benignity classification.

startingState.trigger: An external assay has suggested an insertion near SMARCB1 intron 2 and the researcher needs population-reference occurrence, structure, genotype, and callability without transferring the paper family's phenotype or mosaic status.
inputs: Paper coordinate hg19/GRCh37 chr22:24,134,114 in SMARCB1 intron 2
Paper insertion length 2,763 nt and family SVA-E
Paper structural template: CCCT repeat, Alu-like repeat, GC-rich VNTR, SINE region, poly(A) tail, L1-like endonuclease site, and 10 bp target-site duplication
An independently checked hg19-to-hg38 point-remap receipt
External breakpoint/insert sequence or hash when sequence-identical matching is requested
A predeclared distinction between ordinary germline carrier status and quantitatively supported mosaicism
Known unknown: The paper does not publish the full 2,763 nt insert sequence, a sequence hash, exact domain boundaries, or an exact poly(A)-tail length
Known unknown: Whether a population record at the site would retain complete inserted sequence rather than symbolic or truncated ALT representation
Known unknown: Whether any source genotype has validated low-allele-fraction sensitivity for mosaicism
Known unknown: Whether site coverage can be converted into event-detection callability for a 2.763 kb SVA-E insertion
startingState.question: Is the same exact or structure-comparable SMARCB1 SVA-E insertion represented in callable HGSVC/HPRC chromosome copies, as distinct from a same-site different insertion or ordinary nearby carrier overlap; and does any putative carrier have enough quantitative evidence to support mosaicism rather than ordinary germline carrier status? Allowed outcomes: Return one of: sequence-identical SVA-E; structure-comparable SVA-E with unresolved nucleotide identity; same-site different insertion; nearby/ordinary overlap only; not observed in representation-complete callable copies; or data-blocked. Separately return mosaic-supported or mosaicism unsupported, with the latter required when quantitative evidence is absent.
startingState.stopRule: Stop when any required item is missing: Original reference build and coordinate convention; A validated build-remap receipt before enabling the browser CTA; Both breakpoint/TSD identity and inserted-sequence evidence for a sequence-identical claim; Event-level callability before reporting not observed; Quantitative sample-level source evidence plus a validated assay/decision rule before labeling mosaicism.

before: Record the paper build, insertion coordinate, interbase convention, length, SVA-E classification, ordered domains, TPRT features, breakpoint assays, and the qualitative-only boundary on maternal mosaicism. Required evidence: hg19/NC_000022.10 coordinate; 2,763 nt insertion length; SVA-E and ordered domain template; 10 bp TSD and both breakpoint validations; Paper family evidence with no numerical mosaic fraction. UI/API boundary: Keep paper facts separate from analyst matching rules and browser observations; do not serialize the case as merely an intronic insertion. Expected: A structure-complete literature template with explicit unknown full sequence and explicit qualitative maternal-mosaic evidence.

Remap the paper point to GRCh38, verify plus-strand one-to-one mapping and independent flanking-reference identity, then approve the existing 61,294 bp region as a verified display window before rendering a browser CTA. Required evidence: hg19ToHg38 chain identity; NC_000022.10 and NC_000022.11 context sequences; Coordinate and interbase conventions; Region-span check against the 100 kb Y1 limit. UI/API boundary: Do not enable a region CTA while the index status is approximate. After receipt validation, use chr22:23781823-23843117 and overlay the exact mapped point at 23,791,927. Expected: A verified GRCh38 display window containing the remapped insertion point, with a retained remap hash and junction caveat.
inside: Query the verified window and classify candidates using a tiered rule: nucleotide-identical; structure-comparable SVA-E; same-site different insertion; or ordinary nearby overlap. Required evidence: Canonical insertion anchor and both breakpoint/TSD sequences; Full insert sequence or sequence hash; SVA subfamily and orientation; Ordered domain annotations and poly(A) evidence; Source variant identity and representation provenance. UI/API boundary: Never elevate a nearby SNV/indel, generic INS, or insertion-family group to paper-event equivalence. Show which exact-structure fields matched and which were unavailable. Expected: One candidate class plus a field-by-field match ledger, or data-blocked when source representation cannot carry the needed structure.

For each exact/structure-comparable carrier, display GT and quantitative support fields when available, then evaluate mosaicism only under a predeclared source-specific assay rule. Required evidence: GT and ploidy; DP/GQ and ref/alt AD or equivalent molecule counts; Caller support and no-call reason; Validated mosaic sensitivity and decision threshold; Tissue/source provenance. UI/API boundary: Default a standard germline alternate genotype to carrier. If quantitative support or validated mosaic calibration is missing, show mosaicism unsupported—not non-mosaic and not mosaic. Expected: Separate fields for carrier status and mosaic-evidence status, with quantitative support and provenance or an explicit unsupported reason.

Intersect chromosome copies for which the source/caller can detect and fully represent a 2.763 kb SVA-E at this site; report exact/structure AC, event AN, no-calls, representation failures, and ordinary-overlap counts. Required evidence: Event-class sensitivity and size range; Per-copy site and insertion callability; No-call/reason fields; Complete ALT/subfamily/TSD representation; Accepted run and sample roster. UI/API boundary: Display base coverage separately. Do not use 100% over-10x base coverage or AN from a nearby SNV as the SVA event denominator. Expected: Event-level AC/AN and missingness only when representation is complete; otherwise data-blocked.
after: Export paper/remapped coordinates, structure template, candidate match ledger, carrier and mosaic-evidence status, event AC/AN/missingness, source/run identity, filters, and immutable query receipt for external MEI review. Required evidence: P/I/B evidence classes; Remap and sequence-context receipt; Exact-versus-overlap classification; Quantitative genotype or unsupported reason; Event-level denominator or data-blocked reason. UI/API boundary: A reloaded export must reproduce the verified region and all result classes without relying on a screenshot. Expected: A bounded population-reference handoff that cannot be mistaken for diagnosis, family segregation, or a mosaicism determination without quantitative evidence.

Comparison contract — Paper hg19 SMARCB1 intron-2 2,763 nt SVA-E structural template versus One GRCh38 HGSVC/HPRC chromosome-copy insertion event: Sequence-identical requires mapped interbase junction, both breakpoint/TSD sequences, orientation, and complete inserted sequence/hash. Structure-comparable requires same site, 2,763 nt-compatible length, SVA-E, ordered CCCT/Alu-like/VNTR/SINE/poly(A) architecture, TPRT target-site features, and 10 bp TSD, while explicitly flagging unavailable nucleotide identity. Same-site structural disagreement is different insertion; any nearby SNV/indel/generic overlap is ordinary overlap only. Unit: one fully represented mobile-element insertion on one callable chromosome copy.

Comparison contract — Paper mother's qualitative low-level WGS/PCR evidence versus One population-reference sample genotype: Carrier status derives from a valid alternate genotype. Mosaic-supported additionally requires quantitative ref/alt support, depth, tissue, validated mosaic sensitivity, a predeclared source-specific threshold, and uncertainty. Low cohort AC/AF or an unquantified GT never establishes mosaicism. Unit: one sample-assay observation, separate from event AC/AN.

Threshold boundary — No numerical maternal mosaic fraction. Source/scope: Paper PDF pp. 3 and 7; main text reports only lower maternal amplification in a dilution series / Paper-family evidence. Do not generalize: Do not invent a maternal VAF or use the family's qualitative result as a population-source mosaic threshold.

Threshold boundary — No arbitrary breakpoint-distance tolerance. Source/scope: Analyst rule grounded in the paper's exact hg19 point and breakpoint/TSD validation / This dossier's exact-site comparison. Do not generalize: The 61,294 bp display window and plus/minus 1 kb audit are navigation/search bounds, not biological equivalence tolerances.

Threshold boundary — If and only if exact-event AC=0 and representation-complete event AN is established, report a named binomial method or approximate rule-of-three bound; 3/584 is approximately 0.00514. Source/scope: Statistical reporting convention / Conditional population-reference absence statement. Do not generalize: Current checks do not establish SVA-event AN=584; base coverage and nearby-SNV AN do not satisfy the condition.

Failure recovery — The approximate index window is linked before the exact build/site is verified. Detect: No hg19-to-hg38 receipt or sequence-context hash accompanies the CTA. Recover: Verify the one-to-one remap and independent context, then mark the region verified; otherwise suppress the CTA.

Failure recovery — A nearby ordinary carrier or generic INS is described as the SVA-E. Detect: The result lacks matching junction/TSD, subfamily, orientation, and insert sequence/structure fields. Recover: Downgrade to ordinary overlap or same-site different insertion and enumerate missing exact-structure fields.

Failure recovery — A low AC/AF or GT=0/1 is labeled mosaic. Detect: No sample-level DP/AD or molecule counts, tissue, calibrated assay, threshold, and uncertainty are present. Recover: Retain carrier status and label mosaicism unsupported.

Failure recovery — Strong base coverage is treated as proof that a 2.763 kb SVA-E is absent. Detect: AN derives from base depth or another nearby record rather than insertion-event callability. Recover: Require event-class sensitivity, complete representation, and per-copy callability or return data-blocked.

Denominator contract — unit: One HGSVC/HPRC chromosome copy for which a 2.763 kb SVA-E at the mapped SMARCB1 junction is detectable and fully representable. Callable only when: A chromosome copy is callable only if the accepted source/caller can detect an insertion of this class/size at the site, preserve both breakpoints and relevant insert structure, and distinguish reference, exact/structure-comparable, different insertion, and no-call states. Base depth, ordinary SNV callability, or a generic GT at another record is insufficient. Required counts: Participants queried and maximum possible autosomal copies; Sequence-identical AC; Structure-comparable-only AC; Same-site different-insertion count; Ordinary nearby-overlap carrier count; Event-level AN; No-call and representation-incomplete copy counts; Carrier count with quantitative genotype support; Carrier count with mosaic-supported evidence; Carrier count with mosaicism unsupported; Cohort-wide and every displayed stratum AC/AN. Stratify by: Source-provided ancestry group with AC/AN; Sex metadata as descriptive metadata only; chr22 is autosomal; Cohort/release/run; Mosaic evidence status, not mixed into allele frequency. Missingness: Missing insert sequence, subfamily/TSD/orientation, genotype support, calibrated mosaic assay, no-call reason, or event-class callability is unavailable/data-blocked, never reference and never zero. Mosaicism unsupported means the evidence cannot establish mosaicism; it does not mean non-mosaic. Confidence boundary: Only after complete insertion-event AN is established: for AC=0, report the chosen exact/binomial method. A conditional rule-of-three illustration at AN=584 is approximately 0.00514; the current live check does not establish event AN=584.

Safety boundary — browser can support: A verified paper-to-GRCh38 insertion-site overlay; Tiered sequence-identical, structure-comparable, same-site different insertion, ordinary overlap, not observed, or data-blocked population-reference results; Carrier occurrence, event-level AC/AN, missingness, and provenance when supported; An explicit mosaicism-unsupported result when quantitative/calibrated evidence is absent; A reproducible handoff for external MEI review. Browser cannot support: Diagnosis of ATRT or rhabdoid tumor predisposition; Pathogenicity, benignity, causality, penetrance, recurrence risk, or clinical classification; Transfer of the paper family's maternal segregation, tumor second-hit, splicing, or mosaic evidence to a reference participant; Sequence-identical recurrence without complete sequence/breakpoint evidence; Mosaicism from low cohort frequency, ordinary heterozygosity, or uncalibrated allele balance; A true absence claim without insertion-event representation and callability; Patient upload, PCR/Sanger validation, or replacement for clinical laboratory review. Required wording: sequence-identical represented SVA-E observed in AC/AN callable chromosome copies; structure-comparable SVA-E; nucleotide identity unresolved; same-site different insertion; ordinary nearby overlap only—not the paper MEI; mosaicism unsupported—quantitative/calibrated source evidence is absent; not observed in this release only when insertion-event AN is complete; data-blocked—MEI representation, genotype evidence, or callability is insufficient; population-reference evidence only; not diagnostic and not a pathogenicity or benignity classification

Reproducible handoff — roles: Mobile-element/structural-variation analyst; Genome-build/remap reviewer; Callset and genotype-semantics owner; Clinical genetics safety reviewer. Required export fields: paper DOI/PMID, hg19 coordinate, and PDF citations; GRCh38 mapped base/interbase junction and remap/context hash; display region and CTA verification status; insert length, sequence/hash availability, SVA subfamily, orientation, domains, poly(A), target motif, and TSD; candidate source_variant_id/alt_index and exact/structure/overlap class; carrier GT/ploidy and DP/GQ/AD/PL/caller support when available; mosaic-evidence status, tissue, assay, threshold, measured fraction, and unsupported reason; event AC/AN, no-call and representation-mismatch counts by cohort/stratum; source URI/generation, database, release, run_id, status, query time, filters, and receipt hash; forbidden clinical interpretation. Shareable state: Verified-region/remap receipt; MEI structure and candidate-match ledger; Carrier-versus-mosaic evidence table; Event denominator and missingness table; P/I/B evidence ledger

branches.action: Permit the verified region and exact-site overlay, but keep nucleotide-identical matching unavailable.

branches.condition: Same junction, TSD, orientation, and complete insert sequence/hash match
branches.action: Label sequence-identical SVA-E and proceed to genotype/callability review.

branches.condition: Same junction, length/subfamily/domain/TSD structure match but nucleotide sequence is unavailable
branches.action: Label structure-comparable SVA-E; explicitly withhold sequence-identical recurrence.

branches.condition: Same site but subfamily, TSD, sequence, orientation, or domain structure differs
branches.action: Label same-site different insertion and stop equivalence claims.

branches.condition: Only a nearby SNV/indel, generic insertion, gene overlap, or insertion-family group exists
branches.action: Label ordinary nearby overlap only and stop MEI equivalence claims.

branches.condition: The source/API omits sequence/subfamily/TSD/orientation needed for the requested tier
branches.action: Return data-blocked for that tier rather than guessing from position and length.

branches.condition: GT supports an alternate allele but quantitative support/calibration is absent
branches.action: Report ordinary carrier; mosaicism unsupported.

branches.condition: Low alternate fraction is quantitatively observed but the source has no validated mosaic assay/threshold
branches.action: Report low-balance genotype evidence; mosaicism unsupported.

branches.condition: Quantitative evidence passes a predeclared validated source-specific mosaic rule
branches.action: Report mosaic-supported with measured fraction, depth, threshold, assay, tissue, and uncertainty; do not transfer clinical meaning.

branches.condition: Only low cohort AC/AF is available
branches.action: Do not infer within-person mosaicism; report cohort rarity only.

branches.condition: Event-level detection/representation or per-copy callability is incomplete
branches.action: Report data-blocked; do not report 0/584.

branches.condition: No exact/structure-comparable event is found and all event-level copies are callable

branches.action: Mark the handoff incomplete and do not use it for event-level review.

evidence.claim: Targeted sequencing, WES, copy-number analysis, and later short-read WGS did not identify the causal SMARCB1 variant; WGS nevertheless showed heterozygous discordant mapping in intron 2 in sibling II-2.
evidence.citation: Sabatella et al. 2021 PDF pp. 2 and 4 (journal pp. 203 and 205)

evidence.claim: PacBio HiFi sequencing at 8x identified a 2,763 nt insertion 33 bp downstream of exon 2 at hg19 genomic position chr22:24,134,114 in SMARCB1 intron 2; Fig. 2 shows two alternative-supporting reads and two wild-type reads.
evidence.citation: Sabatella et al. 2021 PDF pp. 4 and 6, Fig. 2C

evidence.claim: The insert is an SVA element composed, in the paper's stated order, of a CCCT repeat, an Alu-like repeat, a variable number of GC-rich tandem repeats (VNTRs), a SINE region, and a poly(A) tail.
evidence.citation: Sabatella et al. 2021 PDF p. 5 (journal p. 206)

evidence.claim: The insertion has target-primed reverse-transcription hallmarks: an L1 endonuclease-like target site, a long poly(A) stretch, and a flanking 10 bp target-site duplication.
evidence.citation: Sabatella et al. 2021 PDF p. 5 (journal p. 206)

evidence.claim: RepeatMasker analysis of the full-length SINE region showed strongest resemblance to SVA-E, one of the youngest and most active human-specific SVA subfamilies.
evidence.citation: Sabatella et al. 2021 PDF p. 5 (journal p. 206)

evidence.claim: Both 5-prime and 3-prime breakpoint-spanning PCRs and Sanger sequencing validated the PacBio-predicted junctions. The 3-prime tumor-II-1 product was slightly smaller, interpreted as a shorter poly(A) tract and possible SVA-E instability.
evidence.citation: Sabatella et al. 2021 PDF p. 7, Fig. 3

evidence.claim: Family evidence placed the affected allele on the maternal haplotype: the father had no WGS abnormality, the mother had lower-level discordant mapping at the same position, both sibling tumors retained the maternal allele homozygously across ten informative SNPs in about 16 kb, and breakpoint PCR amplified maternal blood DNA.
evidence.citation: Sabatella et al. 2021 PDF pp. 4 and 7; supplementary Table S1 description

evidence.claim: The maternal mosaic conclusion is qualitative: serial-dilution breakpoint PCR showed lower amplification in the mother than sibling II-2, but the main paper reports no numerical maternal VAF, cell fraction, read count, confidence interval, or calibrated detection threshold.
evidence.citation: Sabatella et al. 2021 PDF pp. 3 and 7; supplementary Fig. S3 description

evidence.claim: The paper demonstrated aberrant splicing from exon 2 into an SVA-E Alu-like-domain acceptor; this is case functional evidence and is not reproduced by population occurrence.
evidence.citation: Sabatella et al. 2021 PDF pp. 7-8, Fig. 4

evidence.claim: UCSC hg19ToHg38 chain mapping sends hg19 chr22:24,134,114 one-to-one on the plus strand to hg38 chr22:23,791,927. Independent 101 bp NCBI contexts from NC_000022.10:24,134,064-24,134,164 and NC_000022.11:23,791,877-23,791,977 are identical with SHA-256 524c42f2127b1fb6a5cc1c12a2b290214935a1bd3344af4d2a612515a29e554e.
evidence.citation: Analyst remap and independent NCBI EFetch sequence-context check, 2026-08-11

evidence.claim: Sequence-identical matching requires the same mapped junction, both breakpoint/TSD sequences, orientation, and full insert sequence or hash. Because the paper does not publish that full sequence, the strongest paper-only template is exact-site and structure-comparable SVA-E, not nucleotide-identical recurrence.
evidence.citation: Analyst reconstruction from P2-P6; requires MEI-domain review

evidence.claim: A nearby SNV/indel carrier, a generic insertion, or a same-site SVA with different subfamily/TSD/sequence is not the paper event. Ordinary carrier overlap and exact MEI structure must be separate result classes.
evidence.citation: Analyst matching rule grounded in P2-P6

evidence.claim: In a population germline VCF, low AC/AF and GT=0/1 describe cohort occurrence, not within-person mosaic fraction. Mosaic-supported requires quantitative sample-level evidence from a validated mosaic assay; absent that, the mandatory result is mosaicism unsupported.
evidence.citation: Analyst safety/data-semantics rule grounded in P8 and current source/API contracts

paper.title: Long-Read Sequencing Revealed Extragenic and Intragenic Duplications of Exons 56–61 in DMD in an Asymptomatic Male and a DMD Patient

locus: DMD exons 56–61 and an extragenic CFAP47-region placement on chrX; paper coordinates are hg19/GRCh37. Candidate GRCh38 reference-context mappings are DMD chrX:31,326,327–31,549,844 for the affected tandem interval, DMD chrX:31,329,852–31,581,111 for the asymptomatic inverted duplicated interval, and chrX:35,836,757–35,927,062 for the extragenic placement reference span; altered-junction remap remains gated.

persona.role: Rare-disease structural-variation researcher or laboratory scientist
persona.context: Research follow-up after exon-level dosage testing reports DMD exons 56–61 duplicated but does not resolve the duplicated genomic segment, placement, orientation, junctions, or product architecture

nonDiagnosticBoundary: This workflow can distinguish represented population-reference architectures and report their callable X-chromosome-copy counts. It cannot infer a reference participant's phenotype, transfer the two paper cases' phenotypes to population carriers, classify an individual's duplication, establish penetrance, or provide diagnosis or genetic counseling.

startingState.trigger: An externally detected DMD exons 56–61 copy gain whose clinical context is discordant, unknown, or intentionally excluded from the population-reference query.
inputs: Original assembly and coordinate convention; the paper uses hg19/GRCh37 and transcript NM_004006.3
Exon-level dosage result and assay limits; MLPA/WES establishes duplicated exon content but not placement or orientation
Both retained-flank junctions, duplicated genomic segment, placement locus, orientation, copy number, local assembly/read support, and orthogonal validation status
For the affected paper architecture: hg19 candidate duplicated interval chrX:31,344,444–31,567,961, with a direct tandem product junction and a two-base AT microhomology normalization ambiguity

For the asymptomatic paper architecture: hg19 duplicated interval chrX:31,347,969–31,599,228 in inverted orientation, linked extragenically to chrX:35,854,874 and chrX:35,945,179 within a larger complex rearrangement
Event-aware GRCh37-to-GRCh38 remap receipt containing source and target accessions, retained flanks, altered junction sequence, endpoint convention, tool/chain version, and sequence hashes
Cohort/release/run, non-PAR X ploidy model, architecture-specific callability rule, callable/no-call chromosome-copy counts, and participant counts kept separate
startingState.question: Does the population release contain the same exon dosage as a resolved intragenic direct tandem duplication, the resolved extragenic inverted placement, or another architecture, and what is the callable X-copy denominator for each architecture?
startingState.stopRule: Stop exact matching if the source build, endpoint convention, altered junction, orientation, placement, or same-copy linkage is unavailable. Stop GRCh38 navigation if only the generic index window or a chain-only coordinate is available. Stop absence claims unless every required junction is representation-completely callable under explicit non-PAR X ploidy. Never use exon dosage alone or a population carrier to infer phenotype.

before: Preserve the paper's hg19/GRCh37 coordinates and its internal discrepancy: Table 1/text give the affected junction endpoint chrX:31,567,961, while the Figure 2 caption gives chrX:31,567,959; retain both until the two-base AT microhomology and Sanger trace establish one normalized event convention.

Represent the two paper findings as separate architecture signatures. The asymptomatic signature is an inverted 251.4 kb DMD segment placed outside DMD in a complex chrX rearrangement; the affected signature is a direct intragenic tandem duplication. 'Exons 56–61 duplicated' is only the shared dosage observation.

Remap complete altered junctions and unique retained flanks to GRCh38. The independently checked constant -18,117 bp reference-context shift supplies candidate coordinates only; reference chain/sequence agreement is not an altered-product junction receipt.

Define exact intragenic-tandem equivalence as sequence-compatible duplicated boundaries, direct head-to-tail orientation, the normalized product junction, copy gain, and same-event/copy linkage. Define exact extragenic equivalence as sequence-compatible DMD donor boundaries, inverted orientation, both DMD-to-placement junctions, placement locus, and same-event/copy linkage; require all ordered complex components only when claiming the complete family-1 complex rearrangement.

Create a synchronized query state rather than one 100 kb locus: provisional GRCh38 windows around both DMD boundary clusters plus the 90.3 kb extragenic placement neighborhood. Block the index's chrX:32,168,643–32,268,643 window because it overlaps none of the mapped paper boundaries.
inside: Verify GRCh38, HGSVC/HPRC, accepted primary database/release/chromosome/run, and modality availability in every synchronized window before comparing records.

Enumerate every DUP, INV_DUP, complex-duplication, BND/CTX/CPX, INS-like, and split representation at all required boundaries. Preserve source_variant_id and ALT index, but do not assume a source record ID is an event/mate identifier.

Apply a paired/event-aware predicate: require all architecture-defining boundaries, orientation, junction sequence, placement, and same-copy linkage. Label interval overlap, one matching boundary, DMD overlap, or the same duplicated exons as candidate/dosage-only evidence.

Compare the two architecture families side by side. Keep the family-1 DMD inverted copy, CFAP47-region placement, deletion, and additional duplications ordered; keep the family-2 direct tandem junction separate even when a flat CNV track shows the same exon copy gain.

For each resolved architecture, report global and XX/XY-stratified event AC/AN, callable X copies, no-call copies, participants, and the ploidy rule. At this non-PAR X locus an XX participant contributes at most two callable copies and an XY participant at most one; neighboring record AN or aggregate base depth is not event callability.

Open a carrier chromosome-copy view only when the exact event, sample identity, deterministic copy assignment, and compatible phase evidence are available. Copy A/B or GT strand is not maternal/paternal identity, and no population copy receives an affected/asymptomatic label.
after: Export original and remapped coordinates, endpoint convention, retained flanks and junction hashes, all component records and ALT indexes, placement/orientation/linkage evidence, exact-versus-candidate classification, event AC/AN, XX/XY callable/no-call counts, participant counts, database/release/run, query windows/payload, timestamp, and browser state.

Hand the bounded architecture result back for patient-specific segregation, dystrophin/RNA/protein evaluation, clinical examination, and expert interpretation outside the browser. Preserve the paper cases as motivating observations, not outcome labels or penetrance evidence.

branches.condition: The build, endpoint convention, altered-junction remap, orientation, placement, or same-copy linkage is missing
branches.action: Report unresolved/data-blocked and list the missing evidence; do not issue an exact-match or not-observed result.

branches.condition: Exons 56–61 have increased dosage but placement, orientation, or junctions differ or are unavailable
branches.action: Report exon-content/dosage similarity only and keep the architecture unresolved or distinct.

branches.condition: Both normalized boundaries, direct tandem orientation, product junction, copy gain, and same-copy linkage match the family-2 signature
branches.action: Report exact comparable intragenic tandem architecture with architecture-specific callable AC/AN and provenance; make no phenotype or clinical-classification claim.

branches.condition: Both DMD donor-to-placement junctions, inverted orientation, extragenic placement, duplicated segment, and same-copy linkage match the family-1 signature
branches.action: Report exact comparable extragenic inverted placement; claim the complete complex rearrangement only if its deletion and additional duplications are also ordered and linked.

branches.condition: Only one boundary, one split record, a generic overlap, or an unlinked set of compatible components is represented
branches.action: Report candidate overlap/partial representation and identify the missing boundary, junction, orientation, placement, or link.

branches.condition: No exact architecture is observed and representation-complete, architecture-specific callability plus X-ploidy reconciliation are available
branches.action: Report not observed in N callable X-chromosome copies, separately for each architecture, with no-call and participant counts and an explicitly conditional upper reference-frequency statement.

branches.condition: No exact row is returned but any junction, representation family, event linkage, or callable X-copy denominator is incomplete
branches.action: Report data-blocked, not AC=0 and not absent.

story.given: a DMD exons 56–61 dosage gain plus its original-build boundaries, junction evidence, placement and orientation, with the affected paper tandem endpoint retained as chrX:31,567,959/31,567,961 until AT-microhomology normalization is resolved
story.when: the researcher validates an altered-junction GRCh38 remap, opens synchronized DMD-boundary and extragenic-placement windows, links all required records on one chromosome copy, compares direct tandem versus inverted extragenic architecture, and audits event-callable non-PAR X denominators
story.then: the browser returns exact intragenic tandem, exact extragenic inverted placement, architecture-distinct/dosage-only candidate, not observed in N callable X copies, or data-blocked, with component/linkage and provenance receipts and without assigning phenotype or clinical meaning

browserRegionBlockedReason: data-blocked: the index's generic GRCh38 chrX:32,168,643–32,268,643 window is not event-specific and overlaps none of the independently chain/sequence-mapped paper boundaries. No single <=100 kb window can represent both DMD donor boundaries and the extragenic placement, and current navigation cannot retain a paired/three-window linked-event receipt. Candidate windows must remain provisional until altered-junction remap validation.

capabilities.step: Navigate to individually bounded candidate GRCh38 windows with accepted chrX primary provenance
capabilities.evidence: On 2026-08-11 the production corrected-boundary region route and API queries returned HTTP 200 with accepted full-chromosome chrX primary provenance. The generic index route also returns 200, but routability does not make its coordinates relevant.

capabilities.step: Replace the generic index window with an event-aware GRCh37-to-GRCh38 mapping
capabilities.evidence: UCSC hg19ToHg38 chain and sequence checks mapped all printed boundary bases with a constant -18,117 bp shift and identical reference contexts, but the paper's altered product junctions were not available as a machine-readable remap input. The 31,567,959/31,567,961 conflict also remains normalization-sensitive.

capabilities.step: Keep multiple DMD and placement windows synchronized as one linked-event query
capabilities.evidence: Current LiteratureWorkflow has one browserRegion or a blocked state, region URLs carry one interval, and neither UI nor GraphQL defines a paired-window/linked-event query receipt.

capabilities.step: Distinguish direct tandem from inverted extragenic placement using orientation and junctions
capabilities.evidence: LongReadVariant exposes position/end/length/REF/ALT/type/source IDs and frequencies, but no explicit junction sequence, orientation, placement/mate, EVENT/MATEID, second chromosome, ordered component path, or copy-number field.

capabilities.step: Group all records belonging to one complex duplication architecture
capabilities.evidence: Current source-event aggregation normalizes duplication subtypes but keys non-deletions by exact reference interval; source_variant_id is explicitly not a guaranteed event ID. Overlap and source prefixes are intentionally insufficient, and separate coordinates are not linked.

capabilities.step: Search exact boundaries and junction sequence
capabilities.evidence: Current local search supports overlapping ranges, positions, identifiers, REF/ALT, and bounded sequence fragments, but comma/newline terms are OR. Sequence matching only inspects REF/ALT/motifs and cannot require all linked boundaries or a junction not present in those fields.

capabilities.step: Use callable non-PAR X chromosome-copy denominators
capabilities.evidence: Live records expose row AC/AN and XX/XY strata, but no exact paper-like event exists and there is no architecture-specific callable/no-call X-copy receipt. Checked structural rows had varying AN, including zeros; neighboring rows and coverage cannot supply an event-negative denominator.

capabilities.step: Inspect event-bearing chromosome-copy context
capabilities.evidence: Production provenance marks HAPLOTYPES unavailable for the accepted chrX run. Even where haplotypes exist, the current contract would still require exact-event linkage and valid copy/phase evidence before joining context.

capabilities.step: Conclude exact population occurrence or safe absence
capabilities.evidence: Across four corrected candidate windows the live API returned 568–1,055 records per window but no >=1 kb event and no relevant DUP/INV_DUP/CPX architecture; it cannot certify representation-complete search or event callability, so the result is data-blocked rather than absent.

capabilities.step: Open a curated DMD detailed-workflow page
capabilities.evidence: Production returned HTTP 404 for this slug. Current source commit c412e2b8 contains 12 records (the four prototypes and eight Batch-1 records) and no ref-19 workflow record.

capabilities.step: Infer affected, asymptomatic, pathogenic, or benign status from a population architecture
capabilities.evidence: The paper is a two-family case comparison, not a penetrance study, and the population cohort has no validated DMD phenotype layer. Architecture can prioritize external review but cannot determine phenotype or diagnosis.

acceptanceTest.fixture: GRCh38 non-PAR chrX fixtures containing: (A) a direct intragenic head-to-tail duplication with the family-2 duplicated segment, linked boundaries and AT-microhomology-normalized junction; (B) the same biological tandem event shifted by two bases within the microhomology; (C) an inverted DMD exon-56–61-containing copy linked by both junctions to the extragenic CFAP47-region placement, with ordered family-1 complex components; (D) a same-exon-dosage interspersed duplication with different placement/orientation; (E) one-boundary and unlinked split records; and (F) callable XX and XY reference copies plus explicit no-call copies and a representation-complete no-event state. Include external paper-case phenotype labels only in a separate, non-query metadata fixture.
acceptanceTest.actions: Attempt the generic index link and require it to fail closed; load a validated altered-junction remap receipt; open and share the synchronized DMD-boundary and placement windows; enumerate all ALTs/components; run exact and dosage-only matching; inspect linkage, orientation, placement, event AC/AN, XX/XY callable/no-call copies and provenance; attempt a phenotype inference; export and reload the analysis receipt.
acceptanceTest.expected: The generic window is rejected as irrelevant. A/B collapse to one exact intragenic-tandem event after documented microhomology normalization. C remains a separate exact extragenic-inverted architecture and exposes its ordered components. D is dosage-similar but architecture-distinct; E is partial/data-blocked. F reports not observed only when every required junction is callable and shows event AC/AN, XX/XY and no-call counts. No population fixture receives a phenotype label. The reloaded export reconstructs all windows, components, mappings, classifications, denominators and provenance exactly.
acceptanceTest.forbidden: The result must not group events solely because exons 56–61 are duplicated, call one boundary or overlap exact, treat source_variant_id as mate/event linkage, use participant N or neighboring/base-depth AN as callable X copies, convert missingness to zero, treat copy A/B as parental identity, transfer affected/asymptomatic labels to population carriers, or label an architecture pathogenic, benign, causal, protective, diagnostic, or suitable for counseling.

evidence.claim: WES and both long-read pipelines were aligned to hg19/GRCh37; DMD target analysis used NM_004006.3. The paper does not provide a GRCh38 event notation.
evidence.citation: PDF pp. 2–3, Whole-Exome Sequencing, Nanopore LRS, PacBio SMRT target sequencing, and junction-PCR methods

evidence.claim: Family 1 III:2 (age 33) and uncle II:9 (age 44) carried the exon 56–61 dosage gain, had no reported DMD symptoms, mildly elevated CK values of 288 and 204 IU/L (reference 24–195), and normal surface EMG; the mother also carried the duplication.
evidence.citation: PDF pp. 3–4, Fig. 1 and Clinical Description and Genetic Analysis

evidence.claim: Family 2 II:6 was a 23-year-old male described as typical DMD: unable to run or jump, wheelchair-dependent at 11, CK 12,696 IU/L, and on 24-hour ventilation for seven years; the exon 56–61 duplication was maternally inherited.
evidence.citation: PDF p. 4, Clinical Description and Genetic Analysis

evidence.claim: In family 1, the exon-containing segment is printed as hg19 chrX:31,347,969–31,599,228 (about 251.4 kb) and is an INVDUP placed outside DMD within a complex duplication-deletion-INVDUP-duplication-duplication arrangement. The two Sanger-supported DMD-to-placement joins pair 31,347,969 with 35,854,874 and 31,599,228 with 35,945,179.
evidence.citation: PDF p. 4 Table 1 and Breakpoint Analysis; p. 5 Fig. 2A and caption

evidence.claim: The additional family-1 hg19 components printed in Fig. 2 are chrX:35,857,033–35,861,970 DEL, chrX:35,854,874–35,857,033 DUP, chrX:35,878,354–35,891,965 DUP, and chrX:35,878,354–35,945,179 DUP. Several non-INVDUP junctions were supported by LRS/target sequencing but not Sanger; the authors state other outside-DMD junctions need further validation.
evidence.citation: PDF pp. 4–6, Table 1, Fig. 2A, and Discussion

evidence.claim: In family 2, the paper prints a direct tandem duplication interval hg19 chrX:31,344,444–31,567,961 with both endpoints Sanger/SMRT-supported. Text/Table 1 use junction coordinate 31,567,961, while the Fig. 2 caption uses 31,567,959; the reported two-base AT microhomology makes endpoint normalization an explicit gate.
evidence.citation: PDF p. 4 Table 1 and Breakpoint Analysis; p. 5 Fig. 2B/caption; p. 4 microhomology paragraph

evidence.claim: The paper reports 4 bp TTGC and 27 bp CTGCCTCAGCCTCCCGAGTAGCTGGGA microhomologies at the two INVDUP junctions and 2 bp AT at the tandem junction; repetitive SINE/LINE elements flank family-1 breakpoints and an AT-rich low-complexity repeat flanks the family-2 junction.
evidence.citation: PDF p. 4, microhomology analysis and Table 1

evidence.claim: The authors predict that the intragenic tandem duplication creates frameshift p.(Thr3055Argfs*5), while explaining the phenotype contrast by different breakpoint junctions. This is a two-unrelated-family report, not a population penetrance estimate.
evidence.citation: PDF pp. 4 and 6, Discussion and Conclusion

evidence.claim: The two findings are exon-content/dosage-identical but not duplicated-sequence-identical: their printed genomic intervals differ (251,260 versus 223,518 bases under an inclusive convention), and their placement and orientation are different. A browser must not collapse them by exon list or copy gain.
evidence.citation: Analyst reconstruction from PDF Table 1/Fig. 2; requires paper-truth and workflow review

evidence.claim: An exact architecture match requires all sequence-compatible boundaries, altered junction(s), orientation, placement and same-copy/event linkage. The complete family-1 CPX additionally requires its ordered deletion and other duplications; a DMD overlap or one DUP row is only a candidate.
evidence.citation: Analyst reconstruction from paper architecture and current source-event limitations; requires workflow review

evidence.claim: UCSC hg19ToHg38 chain SHA-256 5c0598e500ceb5a78c73086929e8ef993aec309bcafb595139b53d440b125a1d maps all printed boundary bases at + strand with a constant -18,117 bp shift. Eleven 201 bp flanks and the three checked reference intervals were sequence-identical between assemblies, yielding candidate GRCh38 coordinates; altered-junction validation and endpoint normalization are still required.
evidence.citation: Read-only UCSC chain/API reference-context verification, 2026-08-11; remap-verification receipt summarized in evidence markdown

evidence.claim: The index window chrX:32,168,643–32,268,643 is not an event window: it overlaps neither candidate DMD interval nor the extragenic placement. A faithful workflow needs synchronized boundary/placement windows and one linked-event receipt.
evidence.citation: Analyst comparison of index coordinates with paper and independently checked candidate GRCh38 boundaries

evidence.claim: At non-PAR DMD, denominator units are callable X chromosome copies under an explicit ploidy model, at most two per XX participant and one per XY participant. Architecture-specific callability requires all defining junctions; roster participants, neighboring record AN and aggregate coverage are not substitutes.
evidence.citation: Analyst denominator contract; requires data-semantics review

evidence.claim: The paper's 'asymptomatic' family-1 label is bounded by reported symptoms, CK and EMG, not proof of lifelong absence of dystrophinopathy; the affected/asymptomatic contrast must remain external case context and cannot label population carriers or establish benign/pathogenic architecture by itself.
evidence.citation: Analyst safety boundary from PDF clinical descriptions and two-family design; requires clinical/product review

evidence.claim: On 2026-08-11 four corrected candidate-window API queries returned 1,043, 1,055, 568 and 1,005 records. None contained an event >=1 kb or a relevant DUP/INV_DUP/CPX; only a 10 bp DUP occurred in one DMD-left window and a 316 bp alu_del in one DMD-right window. This is data-blocked, not certified absence.
evidence.citation: Read-only production GraphQL checks against gnomad-lr-api-00018-xoz, 2026-08-11

evidence.claim: The generic index window returned 2,423 records and eight DUP-typed alleles, all only 9–89 bp, demonstrating that a populated/HTTP-200 window is not evidence that it covers the paper event.
evidence.citation: Read-only production GraphQL and route check for chrX:32,168,643–32,268,643, 2026-08-11

evidence.claim: Production provenance identifies accepted GRCh38 chrX primary run y1-full-prototype-hgsvc-hprc-chrX-aggregate-20260803T214532Z-4f2676-r1 in database gnomad_lr_y1_scratch_demo_full_genome_20260803, but marks HAPLOTYPES unavailable. Checked structural-row AN ranged down to zero and up to 365, with XX up to 292 and XY up to 73; no exact-event AN exists.
evidence.citation: Read-only production GraphQL provenance/frequency checks, 2026-08-11

evidence.claim: Current source commit c412e2b8 exposes source/ALT identity, interval and frequency fields, exact interval/family source-event grouping, OR range/identifier/sequence search and a 100 kb Haplotype View cap, but no junction/orientation/mate/event/copy-number contract or paired-window receipt. Ref 19 is not among its 12 detailed records; production returns 404 for the slug.
evidence.citation: Current source and read-only production route checks, 2026-08-11

capabilityBasis: Read-only manifest, complete seven-page PDF, shared-schema, implemented-record, current-source, UCSC reference-context, production route and HGSVC/HPRC API checks on 2026-08-11. Current browser source commit c412e2b895f061314f874a9e05c9fed6e7835dc6; deployed API/browser revisions gnomad-lr-api-00018-xoz and gnomad-lr-browser-00012-suv. Individual route success and reference-only liftover do not establish altered-junction equivalence, event linkage, event callability, phenotype, or safe absence.

paper.title: Long‐Read Sequencing Resolves a Complex Structural Variant in PRKN Parkinson's Disease

locus: PRKN/FRA6E · separate GRCh38 inversion chr6:161,351,957–168,777,862 and exon 3 deletion chr6:162,214,329–162,274,466; exact architecture requires three synchronized windows and linkage/phase receipts

persona.role: Structural-variation researcher or molecular genetics laboratory scientist
persona.context: Research comparison after an external assay has identified a PRKN inversion, exon deletion, or unresolved second allele; the browser supplies population-reference structure only.

nonDiagnosticBoundary: The browser cannot diagnose Parkinson's disease, assign pathogenicity or benignity, equate exon overlap with exact recurrence, call inversion and deletion one complex event, infer trans phase without evidence, or convert absence among 292 reference participants into causal evidence. Population-reference evidence only; not diagnostic and not a pathogenicity or benignity classification.

startingState.trigger: An external GRCh38 result suggests a PRKN inversion and/or exon 3 deletion, and the researcher needs to distinguish exact recurrence of the paper architecture from a different inversion that merely overlaps PRKN.
inputs: Paper inversion notation as rendered: NC_00006.12:g.161351957_168777862inv; normalized canonical GRCh38 accession: NC_000006.12
Paper exon 3 deletion interval chr6:162214329-162274466del and transcript notation c.(171+1_172-1)_(412+1_413-1)del
All four genomic boundaries, orientation, no-insertion statement for the inversion junctions, and breakpoint-validation evidence
External assay, caller, sample, build, phase/inheritance, and uncertainty provenance
Predeclared comparison class: exact inversion, exact deletion, full inversion-plus-deletion genotype, competing PRKN-affecting inversion, or generic overlap
Separate source-specific callable denominators for every comparison class
Known unknown: Whether any population call is the same two-junction inversion rather than another PRKN-overlapping inversion
Known unknown: Whether the exact exon 3 deletion and exact inversion occur in one participant and are proven in trans
Known unknown: Whether all four boundaries and the 7.43 Mb span are event-callable on each chromosome copy
Known unknown: The exact coordinates and final adjudication of the paper's nine UK Biobank exon-affecting inversion candidates because Supplementary Table S5 is absent
Known unknown: Whether the paper's inconsistent comparator totals and UK Biobank candidate accounting can be reconciled from the supplement
startingState.question: Is the exact paper inversion, the exact exon 3 deletion, or the complete inversion-plus-deletion genotype represented in callable HGSVC/HPRC data, or are returned records only different PRKN-overlapping inversions/structural calls? Allowed outcomes: Return exactly classified outcomes: exact inversion recurrence; exact deletion recurrence; full genotype recurrence with explicit phase; competing PRKN-affecting inversion; candidate overlap only; not observed in representation-complete event-callable data; or data-blocked. Every result includes the matching rule, appropriate denominator, missingness, release/run, and multi-window receipt.
startingState.stopRule: Stop when any required item is missing: GRCh38 build and all four genomic boundaries; A linked-event receipt proving both inversion junctions belong to one inversion; A participant/copy receipt proving inversion and deletion relationship before calling the full genotype recurrent; Event-callable denominators specific to exact inversion, exact deletion, and joint genotype; A source-specific representation and QC rule before comparing to the short-read Manta candidates.

before: Record the inversion and exon 3 deletion as two separate GRCh38 variants, preserve all four boundaries and paper notations, and record twin/maternal inheritance separately from proven molecular phase. Required evidence: Canonical and paper-rendered accession notation; Two inversion boundaries and two deletion boundaries; Assay and validation evidence; Participant-level inheritance/phase evidence; Representation and comparator-count discrepancies. UI/API boundary: The literature record must not collapse the two variants into one symbol or silently convert inferred inheritance into proven trans phase. Expected: One exact inversion object, one exact deletion object, and a separately qualified participant genotype relationship.

Predeclare exact inversion, exact deletion, full phased genotype, competing PRKN-affecting inversion, and generic-overlap rules before viewing population calls. Required evidence: Exact paper intervals and orientation; Allowed breakpoint uncertainty, if any, with source; Manta broad comparator rule; Same-event and trans-phase requirements. UI/API boundary: Show exact and overlap results in separate classes; never promote transcript overlap or similar size to exact recurrence. Expected: A machine-readable classification rule with no post hoc distance tolerance.
inside: Open chr6:161326957-161376957, chr6:162194397-162294397, and chr6:168752862-168802862 under one HGSVC/HPRC build/cohort/release/run state. Required evidence: Direct GRCh38 boundary validation; Three bounded regions; One accepted chr6 primary/haplotype run; A synchronized multi-window query receipt. UI/API boundary: Render three synchronized panels or one linked-event workspace; do not use the index's unrelated/truncated 100 kb window as the event overlay. Expected: Both inversion neighborhoods and the complete exon deletion are visible under identical provenance.

Reconcile INV/BND/CPX and DEL representations; require both inversion junctions to form one oriented event and both deletion boundaries to form the exact 60,138 bp deletion before evaluating participant-level phase. Required evidence: Source records and complete ALT/INFO semantics; Breakpoint orientation and interval uncertainty; Mate/event linkage or an equivalent symbolic-INV identity; Carrier chromosome-copy identity at all three windows; Exact and overlap classifications. UI/API boundary: Display constituents and missing components. A 54 kb insertion, one nearby breakend, or another exon-overlapping inversion remains a candidate/competitor. Expected: Separate exact-inversion, exact-deletion, competing-inversion, candidate-overlap, representation-mismatch, and data-blocked labels.

Report exact inversion AC/AN, exact deletion AC/AN, and phased joint-genotype count/participant denominator separately; also report partial, competing, representation-mismatch, and no-call counts. Required evidence: All-component event callability; Participant and chromosome-copy carrier identity; Phase confidence; Cohort strata; Source/caller-specific comparator eligibility. UI/API boundary: Never substitute AN from one nearby record or the maximum 584 autosomal copies for inversion-event AN. Never pool UK Biobank/AMP-PD Manta candidates with Y1 exact matches. Expected: Separate denominators for exact inversion copies, exact deletion copies, joint callable participants, and broad competing-inversion screens.
after: Export paper and normalized notation, three windows, constituent records, linkage/phase receipts, exact-versus-competing rule, all denominators, missingness, source/run, and comparator discrepancies for structural-variation review. Required evidence: Multi-window state; Inversion event and deletion event receipts; Participant phase status; Denominator and provenance tables; P/I/B ledger and safety wording. UI/API boundary: Reloading the export must reconstruct all panels and classifications without relying on screenshots or manuscript prose. Expected: A reproducible handoff limited to population-reference occurrence, competition, not-observed, or data-blocked outcomes.

Comparison contract — Paper GRCh38 inversion NC_000006.12:g.161351957_168777862inv versus One HGSVC/HPRC chromosome-copy inversion: Exact recurrence requires both paper boundaries, inversion orientation, and one linked symbolic-INV or reciprocal-junction event after representation normalization; any different PRKN-overlapping inversion is competing architecture. Unit: linked inversion event per callable chromosome copy.

Comparison contract — Paper GRCh38 exon 3 deletion chr6:162214329-162274466del versus One HGSVC/HPRC chromosome-copy deletion: Exact recurrence requires both deletion boundaries and the 60,138 bp deleted interval after normalized representation; similar exon dosage or overlap is insufficient. Unit: exact deletion event per callable chromosome copy.

Comparison contract — Paper twin genotype: exact inversion plus exact exon 3 deletion versus One HGSVC/HPRC participant: Full comparable genotype requires both exact events in one participant plus explicit trans phase; co-occurrence without phase is a separate unresolved class. Unit: phased two-event genotype per callable participant.

Comparison contract — Paper short-read comparator candidates versus HGSVC/HPRC structural calls: Broad competing class follows the paper's Manta rule (inversion, affects PRKN transcript, 50 bp-10 Mb, IGV-QC) but must remain separate by caller/technology and must not be counted as exact recurrence. Unit: source-specific screened participant and inversion call.

Threshold boundary — 100,000 bp maximum Y1 Haplotype View span. Source/scope: Current browser source LongReadUnifiedView.tsx:313 / UI rendering limit. Do not generalize: This is not a biological threshold; the 7.43 Mb inversion plus a separate 60.1 kb deletion requires three linked windows.

Threshold boundary — Paper comparator filter: inversion affecting a PRKN transcript and size 50 bp to 10 Mb, followed by IGV review. Source/scope: Daida et al. 2023 PDF p. 3 / UK Biobank/AMP-PD short-read competing-inversion screen. Do not generalize: This broad rule does not establish exact recurrence, equivalence across callers, pathogenicity, or a Y1 callable denominator.

Threshold boundary — No post hoc breakpoint-distance tolerance; exact means the paper's four GRCh38 boundaries after representation normalization. Source/scope: Analyst rule grounded in exact paper coordinates / This dossier. Do not generalize: A future caller-specific confidence interval may define a reviewed tolerance, but display-window overlap is never exact matching.

Threshold boundary — Only if AC=0 and the relevant event-level AN is complete, report an exact-binomial or declared rule-of-three upper bound. Source/scope: Statistical reporting convention / Conditional population-reference absence. Do not generalize: Current checks do not establish inversion-event AN=584, deletion-event AN=584, or joint participant N=292.

Failure recovery — The current index window is treated as the paper event. Detect: chr6:161987596-162087596 contains none of the four paper boundaries. Recover: Use the three validated windows or block the Try-in-browser action until multi-window state exists.

Failure recovery — Any PRKN exon-overlapping inversion is called recurrent. Detect: Breakpoints, size, orientation, or event linkage differ from the paper inversion. Recover: Label competing inversion and preserve exact-versus-overlap rule.

Failure recovery — The inversion and deletion are collapsed into one complex event or assumed trans. Detect: No separate event identities and participant-level phase receipt are present. Recover: Report each event separately; label co-occurrence phase unresolved until proven.

Failure recovery — The paper's 43,538/4,941 abstract totals, 43,858/3,403 methods totals, or nine-candidate count are silently harmonized. Detect: A record provides one number without section/QC provenance or omits the false-positive inconsistency. Recover: Retain both count sets and require Supplementary Table S5 before enumerating candidates.

Failure recovery — Record AN or 584 maximum copies is reported as event AN. Detect: The denominator lacks both inversion junctions, deletion callability, or participant phase eligibility. Recover: Compute class-specific callable intersections or report data-blocked.

Denominator contract — unit: Parallel, non-interchangeable units: one linked inversion event per callable chromosome copy; one exact deletion event per callable chromosome copy; one phased two-event genotype per callable participant; and one source-specific screened participant/call for the broad competing-inversion comparison. Callable only when: An inversion copy is callable only when the accepted source/caller can detect and link both junctions/orientation across 7.43 Mb; a deletion copy is callable only for both exact boundaries; a joint participant is callable only for both events plus phase eligibility. Ordinary variant AN, local coverage, or callability in one window is insufficient. Required counts: Participants queried and maximum possible autosomal copies; Exact inversion AC and event AN; Exact deletion AC and event AN; Participants with both exact events, with proven trans, proven cis, or unresolved phase; Joint-genotype callable participant denominator; Competing PRKN-affecting inversion count under a declared caller/technology rule; Partial/unlinked candidate, representation-mismatch, and no-call counts; Cohort-wide and every displayed stratum AC/AN for each eligible event class. Stratify by: Source-provided ancestry group with AC/AN; Cohort/release/run and caller/technology; Case/control ascertainment only for the paper comparator, never inferred for HGSVC/HPRC. Missingness: Any missing junction, missing exact boundary, absent event/copy linkage, unresolved phase, uncertain representation, or missing class-specific callability is unavailable/data-blocked for that class, not a reference call and not zero. Strata with AN=0 display unavailable. Confidence boundary: Only after the relevant class-specific denominator is complete: for AC=0, report the declared exact-binomial method or rule-of-three upper bound. Current checks do not justify 0/584 exact inversions, 0/584 exact deletions, or 0/292 phased genotypes.

Safety boundary — browser can support: Whether an exactly represented inversion or deletion is observed in its own callable HGSVC/HPRC units; Whether both exact events co-occur and, only with evidence, are in trans in a callable participant; Whether another PRKN-overlapping inversion is a competing architecture rather than exact recurrence; Explicit class-specific denominators, missingness, provenance, and a reproducible multi-window handoff once the data model exists. Browser cannot support: Diagnosis of Parkinson's disease or PRKN-PD; Pathogenicity, benignity, penetrance, causality, or individual risk; Transfer of the twins' phenotype or paper authors' likely-damaging interpretation to reference participants; A true absence claim while event representation/linkage/callability is unavailable; Trans phase from co-occurrence alone; Reconciliation of missing Supplementary Table S5 candidate details; Patient upload, transcript-effect validation, PCR, or replacement for clinical variant review. Required wording: exact represented inversion/deletion observed in AC/AN callable units; competing PRKN-affecting inversion—different architecture, not exact recurrence; co-occurrence with phase unresolved unless a trans receipt is present; not observed in this release only when class-specific representation and callability are complete; data-blocked—linkage, phase, representation, or callability is insufficient; population-reference evidence only; not diagnostic and not a pathogenicity or benignity classification

Reproducible handoff — roles: Structural-variation analyst; PRKN/disease-area scientist; Callset/data-semantics owner; Clinical genetics safety reviewer. Required export fields: paper DOI/PMID and original/normalized accession notation; all four GRCh38 boundaries and coordinate convention; three region URLs and shared cohort/build/run state; source_variant_ids, ALT indices, types, intervals, orientation, event/mate/copy links; separate exact inversion, exact deletion, competing inversion, overlap, and joint-genotype labels; phase/inheritance evidence and confidence; class-specific AC/AN, participant denominator, strata, partial/no-call/representation-mismatch counts; source VCF URI/generation, database, release, run_id, status, query timestamp; paper comparator count/QC discrepancies and missing-supplement status; filters, UI state, matching rule, and forbidden interpretation. Shareable state: Three-window query receipt; Two-event constituent and phase diagram; Machine-readable result/denominator table; P/I/B evidence ledger

acceptanceTest.fixture: Six pinned fixtures: A exact two-junction inversion only; B exact deletion only; C both exact events proven in trans; D a different PRKN exon-overlapping inversion; E a generic 54 kb insertion/one-breakpoint overlap; F one or more uncallable/unlinkable components.
acceptanceTest.actions: Load all three windows under one accepted HGSVC/HPRC chr6 state; Run exact and broad comparator matching and inspect all event constituents/orientations; Inspect chromosome-copy and participant phase evidence; Inspect exact-event AC/AN, joint participant denominator, strata, partial calls, no-calls, and provenance; Export and reload the receipt.
acceptanceTest.expected: A is exact inversion recurrence only; B is exact deletion recurrence only; C is full comparable phased genotype; D is competing PRKN-affecting inversion, never exact recurrence; E is candidate overlap only and lists missing/mismatched components; F is data-blocked, never zero; Every class has its own callable denominator or an explicit unavailable status; Reload reconstructs all three windows, both event definitions, phase state, classifications, counts, and run identity.
