evidence.claim: The study concerns affected monozygotic twins of Japanese ancestry with onset at age 17; no other family member had diagnosed Parkinson's or another neurological disease.
evidence.citation: Daida et al. 2023 PDF pp. 2 and 4 (journal pp. 2250, 2252)

evidence.claim: Targeted panel/WES found heterozygous PRKN c.814C>A (p.L272I), but its 0.014 frequency in 38KJPN led the authors to treat it as a relatively common polymorphism rather than the causal second allele.
evidence.citation: Daida et al. 2023 PDF p. 5 (journal p. 2253)

evidence.claim: MLPA and long reads identified a heterozygous 60,138 bp GRCh38 exon 3 deletion in both twins but not their mother: chr6:162214329-162274466del, also written c.(171+1_172-1)_(412+1_413-1)del.
evidence.citation: Daida et al. 2023 PDF pp. 4-6; Fig. 1B-C

evidence.claim: Long reads identified a separate heterozygous inversion in both twins and their mother, rendered in the paper as NC_00006.12:g.161351957_168777862inv and described as approximately 7,425,905 bp/7.4 Mb, involving PRKN exons 1-11.
evidence.citation: Daida et al. 2023 PDF pp. 5-6; Fig. 3

evidence.claim: The author-labeled 5-prime inversion breakpoint at chr6:161351957 is in PRKN intron 11 and was predicted to separate exon 12 from the remaining transcript; the distal author-labeled 3-prime breakpoint is chr6:168777862. No insertion sequence was present at either inversion breakpoint.
evidence.citation: Daida et al. 2023 PDF pp. 5-6; Fig. 3A-B

evidence.claim: PCR confirmed both inversion breakpoints, additional short-read WGS confirmed the inversion and deletion, and ONT data were generated at approximately 38x with average read N50 19 kb.
evidence.citation: Daida et al. 2023 PDF p. 5 (journal p. 2253)

evidence.claim: Inversion breakpoint context included a 148 bp SINE 96 bp upstream of the 5-prime breakpoint and a 245 bp LINE 178 bp downstream of the 3-prime breakpoint; 100 bp flanks had 37.1% similarity and no palindrome. The exon 3 deletion had blunt ends, a 3-prime SINE context, and 42.3% flank similarity.
evidence.citation: Daida et al. 2023 PDF p. 6 (journal p. 2254)

evidence.claim: Comparator counts differ inside the paper: the abstract reports 43,538 UK Biobank and 4,941 AMP-PD participants; methods/results report 43,858 UK Biobank participants and 3,403 AMP-PD samples after QC (1,131 controls, 2,272 cases).
evidence.citation: Daida et al. 2023 PDF pp. 1-2, 3, and 6

evidence.claim: The short-read comparator selected Manta calls that were inversions, affected a PRKN transcript, and were 50 bp to 10 Mb, followed by IGV review. This is a broad competing-inversion definition, not exact breakpoint matching.
evidence.citation: Daida et al. 2023 PDF p. 3 (journal p. 2251)

evidence.claim: AMP-PD had 11 inversion calls in 17 subjects; two exon-affecting calls came from the same PD subject, and short reads could not establish whether those two were on the same allele. UK Biobank had 31 calls in 46 subjects, including nine exon-affecting calls and 22 intronic calls; all exon-affecting calls were in non-PD subjects.
evidence.citation: Daida et al. 2023 PDF pp. 6-7 (journal pp. 2254-2255)

evidence.claim: The UK Biobank accounting is internally ambiguous: one of nine exon-including inversions was called false-positive by IGV, but the next summary still says nine UK Biobank inversions and two AMP-PD inversions were potential transcript-affecting events. The supplement is needed to resolve the final set.
evidence.citation: Daida et al. 2023 PDF p. 7 (journal p. 2255); Supplementary Fig. S5/Table S5 referenced

evidence.claim: The authors did not find the exact family inversion or a similar-size inversion in the surveyed short-read datasets. Limitations included no RNA data, unavailable father DNA, and comparator analysis restricted to European-ancestry individuals.
evidence.citation: Daida et al. 2023 PDF pp. 7-8 (journal pp. 2255-2256)

evidence.claim: The inversion and exon 3 deletion are separate variants, not one contiguous complex event. The paper concludes compound heterozygosity, but father DNA was unavailable and the local text does not document direct molecule-level trans phasing; recurrence of the full genotype therefore requires an explicit participant-level trans receipt.
evidence.citation: Analyst reconstruction from P3-P6 and P12; requires genetics review

evidence.claim: The HGVS-inclusive inversion interval contains 7,425,906 reference bases while the paper's stated 7,425,905 bp equals endpoint subtraction. Both representations must be retained rather than treated as conflicting breakpoints.
evidence.citation: Analyst arithmetic from P4

evidence.claim: Exact recurrence requires three synchronized windows and two levels of linkage: both inversion junctions as one event, then the inversion and exact deletion as a phased two-variant genotype. A different PRKN exon-overlapping inversion is a competing architecture, not recurrence.
evidence.citation: Analyst workflow reconstruction from P3-P12

evidence.claim: Independent NCBI NC_000006.12 and Ensembl GRCh38 201 bp sequence requests agreed exactly at all four printed genomic boundaries, supporting direct GRCh38 routing without liftover.
evidence.citation: Read-only NCBI EFetch and Ensembl REST checks, 2026-08-11; hashes in evidence markdown

evidence.claim: The deployed browser returned HTTP 200 for three exact-event windows, but returned 404 for the PRKN workflow-detail route and paper PDF. Route 200 proves navigation only.
evidence.citation: Read-only deployed route checks, 2026-08-11

evidence.claim: The live API returned 1,634, 2,492, and 1,034 records in the inversion-PRKN, exon-deletion, and distal-inversion windows, respectively, with no INV/BND/CTX/CPX record and no record at any exact paper boundary.

evidence.claim: The deletion window contained a 54,418 bp insertion call with AC=1/AN=2 and a 3,333 bp duplication call with AC=1/AN=584, but neither is the paper's exact 60,138 bp deletion or evidence of linked architecture.

paper.title: Short and long-read whole genome sequencing explains most undiagnosed Autosomal Dominant Polycystic Kidney Disease

archetypes: A7 — Deep intronic and regulatory variants

persona.role: Kidney-genetics variant scientist or clinical-research analyst
persona.context: Research prioritization of an externally detected PKD1 intronic allele after coding-focused testing was non-diagnostic or the allele was previously considered benign/uncertain

nonDiagnosticBoundary: This workflow can establish only whether the exact GRCh38 genomic allele is represented in a named population-reference release and whether a defensible allele-callable denominator exists. It cannot determine gene-versus-pseudogene origin for a patient's read, infer a branchpoint or splice effect, transfer the paper's RNA result to another person or allele, apply ACMG/AMP criteria, classify pathogenicity, estimate ADPKD risk, or diagnose anyone.

startingState.trigger: An externally detected PKD1 NM_001009944.3:c.11017-25A>G candidate from an ADPKD research case, with original assay/build and a request for bounded population-reference context before independent transcript review.
inputs: Paper case RBW403 and transcript allele NM_001009944.3:c.11017-25A>G; do not generalize from the other eight families
Original short-read alignment build hg37/GRCh37 and genomic bridge NC_000016.9:g.2143119T>C to NC_000016.10:g.2093118T>C on GRCh38
Reverse-strand normalization: transcript A>G corresponds to genomic-forward T>C; UCSC reference checks must show T on both assemblies
Source assay and PKD1-versus-pseudogene disambiguation evidence, including LR-PCR/Sanger when the assayed segment is homologous; coordinate placement alone is not origin evidence
A predeclared exact-match rule requiring chromosome, position, REF, ALT, reference assembly, source ALT index, filters, and accepted run identity
A predeclared callability rule requiring exact-locus SNV-callable chromosome-copy AN and no-call/missing counts; aggregate depth percentages are context, not AN

A separate external RNA evidence receipt covering tissue, PKD1-specific primer logic, RT-negative and healthy controls, amplicon identities, Sanger traces, natural exon-38 skipping baseline, and analyst sign-off
startingState.question: In each selected release, is GRCh38 chr16:2093118 T>C represented as the exact allele, and—only if exact-locus callability is validated—what bounded AC/AN and missingness can be reported before handing the case to independent transcript-evidence review?
startingState.stopRule: If build/strand/REF/ALT identity, PKD1 source assignment where relevant, accepted release provenance, or exact-locus allele callability is unresolved, stop before any rarity or not-observed claim. A browser annotation or population count never establishes splice effect or pathogenicity.

before: Freeze the selected case only: RBW403, NM_001009944.3:c.11017-25A>G. Retain that the study aligned short reads to hg37 and that the allele had been detected on earlier tests but was predicted benign by then-available tools.

Reconcile coordinates independently: ClinVar VCV001800458 maps the transcript allele to GRCh37 chr16:2143119 T>C and GRCh38 chr16:2093118 T>C; verify a T reference base on both assemblies and retain the transcript/genomic reverse-strand distinction.

Record the PKD1 pseudogene boundary explicitly. The paper describes six highly homologous pseudogenes and uses LR-PCR before Sanger only when a variant lies in the homologous region; its RNA protocol requires at least one PKD1-unique primer pair when relevant. Do not claim the browser establishes patient gene-versus-pseudogene origin, and do not imply this intron-37 case was a long-read rescue.

Define exact occurrence and callability before looking: exact GRCh38 chromosome/position/REF/ALT plus accepted source identity; for non-observation, independently validated SNV-callable chromosome copies and no-call counts at the same base.
inside: Open the manifest's 56,628 bp PKD1 overview and then focus on chr16:2093018–2093218. Verify GRCh38, cohort, database, release, chr16 run, scope, acceptance state, and separate primary-versus-coverage run identities.
Search the genomic-forward allele as chr16:2093118 T>C or canonical small-variant ID, not as transcript A>G. Require exact position and alleles; nearby intronic SNVs are non-matches.

If an exact row exists, inspect source_variant_id, alt_index, filters, AC/AN/AF, genotype fields, population denominators, and provenance. Keep HGSVC/HPRC and aggregate-only AoU results separate; never use AoU for carrier, haplotype, or sample-origin claims.

If no exact row exists, inspect locus coverage only as QC context. Do not convert over-1×/5×/10× percentages or AN from a nearby variant into target AN. Require an independently admitted exact-locus callability/no-call receipt before saying not observed.

Treat major_consequence, transcript consequence, branchpoint labels, or generic intronic placement as annotations only. The browser has no case RT-PCR/Sanger evidence and must not infer aberrant splicing.
after: Assign one result: exact allele observed with record-specific counts; exact allele not observed among N independently validated callable chromosome copies; nearby/non-matching allele only; or population inference data blocked.

Export the genomic/transcript normalization, exact query, cohort/release/database/run/scope/status, source record and ALT index, filters, AC/AN/missingness, coverage context and its separate run, timestamp, browser state, and match/callability rule versions.

Hand the population receipt—not a classification—to an independent transcript-evidence workflow. That review must evaluate the paper-cited branchpoint prediction, predominant exon-38 skipping, lower-level 180 bp intron-37 retention, approximately 5% natural exon-38 skipping in control kidney GTEx data, assay controls, and PKD1-specific amplification provenance.
Keep RNA interpretation, segregation/phenotype review, ACMG/AMP application, classification, diagnosis, counselling, and patient management outside the browser.

branches.condition: The input is only NM_001009944.3:c.11017-25A>G and no build/strand/genomic reconciliation receipt exists
branches.action: Do not search a guessed genomic allele; obtain a reviewed transcript-to-genome bridge and reference-base check.

branches.condition: GRCh37 chr16:2143119 T>C, GRCh38 chr16:2093118 T>C, or the reference T base does not reconcile
branches.action: Report coordinate/allele mismatch and stop; never substitute a nearby intron-37 allele.

branches.condition: The case assay lies in a PKD1-pseudogene-homologous segment but PKD1-specific source assignment is absent
branches.action: Report gene-versus-pseudogene origin unresolved and require orthogonal PKD1-specific validation; an aligned browser coordinate is insufficient.

branches.condition: An exact chr16:2093118 T>C record is returned from an accepted run and identity, ALT index, and filters reconcile
branches.action: Report exact allele observed with record-specific global and stratum AC/AN/AF, missing fields, and provenance. Do not label it benign, pathogenic, splice-altering, or equivalent to the case's RNA phenotype.

branches.condition: Only a nearby position, T>C at another base, another ALT at 2093118, or transcript A>G searched in genomic-forward space is returned
branches.action: Report non-match; do not borrow its AN, frequency, annotation, carriers, or haplotypes for the target.

branches.condition: No exact target row is returned and only aggregate depth-percentage coverage is available
branches.action: Report population inference data blocked. Coverage may be shown as context but is not exact-locus callable AN and does not establish AC=0.

branches.condition: No exact target row is returned but an independently validated exact-locus SNV-callability receipt supplies callable chromosome copies and no-call counts
branches.action: Report 'not observed among N allele-callable chromosome copies in release R' with missingness and uncertainty; make no splice or pathogenicity inference.

branches.condition: A population stratum has AN=0, an unvalidated denominator, or a denominator too small for a useful rarity claim
branches.action: Show the denominator and mark that stratum unavailable or uninformative; do not convert missingness into zero frequency.

branches.condition: The user requests AoU carriers, haplotypes, patient-level origin, or gene-versus-pseudogene phasing
branches.action: Refuse the request because AoU is aggregate-only; use no HGSVC/HPRC fallback for an AoU claim.

branches.condition: The browser displays an intronic/splice-region/transcript consequence or a population frequency
branches.action: Treat it as annotation or occurrence only and proceed to external transcript review; do not infer branchpoint disruption, exon skipping, intron retention, or pathogenicity.

branches.condition: The external RNA receipt reproduces the paper's blood RT-PCR/Sanger findings with appropriate controls and PKD1-specific amplification provenance
branches.action: Return that evidence to an independently governed expert interpretation process; do not write the RNA conclusion back as a browser-derived result.

branches.condition: External RNA controls, amplicon identity, natural-splicing comparator, or required PKD1-specific primer evidence is incomplete
branches.action: Report transcript effect unresolved and request additional external evidence; population rarity cannot fill the gap.

branches.condition: A user asks the workflow to classify, diagnose, estimate penetrance/risk, or recommend management
branches.action: Refuse that inference and identify the independent clinical and transcript-evidence review required.

story.given: RBW403's externally detected PKD1 NM_001009944.3:c.11017-25A>G allele, a reviewed reverse-strand bridge to GRCh38 chr16:2093118 T>C, source-assignment provenance, and a predeclared exact-locus callability rule

paper.title: Improved structural variant interpretation for hereditary cancer susceptibility using long-read sequencing

locus: IFT140/TSC2 · paper GRCh37 NC_000016.9:g.1566535_1566536ins2119755_2119863inv; candidate GRCh38 NC_000016.10:g.1516534_1516535ins2069754_2069862inv (no CTA; exact event receipt gated)

persona.role: Hereditary-cancer structural-variation researcher or laboratory scientist
persona.context: Research follow-up after short-read genome sequencing reports a recurrent, apparently gene-disrupting long-range inversion across IFT140 and TSC2

nonDiagnosticBoundary: This workflow may distinguish a false long-range inversion call from a sequence-resolved intronic insertion architecture and describe comparable population-reference records with qualified callability. It cannot apply BS2 or any ACMG/AMP criterion, classify an individual's SV, infer benignity/pathogenicity or cancer risk, diagnose tuberous sclerosis, or recommend/refuse clinical referral. Population occurrence alone must never reclassify an SV.

startingState.trigger: A short-read call represented as GRCh37 NC_000016.9:g.1566535_2119866inv, supported by paired reads, split reads, and contigs and initially interpreted as a potentially pathogenic IFT140–TSC2 long-range inversion.
inputs: Original GRCh37/NC_000016.9 pre-LR call, caller outputs, evidence types, confidence intervals, tissue, and uncertainty
Paper-resolved GRCh37 event NC_000016.9:g.1566535_1566536ins2119755_2119863inv: a reverse-oriented Alu-derived segment from TSC2 intron 16 inserted into IFT140 intron 30
Breakpoint-spanning long reads or an orthogonal altered-junction sequence; the main PDF's schematic and HGVS alone do not replace the unavailable supplementary alignment evidence
Event-aware GRCh37→GRCh38 receipt with target and donor flanks, altered junction, orientation, reference accessions, chain/tool version, and sequence hashes
A declared match tier: exact linked architecture, sequence-compatible candidate, generic overlap, false long-inversion representation, non-match, bounded not observed, or data blocked
Architecture-specific callable and missing chromosome-copy counts; ordinary nearby depth or a candidate row's AN is insufficient
Case phenotype, unsuccessful PCR, tumor LOH, and expert classification evidence retained as external review inputs, not browser-derived facts
startingState.question: Does a selected population-reference release contain the same linked architecture—an equivalent reverse-oriented TSC2-intron-16 Alu segment inserted at the IFT140-intron-30 target—not merely an overlapping inversion or nearby Alu-like insertion—and what chromosome copies were callable for that complete architecture?
startingState.stopRule: The local supplement and machine-readable altered-junction sequence are unavailable, and current data cannot prove target, donor interval, reverse orientation, and same-event/copy linkage. Preserve unmapped/data-blocked status, emit no browser CTA, and do not claim exact recurrence, absence, or clinical classification until those gates are satisfied.

before: Preserve two distinct objects: the pre-LR GRCh37 long-inversion hypothesis NC_000016.9:g.1566535_2119866inv and the long-read-resolved insertion NC_000016.9:g.1566535_1566536ins2119755_2119863inv. Never rewrite the former as if short reads had observed the latter.

Normalize the resolved event as target breakpoint + donor interval + reverse orientation + inserted sequence + same-event/copy linkage. Record that three unrelated paper cases shared the short-read miscall, while the authors' likely-benign classification also used case-specific phenotype and expert-review evidence.

Retain the candidate GRCh38 notation NC_000016.10:g.1516534_1516535ins2069754_2069862inv only as a reference-context-supported remap. Require the unavailable altered-junction/supplement evidence before publishing an exact event overlay or CTA.

Define exact equivalence before querying: sequence-compatible target junction, equivalent reverse-complement donor segment, orientation, inserted structure, and linkage on one chromosome copy. Nearby insertion, Alu homology, interval overlap, or shared gene labels are candidates only.
inside: After the remap gate is satisfied, open linked target and donor windows and attest GRCh38, cohort, release, database, chromosome scope, accepted run, caller, and source representation before inspecting occurrence.

Search the target insertion and donor segment as one architecture. Compare raw and normalization-equivalent breakpoints, inserted sequence, length, reverse orientation, source IDs/ALT indexes, and same-copy linkage; current range terms are OR and cannot prove a linked event.

Treat live record chr16-1516498-INS-133~1 as a sequence-compatible candidate only: after a 36-bp right rotation to the paper target its 133-bp insert contains the complete expected 109-bp reverse donor sequence, but retains 3-bp and 21-bp extra flanks and lacks explicit donor/orientation/linkage fields.

For any exact architecture, report AC only against chromosome copies callable across target, donor, orientation, and complete insertion representation, with no-call, one-end-only, unresolved-orientation, and representation-mismatch counts. AoU remains aggregate-only and cannot support carrier or haplotype claims.
after: Assign one bounded result tier and export original and normalized coordinates, altered-junction/remap receipt, both windows, sequence/orientation/linkage evidence, source IDs, AC/AN/missingness, cohort/release/run/database/scope, query state, rule version, and timestamp.

Hand the receipt, the original short-read evidence, orthogonal long-read/PCR evidence, phenotype and tumor evidence, and uncertainty to an independent expert clinical review process. The browser does not reproduce or automate the paper's likely-benign classification.

Use only descriptive wording: comparable linked architecture observed; sequence-compatible candidate; false long-inversion representation; not observed among N architecture-callable copies; or data blocked.

branches.condition: The altered-junction sequence or decisive supplementary breakpoint evidence is unavailable
branches.action: Keep the record unmapped/data-blocked, show the paper coordinates and candidate remap as text only, and emit no browser CTA or exact-event overlay.

branches.condition: Only the original long-range inversion representation is returned
branches.action: Label it the pre-LR hypothesis/possible recurrent short-read artifact and require orthogonal sequence resolution; do not infer the insertion architecture or clinical class.

branches.condition: A nearby insertion contains Alu-like sequence but target, complete donor interval, orientation, or same-event/copy linkage differs or is unavailable
branches.action: Report sequence-compatible candidate or generic overlap. Keep its occurrence and row-level AN separate from exact-architecture recurrence and callability.

branches.condition: Both junctions, complete inserted sequence, reverse donor orientation, and same-event/copy linkage are sequence equivalent under a validated remap
branches.action: Report comparable linked architecture observed with architecture-callable AC/AN and provenance, then hand off externally; never label it benign or apply BS2.

branches.condition: No exact event is returned and architecture-specific callability is unavailable
branches.action: Report data blocked, not AC=0, absent, rare, or evidence for pathogenicity.

branches.condition: No exact event is found among independently validated representation-complete callable chromosome copies
branches.action: Report a bounded not-observed result with denominator and uncertainty; do not infer pathogenicity or modify classification.

branches.condition: Population occurrence is present, including the same candidate source record in more than one cohort
branches.action: Report cohort-specific occurrence and callability only. Population occurrence alone must not reclassify the SV or substitute for phenotype, segregation, orthogonal validation, or expert review.

capabilities.evidence: HGSVC/HPRC supports haplotype/carrier views for representable records, but no exact architecture is established; AoU is summary-only and carrier claims are unavailable.

capabilities.evidence: Current variant exports do not preserve the pre-LR call, target–donor sequence relation, altered-junction/remap receipt, linked-window state, architecture-specific missingness, or external-review handoff.

capabilities.step: Use population occurrence to apply BS2, classify the SV, infer cancer risk, or make a referral decision
capabilities.evidence: The paper's conclusion combined long-read architecture with case-specific phenotype and expert review. Cohort occurrence alone cannot reproduce that process or establish benignity.

acceptanceTest.fixture: Six fixtures: (1) the paper's GRCh37 false long inversion; (2) an exact GRCh38 target insertion with complete 109-bp reverse donor sequence, both junctions, orientation and same-copy linkage; (3) the live 133-bp left-shifted sequence-compatible candidate; (4) a generic nearby Alu insertion; (5) a one-end-only record; and (6) callable and uncallable chromosome copies with no exact event.
acceptanceTest.actions: Attempt navigation without the supplement/altered-junction receipt; add a validated event-aware remap; compare target, donor, sequence, length, orientation and linkage; inspect HGSVC/HPRC and AoU counts; request an absence statement and classification; export for external review.
acceptanceTest.expected: Without the receipt, the page remains unmapped/data-blocked and emits no CTA. Fixture 1 remains the pre-LR hypothesis. Fixture 2 alone reaches exact architecture. Fixture 3 is labelled sequence-compatible candidate with its 133/109-bp and 36-bp-shift discrepancy; fixtures 4–5 remain generic/partial. Fixture 6 separates not observed from not callable. Cohort-specific AC/AN and missingness are shown without cross-cohort carrier claims, and the export ends in an external-review handoff.
acceptanceTest.forbidden: The result must not equate an Alu-like sequence or interval overlap with exact architecture, treat row-level AN as architecture callability, report AC=0 when data are blocked, emit a region CTA while the remap is gated, call any event benign/pathogenic, apply BS2 or other ACMG/AMP criteria, infer cancer/tuberous-sclerosis risk, or make a patient/referral decision.

paper.title: Robust Detection of Somatic Mosaicism and Repeat Interruptions by Long-Read Targeted Sequencing in Myotonic Dystrophy Type 1

locus: DMPK DM1 repeat · exact current source event GRCh38 chr19:45,770,204–45,770,264 (`chr19-45770204-TRV-60`); source-forward CAG is the reverse-complement orientation of the paper's CTG

persona.role: Repeat-expansion researcher or laboratory scientist
persona.context: Population-reference comparison after an externally characterized DMPK allele, with assay-labelled repeat size, interruption structure, tissue, and—when measured—a per-molecule distribution

nonDiagnosticBoundary: This workflow asks whether a comparable germline DMPK sequence or repeat-count state is represented in a named population-reference source. It cannot diagnose DM1, classify an allele, estimate prognosis or age of onset, or reproduce a blood, trophoblast, muscle, or other tissue's somatic mosaic distribution from a germline VCF.

startingState.trigger: An external DMPK result or paper comparator with a repeat count or distribution and, when available, full interruption sequence.
inputs: Both externally reported alleles, original build/coordinates, CTG/CAG strand orientation, assay, tissue, collection time, and uncertainty
Raw assay outputs kept distinct: conventional PCR/TP-PCR/Sanger, Southern or small-pool measurements, and long-read per-molecule counts, modes, maxima, read depth, and filters
Ordered repeat structure when known, including pure CTG, single CAG, CCG, and CCGCTG units rather than a purity label alone
A predeclared comparison tier: exact represented sequence, ordered interruption structure, repeat-count similarity, or signed ALT-minus-REF length only
Cohort-specific source availability, source event and ALT identity, callable AC/AN, strata, expected roster when available, missing/no-call accounting, release/run, and query receipt
For the paper's stable comparator, retain 5′-(CTG)6(CCGCTG)13(CTG)5-3′; do not replace it with the number 37
startingState.question: Does an available population source contain the exact represented DMPK sequence, a weaker ordered-structure or repeat-count match, or no interpretable match, and which questions remain unavailable because the only current event source is aggregate AoU?
startingState.stopRule: Stop exact comparison when build, represented span, orientation, or sequence is missing. Stop chromosome-copy, carrier, phase, or haplotype comparison when only AoU is available. Stop an absence claim unless event-series completeness, callable AN, reference/no-call accounting, and the exact matching rule are explicit. Never substitute a germline VCF distribution for a tissue somatic distribution.

before: Record the external result without collapsing inherited/germline allele state and tissue-specific molecule distribution: preserve assay, tissue, age/time, read filters, every reported mode or range, maximum, and ordered interruption sequence.

Normalize the DMPK locus to exact GRCh38 source event chr19-45770204-TRV-60 while retaining the paper's CTG notation. Reverse-complement the full ordered sequence for source-forward comparison; CCG becomes CGG and order reverses, so motif-name substitution alone is insufficient.

Declare the comparison tier before viewing the population data. Exact byte sequence over the same span is strongest; a validated ordered motif decomposition is weaker; repeat count is weaker again; signed ALT-minus-REF base-pair difference is not a repeat count.
Treat the paper's patient and family distributions as assay/tissue comparators, not population thresholds or labels.
inside: Check source availability before interpreting a blank result. The current HGSVC/HPRC chr19 source and haplotypes are available globally but return no chr19-45770204-TRV-60 row; select AoU for the current event and label it summary-only.

Open chr19:45,766,131–45,786,131 in AoU, verify accepted Y1 GRCh38 chr19 provenance, and group every ALT under source event chr19-45770204-TRV-60 rather than treating ALT-suffixed rows as independent loci.

Compare exact source-forward ALT sequence first. Report ordered CAG/CGG interruption structure only when a validated decomposition exists; otherwise keep exact sequence, ancillary CAG repeat count, and signed length as separate observables.

Inspect the aggregate allele-size and biallelic genotype histograms with their source labels and units. They describe germline population-reference counts, not named chromosome copies, carriers, phase, or tissue molecule distributions.
Compare the stable 37-unit sequence and the E-family interrupted structures as explicit branches. A 37-count bin or equal-length ALT is not an exact match to (CTG)6(CCGCTG)13(CTG)5.

For every observation show cohort, event/ALT ID, matching rule, AC/AN and strata, missing or unavailable status, exact release/run, and query date. Do not silently derive a reference count or no-call count from summed ALT AC.
after: Return one bounded outcome: exact aggregate sequence observed; ordered-structure match observed; repeat-count-only similarity; signed-length-only similarity; not observed in representation-complete callable aggregate data; or source/representation/callability blocked.

State tissue somatic distribution unavailable as a separate result whenever the starting artifact includes per-molecule mosaicism; retain the external distribution in the export without presenting it as browser-derived.

Export original and normalized coordinates, strand transform, common comparison span, exact sequence or weaker rule, event/ALT IDs, AC/AN and missingness, source availability, histogram units, release/run, and the explicit germline-versus-tissue limitation.
Hand off for orthogonal sizing/sequencing, multi-tissue or longitudinal testing, segregation, phenotype review, and interpretation outside the population browser.

branches.condition: The HGSVC/HPRC region is reachable but chr19-45770204-TRV-60 is not returned
branches.action: Report the event as unavailable in HGSVC/HPRC and switch explicitly to AoU aggregate data; do not report zero frequency or infer non-carriage in HGSVC/HPRC.

branches.condition: AoU is the selected source
branches.action: Allow aggregate event ALTs and allele/genotype histograms, but disable carrier, chromosome-copy, phase, haplotype, sample-metadata, and tissue-mosaic claims.

branches.condition: An exact source-forward ALT sequence matches over the same represented span with explicit AC/AN
branches.action: Report aggregate population-reference occurrence with event/ALT identity and provenance only; do not infer DM1 status, stability, or tissue behavior.

branches.condition: A repeat count or signed length is similar but ordered CCG/CTG structure is missing or different
branches.action: Report repeat-count-only or signed-length-only similarity and label exact structural equivalence data-blocked.

branches.condition: No exact match is returned but the full event series, reference state, expected roster, or no-call accounting is not explicit
branches.action: Report source/representation/callability blocked, never absent or zero.

branches.condition: No exact match is observed in a representation-complete callable event series
branches.action: Report not observed with the exact sequence rule, callable AN, missing/no-call count, cohort, and release; this is not evidence of pathogenicity or penetrance.

branches.condition: The external artifact contains a broad, bimodal, longitudinal, or tissue-specific molecule distribution
branches.action: Preserve that distribution as external evidence and return tissue somatic distribution unavailable from germline population VCF; request matched-tissue single-molecule evidence for that question.

branches.condition: The external allele lies above the current population event's observed repeat-count ceiling
branches.action: Report outside the checked source's observed range with source and denominator, not absent from humans, diagnostic, or pathogenic.

story.then: the browser returns an exact aggregate sequence, weaker structure/count/length similarity, safe not-observed result, or blocked result with provenance, while explicitly stating that AoU supplies no carriers or haplotypes and that a germline VCF cannot reproduce tissue somatic mosaicism

All rows had AN 2052; ALT AC summed to 2042, but reference-copy and no-call counts are not first-class event fields and must not be silently derived.

capabilities.evidence: The paper is a selected clinical/family assay study, its distributions are tissue- and age-dependent, and its amplicon method is biased toward smaller repeats. Population occurrence or non-observation cannot transfer those outcomes.

acceptanceTest.fixture: A source-aware DMPK fixture with (a) accepted HGSVC/HPRC chr19 data but no chr19-45770204-TRV-60 event, (b) an AoU summary-only event containing an exact stable-37 sequence, a same-count pure allele, a CCG-interrupted allele, a no-call/reference-accounting gap, and aggregate allele/genotype histograms, and (c) an external blood/trophoblast per-molecule distribution with two modes; include no diagnosis or prognosis fields.
acceptanceTest.actions: Open the workflow and exact GRCh38 window; verify HGSVC/HPRC event absence without calling zero; select AoU; verify accepted run and summary-only status; group all source-event ALTs; declare span and strand transform; compare exact ordered sequence before repeat count and signed length; inspect AC/AN, histogram units, reference/no-call receipt, and export/reload state.
acceptanceTest.expected: The CTA selects or requests AoU rather than silently opening an empty HGSVC/HPRC haplotype view; one grouped event is shown; exact stable-37, same-count/different-structure, interrupted, reference/no-call, and external tissue-mosaic states remain distinct; every population observation has event/ALT ID, rule, AC/AN, source, release/run, and missingness; no carrier IDs appear for AoU; export/reload reproduces all values and preserves the external distribution as non-browser evidence; absence fails closed when completeness is missing.
acceptanceTest.forbidden: The result must not diagnose DM1, label an allele pathogenic, benign, stable, protective, or prognostic, convert HGSVC/HPRC event unavailability to zero, invent AoU carriers or haplotypes, treat signed base-pair length as a CTG count, equate a 37-count bin with (CTG)6(CCGCTG)13(CTG)5, substitute a germline population histogram for a tissue somatic distribution, or turn incomplete representation/callability into absence.

evidence.claim: Table 1 reports expanded-repeat modes/maxima of E1 447/1099, E2.1 383/831, E3 bimodal 173 and 215/478, L2 957/2138, L3 1156/2081, A4.1 109/245, 1201 118/619, B2 292/802, and 5289 185/896 CTG repeats; 9994–10,000 reads per sample were analyzed and 82–96% of analyzed reads were expanded alleles.
evidence.citation: Local PDF pp. 3–6, Table 1 and Figs. 4–7

evidence.claim: Family E showed a pure E1 expansion, E2.1 with a major 3′ structure (CTG)n(CCGCTG)(CTG)7(CCGCTG)(CTG)11 and two or three CCG interruptions across blood cells, and E3 with six CCG interruptions plus a bimodal 173/215 distribution; the authors interpreted the E2.1/E3 interruptions as de novo across paternal transmissions and associated them with stabilization/contraction in this family.
evidence.citation: Local PDF pp. 3, 6, 12–13; Table 1 and Table 3

evidence.claim: A4.1 carried one CAG interruption and B2 three CCG interruptions; their somatic mosaicism was lower than the respective pure-repeat comparators 1201 and 5289 in this selected comparison. L2 and L3 had pure repeats, modes above 900, maxima above 2000, and high mosaicism.
evidence.citation: Local PDF pp. 4–6, 9–10, 12; Table 1 and Figs. 6–7

evidence.claim: Seven G37 family members carried the stably transmitted 37-unit sequence 5′-(CTG)6(CCGCTG)13(CTG)5-3′, associated with the paper's DMPK haplotype A; the paper treated it as a stable comparator and not a DM1 expansion in that family.
evidence.citation: Local PDF pp. 10–12 and 18; Fig. 8 and Table 2

evidence.claim: The paper cites interrupted expanded alleles in 3–8% of the non-African DM1 population and emphasizes wide variation in interruption number, type, position, and family context; that cited percentage is not a frequency measured by this study's selected families.
evidence.citation: Local PDF pp. 2 and 18; cited literature summarized in Table 3

evidence.claim: The Sequel II assay was PCR-amplicon targeted sequencing from blood or trophoblast DNA, with preferential amplification of smaller repeats acknowledged as an inherent ceiling. Libraries used a 25-hour movie; CCS reads required at least three passes and mean QV20. The authors demonstrated reads to roughly 2000 CTG and a maximum of 2138, not an unlimited assay range or a multi-tissue distribution.
evidence.citation: Local PDF pp. 18–21; Methods 4.2–4.5 and Table 4

evidence.claim: A faithful population workflow must keep exact sequence, ordered interruption structure, repeat count, signed length, and tissue molecule distribution as separate comparison tiers. Full reverse-complement normalization is required because source-forward CAG reverses both the paper's CTG/CCG motifs and their order.
evidence.citation: Analyst reconstruction from paper structures and exact source REF/ALT; requires sequence-review approval

evidence.claim: The result unit is aggregate callable chromosome copies for AoU ALT AC/AN, not a named chromosome copy. HGSVC/HPRC event unavailability and AoU summary-only availability must be explicit branches; neither is equivalent to biological absence.
evidence.citation: Analyst reconstruction from source contracts and live cohort-specific API provenance

evidence.claim: A tissue somatic distribution can only be preserved as an external input in this workflow. A germline VCF allele/genotype histogram cannot reproduce per-cell or per-molecule blood/trophoblast distributions, their modes/maxima, tissue differences, age effects, or longitudinal instability.
evidence.citation: Analyst reconstruction from paper Methods/Discussion and current Y1 data semantics

paper.title: Concordance of whole-genome long-read sequencing with standard clinical testing for Prader-Willi and Angelman syndromes

locus: GRCh38 chromosome 15 imprinting region. The paper's one-page overview spans chr15:20,000,000–33,000,000; its SNURF-SNRPN-to-UBE3A phase interval is chr15:24,821,608–25,441,024; UBE3A is printed as chr15:25,333,728–25,439,056. The parent-of-origin anchor includes SNURF-SNRPN cpg.7735, printed at chr15:24,878,211–24,878,560, while UBE3A cpg.7736 is chr15:25,438,474–25,439,046.

persona.role: Imprinting-disorder researcher, molecular laboratory scientist, or long-read methods evaluator
persona.context: Research follow-up after external methylation, dosage, UPD, sequence, and phase assays have produced a candidate multimodal state at 15q11.2–q13; the browser is used only to ask whether comparable, fully qualified states are represented in a population-reference release

nonDiagnosticBoundary: This workflow can compare provenance-qualified population-reference methylation, copy-number/structural, sequence, and phase evidence and report whether a comparable linked state is represented, not observed in explicitly callable units, or data-blocked. It cannot analyze a patient, diagnose Angelman or Prader-Willi syndrome, assign pathogenicity or benignity, establish UPD or an imprinting defect, substitute for clinical testing, or call browser copy A/B maternal or paternal.

startingState.trigger: An external 15q11.2–q13 research result in which methylation, dosage/SV, SNV/indel, UPD pattern, or parent-of-origin is being reconciled rather than inferred from one modality.
inputs: Original reference build and accession, coordinate convention, assay/tissue/extraction, sequencing platform, caller/version, batch, depth and callability for every modality
Exact methylation interval(s), per-CpG values and coverage, control-panel definition, DMR rule, and whether evidence is sample-total, source-haplotype, phase-linked, or same-read/same-molecule
Exact CNV/SV boundaries, representation, copy state, breakpoint or depth support, and whether components are linked as one event
Exact SNV/indel genomic identity and normalization, transcript/HGVS if available, genotype support, phase set or molecule evidence, and callable denominator
For UPD claims, chromosome-wide heterozygous/homozygous marker pattern, copy-neutral evidence, informative parental or validated inheritance evidence where required, and segment boundaries

For maternal/paternal wording, an explicit parent-of-origin receipt from informative trio/segregation evidence or a validated locus-specific methylation-to-phase rule joined to the same chromosome copy; browser A/B, HAP1/HAP2, or GT1/GT2 labels are insufficient
HGSVC/HPRC release/database/run identities, the complete 292-person roster state, per-modality source-present/no-output/skip status, and the hash-bound methylation orientation receipt
A synchronized multi-window receipt spanning the SNURF-SNRPN DMR, the complete UBE3A allele, and every CNV/SV or UPD segment used in the comparison
startingState.question: Does the population release contain a comparable joint 15q11.2–q13 state in which methylation, copy/SV, sequence, and parent-of-origin evidence are valid at their declared linkage levels, and what remains discordant or unanswerable?
startingState.stopRule: Stop imprinting or parent-of-origin attribution if methylation is sample-total, if A/B is the only copy label, if the orientation receipt is stale, or if the UBE3A allele and SNURF-SNRPN methylation lack a continuous validated phase/molecule link. Stop exact event comparison when build, variant identity, boundaries, linkage, or modality-specific callability is missing. Stop navigation at the current approximate index interval because it truncates UBE3A, excludes the printed UBE3A CpG island, and cannot include SNURF-SNRPN. Never turn a population observation into a diagnosis or classification.

before: Preserve the external evidence as separate modality records. Record GRCh38 or an auditable remap; exact DMR/CpG intervals and controls; CNV/SV boundaries and representation; SNV/indel identity; chromosome-wide UPD markers; phase blocks; parental evidence; tissue/caller/batch; callable/no-call units; and uncertainty.

Classify linkage before looking at browser data: sample-total < source-labelled HAP1/HAP2 < hash-receipted VCF copy < one validated phase block < same-read/same-molecule. Record parent-of-origin as a separate field that remains unknown unless independently established.

Reject the index CTA chr15:25,336,390–25,436,390. Relative to Table 2 it omits 2,662 bp at each end of UBE3A, entirely misses cpg.7736 at chr15:25,438,474–25,439,046, and is about 458 kb from the distal edge of the printed SNURF-SNRPN cpg.7735 interval.

Use a gated synchronized design, not one region: a bounded SNURF-SNRPN DMR view, one or more UBE3A views sufficient for the exact allele and cpg.7736, and event-specific CNV/SV or UPD views. Require all panels to share GRCh38, cohort, accepted primary run, methylation source run, roster and receipt identity.
inside: Verify accepted chr15 primary and haplotype provenance, methylation source identity, sample availability, orientation-receipt hash, mapping scope, region limits and missingness before displaying any cross-modality interpretation.
Keep sample-total methylation in a separate lane. It may support only a sample-level profile and must never be copied onto A/B, used to choose a parent, or joined to a sequence allele.

Show receipt-qualified per-copy CpGs only when joined capability is AVAILABLE_CONFIRMED for the exact chromosome/run/receipt. Retain source HAP1/HAP2 and VCF strand; label canonical A/B as arbitrary chromosome copies with no maternal/paternal meaning.

Inspect the exact normalized UBE3A SNV/indel and every CNV/SV constituent with source/ALT identity, genotype, filters, AC/AN, no-call state and accepted-run provenance. A nearby allele, broad deletion overlap, or a depth change without exact boundaries is candidate evidence only.

For a UBE3A-to-SNURF-SNRPN linkage claim, require one continuous validated phase block or same-molecule evidence spanning the exact allele and the methylation anchor. A chromosome-wide HAP1-to-GT1 operator mapping with null phase_set does not prove that link.

For parent-of-origin wording, require the linked copy plus informative parental/segregation evidence or a prevalidated imprinting-anchor rule with assay/control and tissue provenance. Display maternal/paternal separately from A/B; never derive it from A/B ordering.

Classify the joint state as exact comparable, modality-concordant but parent-of-origin unresolved, copy/SV-only, sequence-only, sample-total methylation-only, discordant, not observed in fully callable matched data, or data/provenance blocked. Preserve every discordance rather than forcing a syndrome label.

Audit modality-specific denominators. The unit for a linked state is a chromosome copy callable for the exact sequence/event, required CpGs, phase span and copy/UPD evidence; participant N, one row's AN, average depth, and up to 230 sample-total observations at one CpG are not substitutes.
after: Export paper and browser coordinates; every source variant/ALT and event component; CpGs, methylation and coverage; sample-total versus copy/phase/molecule level; A/B, HAP and GT labels; parent-of-origin evidence; CNV/SV and UPD rules; callable/no-call counts; all database/release/run/receipt identities; synchronized windows; filters; timestamp; classification tier; discordances; and safety wording.

Hand the bounded population-reference result to independent molecular and clinical experts for orthogonal methylation, dosage/SV, sequence, parental/segregation and phenotype review outside the browser.

branches.condition: Only sample-total methylation is available
branches.action: Report a sample-level methylation profile only; disable imprinting attribution, same-copy sequence linkage and maternal/paternal wording.

branches.condition: Source HAP1/HAP2 exists but the orientation receipt is absent, stale, excluded, or tied to another primary run
branches.action: Keep source haplotypes separate from VCF strands and A/B; stop every sequence–methylation join.

branches.condition: The orientation receipt is valid but phase_set and molecule identifiers are absent
branches.action: Report receipt-qualified chromosome-copy co-display only. State explicitly that long-range UBE3A–SNURF-SNRPN linkage and parent of origin are not demonstrated.

branches.condition: An exact UBE3A allele and SNURF-SNRPN methylation share a validated continuous phase block, but no valid parental or imprinting-anchor receipt is present
branches.action: Report phase-linked same-copy evidence with A/B-neutral wording; parent of origin remains unknown.

branches.condition: The exact allele, DMR CpGs and a validated parent-of-origin anchor are joined on the same callable chromosome copy
branches.action: Report a parent-of-origin-qualified comparable population-reference state with the full evidence receipt; do not diagnose or classify it.

branches.condition: A CNV/SV and methylation state are individually represented but their event/copy linkage is missing
branches.action: Report co-display or candidate concordance only and identify the missing event/copy link.

branches.condition: Copy-neutral methylation difference is present but chromosome-wide SNV/indel and parental evidence cannot distinguish heterodisomy, isodisomy, mixed UPD, or epimutation
branches.action: Report mechanism unresolved/data-blocked; do not call UPD or an imprinting defect.

branches.condition: Methylation, copy/SV, SNV or phase evidence disagree
branches.action: Preserve a discordant multimodal state, list each assay and missingness reason, and hand off for orthogonal review; do not force one categorical answer.

branches.condition: No comparable linked state is returned and every required modality, representation, copy and phase span is callable under matched provenance
branches.action: Report not observed in N fully callable chromosome copies, with per-modality no-call counts and a conditional population-reference statement only.

branches.condition: No row is returned but any DMR, exact allele, CNV/SV representation, phase span, parent anchor, or callable denominator is incomplete
branches.action: Report data-blocked, not normal, absent, reference, benign, or AC=0.

branches.condition: A user asks for an AS/PWS diagnosis, pathogenicity classification, recurrence risk, or clinical recommendation
branches.action: Refuse the inference and provide only the reproducible population-reference evidence handoff.

story.given: an external GRCh38 15q11.2–q13 evidence package containing exact DMR CpGs and controls, copy/SV state, an exact UBE3A sequence allele or chromosome-wide UPD markers, declared linkage strength, parental evidence, assay provenance and callable/no-call units
story.when: the researcher opens synchronized SNURF-SNRPN, UBE3A and event-specific views under one accepted chr15 state; separates sample-total from per-copy methylation; verifies the orientation receipt; requires a continuous phase/molecule link and an independent parent-of-origin anchor; and audits multimodal denominators and discordances
story.then: the browser returns an exact parent-of-origin-qualified comparable state, same-copy but parent-unknown state, modality-only/candidate state, discordant state, not observed in N fully callable copies, or data-blocked, with a reproducible receipt and no diagnosis, pathogenicity or benignity claim

browserRegionBlockedReason: No single honest CTA exists. The index interval chr15:25,336,390–25,436,390 truncates both ends of the paper's UBE3A interval, misses the printed UBE3A cpg.7736, and excludes the SNURF-SNRPN parent-of-origin DMR. The paper's explicit UBE3A–SNURF-SNRPN phase interval spans 619,417 bp, above the current joined-methylation 100 kb limit, while the one-page CNV/UPD overview spans 13 Mb. Current LiteratureWorkflow supports one region or a blocked state and has no synchronized multi-window/long-range phase receipt.

capabilities.step: Navigate independently to bounded SNURF-SNRPN and UBE3A GRCh38 windows with accepted chr15 provenance
capabilities.evidence: On 2026-08-11 deployed 80 kb SNURF-SNRPN and 50 kb UBE3A routes returned HTTP 200. API queries returned 3,018 and 1,228 primary records, respectively, from accepted full-chromosome chr15 run y1-full-prototype-hgsvc-hprc-chr15-20260728-r1. Independent routability is not a linked workflow.

capabilities.step: Use one region CTA for the paper's multimodal state
capabilities.evidence: The index's 100 kb interval misses required paper evidence; the 619,417 bp phase interval and 13 Mb CNV/UPD overview exceed current joined-methylation limits, and the detail schema carries only one browserRegion.

capabilities.step: Inspect sample-total methylation at printed SNURF-SNRPN and UBE3A CpG intervals
capabilities.evidence: Live sample-total queries returned 37 CpGs at cpg.7734/7735's printed interval (per-CpG n=143–230) and 82 CpGs at cpg.7736 (per-CpG n=229–230). These are sample-level population summaries and cannot support imprinting attribution.

capabilities.step: Display receipt-qualified per-copy methylation
capabilities.evidence: The live chr15 capability was AVAILABLE_CONFIRMED for 231 source-present samples with a 100 kb/25-sample limit. HG00097 returned 37 HAP1/GT1 plus 37 HAP2/GT2 CpGs at SNURF-SNRPN and 83 plus 83 at UBE3A; all phase_set values were null under a chromosome-wide operator mapping.

capabilities.step: Treat browser A/B, HAP1/HAP2, or GT1/GT2 as maternal/paternal
capabilities.evidence: Current GraphQL comments say VCF strand is not a biological haplotype label, and MethylationHelp.tsx says HAP, GT and canonical A/B labels have no maternal or paternal meaning.

capabilities.step: Prove that an exact UBE3A allele and SNURF-SNRPN methylation share one long phase block

acceptanceTest.fixture: A GRCh38 linked-region fixture set containing: (A) sample-total SNURF-SNRPN methylation only; (B) HAP1/HAP2 CpGs mapped to VCF strands by a valid orientation receipt but with null phase_set; (C) an exact UBE3A 3-bp indel and SNURF-SNRPN CpGs in one continuous validated phase block but no parent anchor; (D) the same state with informative trio/segregation or a validated methylation parent-of-origin receipt; (E) a linked 15q deletion with exact boundaries, depth/SV support and copy-specific methylation; (F) copy-neutral heterodisomy, isodisomy, mixed-UPD and epimutation-like marker patterns; (G) unlinked CNV/SV and methylation records; (H) explicit no-output/no-call samples; and (I) a representation-complete callable no-event state. Include a stale orientation receipt and discordant modalities.
acceptanceTest.actions: Attempt the current index CTA and require it to fail closed; open synchronized bounded SNURF-SNRPN, UBE3A and event views; verify GRCh38, primary/methylation runs, roster and receipt hash; load each fixture; separate sample-total from per-copy data; inspect exact alleles and event components; test phase and parent-of-origin gates; classify UPD only with chromosome-wide evidence; audit linked-state callable/no-call counts; attempt diagnostic and A/B-to-parent inferences; export and reload the receipt.
acceptanceTest.expected: The index CTA is rejected. A is sample-total only; B is receipt-qualified A/B co-display with parent and long-range phase unknown; C is same-copy/phase-linked but parent unknown; D alone may use parent-of-origin-qualified wording; E preserves exact event, copy and methylation linkage; F distinguishes heterodisomy/isodisomy/mixed/epimutation-like only when its full evidence rules pass; G is candidate/discordant rather than concordant; H stays unavailable, never zero; I says not observed only with full multimodal callability. Diagnostic and pathogenic/benign inferences are rejected. Reload reconstructs every window, CpG, event/allele, link, parent receipt, denominator, missing state and provenance identity.
acceptanceTest.forbidden: The result must not use the truncated index interval as a complete locus; duplicate sample-total methylation into A/B; label A/B, HAP1/HAP2 or GT1/GT2 maternal/paternal; infer long-range linkage from chromosome-wide mapping with null phase_set; call UPD from methylation alone; collapse a CNV row and nearby methylation into one event without copy linkage; report 22/22 as separate SV sensitivity; treat participant count, row AN or average depth as linked-state callability; convert missingness to zero or reference; infer diagnosis, pathogenicity, benignity, penetrance, recurrence risk, or management; or claim the population browser replaces clinical testing.

evidence.claim: The source is a medRxiv preprint posted April 3, 2024, not certified by peer review; page 1 says it should not be used to guide clinical practice.
evidence.citation: PDF p. 1 header/footer

evidence.claim: Twenty-five blood-derived samples were studied: 23 people with prior clinical and molecular PWS/AS diagnoses and two negative controls. M0168, M0169 and M0379 were positive training controls; the blinded set was 22 cases containing 11 AS, 9 PWS and 2 negatives.
evidence.citation: PDF pp. 2, 4, 9–10, and 19–21; Tables 1 and 3

evidence.claim: After training, three reviewers (two clinical geneticists and one laboratory variant scientist), blinded to diagnosis and positive/negative fraction, independently categorized all 22 as PWS, AS or neither correctly: 20/20 affected and 2/2 negative controls.
evidence.citation: PDF pp. 2, 4, 10, and 13

evidence.claim: Data were aligned to GRCh38 with minimap2 2.26. Clair3 1.0.1 called/phased SNVs and indels; QDNAseq called CNVs; Sniffles 2.0.7 and CuteSV 2.1.0 called SVs; MeOW called DMRs; WhatsHap 1.7 extracted phase blocks.
evidence.citation: PDF pp. 6–8, Methods

evidence.claim: MeOW compared CpG islands having at least 50 non-N positions against an unaffected sequence database using ordered 50-point bootstrap beta regressions; significant DMRs required Benjamini-Hochberg-corrected p<0.01 and Cohen's d≥1.75. The one-page plot suppressed a CpG region when fewer than 20 spanning non-N reads were present and used 20 blood-derived controls.
evidence.citation: PDF pp. 7 and 10, DMR methods and report description
PDF pp. 7–8, Evaluation of differentially methylated regions

evidence.claim: The report covered chr15:20,000,000–33,000,000 and combined 1 kb-bin depth, homozygous/heterozygous SNV patterns, selected CpG methylation versus controls, and rare UBE3A SNVs/indels. It used low depth for deletion, elevated depth for duplication, and SNV zygosity to support deletion/isodisomy/heterodisomy interpretation while warning that segmental duplications create apparent heterozygous artifacts.
evidence.citation: PDF pp. 9–10 and 17, Results and Fig. 2

evidence.claim: Table 3 contains 18 deletion cases, four copy-neutral UPD cases (three heterodisomy, one isodisomy), one UBE3A-variant case, and two negatives. QDNAseq reported a deletion for all 18 and none for the other seven. The blinded subset therefore contained 16 deletions, three UPDs, one UBE3A-variant case and two negatives.
evidence.citation: PDF p. 21, Table 3; training identities from p. 19

evidence.claim: Table 3 says prior changes were identified by SNP array unless specified, with M0379 FISH-only. Its caption names M0855 and M0857 as the two MS-MLPA-only cases, but the table cells also label M0517 and M0520 'MS-MLPA only'; this internal comparator discrepancy must remain unresolved.
evidence.citation: PDF p. 21, Table 3 caption and rows

evidence.claim: M0522 had a de novo 3-bp in-frame UBE3A deletion, but the main PDF supplies no genomic coordinate or HGVS and incorrectly points to Table 2, which contains only breakpoint/gene coordinates. A 4.6 Mb phase block chr15:24471449–29047296 placed the deletion on arbitrary haplotype 2 with hypermethylated SNURF-SNRPN CpG, supporting the paper's maternal interpretation; several reads at the CpG were unphased.
evidence.citation: PDF pp. 11–12, 18, and 20; Fig. 3 and Table 2

evidence.claim: A single phase block spanned SNURF-SNRPN and UBE3A in 92/100 high-coverage ONT 1000 Genomes samples; the authors call this an expected upper limit under their laboratory conditions and note ultra-long methods may improve it at added time/cost.
evidence.citation: PDF p. 11, Phasing and evaluation of de novo UBE3A variants

evidence.claim: Among 18 deletion cases and one isodisomy case, filtering found one GOLGA8M SNV (chr15:28702214 C>G) and one GABRG3 SNV (chr15:27520091 A>G) for manual review; neither was judged disease-causing. No qualifying indels were found.
evidence.citation: PDF pp. 12 and 22, Table 4

evidence.claim: The paper reports that Sniffles and CuteSV were run, but provides no separate SV result table, truth-set adjudication, or SV-specific concordance estimate. The blinded one-page report and Table 3 describe CNV, SNV pattern, methylation and UBE3A review rather than a separately scored SV endpoint.

Limitations include substantial bioinformatics expertise/resources, report maintenance, omission of trio information from the report template, a small selected cohort, and no known imprinting-center deletion or pure epimutation samples. The abstract reports 36x average depth while Results reports 34x; the 25 Table 1 depths average 36.44x.
evidence.citation: PDF pp. 2, 9, 14, and 19

evidence.claim: The 22/22 endpoint is exact for blinded three-way molecular-case categorization after three positive training cases; it must not be restated as independent 100% sensitivity/specificity for DMRs, CNVs, SVs, SNVs, UPD subtypes, or parent-of-origin calls.
evidence.citation: Analyst reconstruction from PDF pp. 2, 9–10, 13, 19 and 21; requires paper-truth review

evidence.claim: The current index window is not defensible: Table 2 prints UBE3A chr15:25333728–25439056, so chr15:25336390–25436390 trims 2,662 bp from each end and misses cpg.7736; it is also incapable of representing the 619,417 bp SNURF-SNRPN-to-UBE3A phase interval or 13 Mb CNV overview.
evidence.citation: Analyst coordinate comparison of manifest, PDF pp. 8–10 and Table 2

evidence.claim: Imprinting attribution requires three distinct receipts: valid locus-specific methylation, linkage of that methylation and the exact sequence/copy event to one chromosome copy, and valid parent-of-origin evidence. Browser A/B and sample-total methylation satisfy none of these jointly.
evidence.citation: Analyst workflow reconstruction from PDF Fig. 3 and current browser semantics; requires workflow/data-semantics review

evidence.claim: A population replay must return a linked-state occurrence, candidate/discordant state, conditional non-observation, or data-blocked result. It cannot reenact the paper's patient diagnosis or use occurrence/absence to classify an external allele.
evidence.citation: Analyst safety reconstruction; requires clinical/product review

evidence.claim: The linked-state denominator is the number of chromosome copies callable for every required allele/event, DMR CpG set, phase span and parent/copy rule under matched provenance. Per-row AN, 292 participants, up to 230 sample-total observations at one CpG, or average depth are not linked-state denominators.
evidence.citation: Analyst denominator contract; requires data-semantics review

evidence.claim: On 2026-08-11 the deployed SNURF-SNRPN and UBE3A region routes returned HTTP 200, but the literature index, ref-48 detail slug and /papers/48.pdf returned HTTP 404 on browser revision gnomad-lr-browser-00012-suv.

LiteratureWorkflow has one browserRegion or a blocked reason; current GraphQL/UI provides no synchronized long-range multimodal/parent-of-origin query or export receipt.

paper.title: Cas9 targeted nanopore sequencing with enhanced variant calling improves CYP2D6 - CYP2D7 hybrid allele genotyping

locus: CYP2D6/CYP2D7 · GRCh38 paper target chr22:42121165-42149371 · CoLoRGen transcript-copy spans CYP2D6 chr22:42126499-42130810 and CYP2D7 chr22:42139576-42144483, both reverse strand

persona.role: Pharmacogene structural-haplotype researcher or molecular genetics laboratory scientist
persona.context: Research comparison of an externally resolved CYP2D6/CYP2D7 locus against population-reference structural haplotypes, with copy order, paralog origin, phase, caller provenance and unresolved states preserved

nonDiagnosticBoundary: This workflow may report a sequence- and structure-resolved CYP2D6/CYP2D7 population-reference haplotype, its copy-slot order, phased marker ledger, exact source/run identity and a version-pinned external star-definition comparison. It cannot derive a named star allele from flat browser variants alone, infer CYP2D6 activity score, metabolizer phenotype, drug response, diagnosis, pathogenicity/benignity, dosing or treatment. PharmVar/star-allele and pharmacogenomic interpretation remain external curated logic.

startingState.trigger: An external assay reports a CYP2D6/CYP2D7 hybrid or a candidate *68-like/*13-like architecture and the analyst needs bounded population-reference structural-haplotype context rather than a flat list of nearby variants.
inputs: GRCh38/NC_000022.11 and an explicit coordinate convention; the paper target is chr22:42121165-42149371

Pinned locus-copy spans and strand: paper/CoLoRGen CYP2D6-203 chr22:42126499-42130810 and CYP2D7-207 chr22:42139576-42144483, both reverse strand; current Ensembl spans are a separately versioned navigation annotation
For each chromosome copy, an ordered segment/copy ledger in genomic-coordinate order, while retaining reverse-strand transcript orientation separately

Exact outer junctions/breakpoints, insertion/deletion span, orientation and complete inserted/consensus sequence or hash; internal CYP2D6/CYP2D7 transition intervals must remain unresolved when not nucleotide-resolved
Copy-slot counts separated into intact CYP2D6, intact CYP2D7, hybrid and deleted slots rather than one undifferentiated CN
Phased SNV/indel marker set with phase-set/read receipt, allele-specific depth, no-calls and caller/model versions

A version-pinned external PharmVar definition. The paper used a closest-variant lookup, but neither the paper PDF nor the checked CoLoRGen repository includes the referenced CYP2D6 PharmVar TSV, so *1/*2/*3/*4 marker definitions are not frozen here

A predeclared comparison rule requiring copy order, copy class, exact breakpoints/sequence, phased markers, callability and accepted source identity; similar length, locus overlap or star-name text alone is not equivalence
startingState.question: For each HGSVC/HPRC chromosome-locus copy, is the same ordered, phased CYP2D6/CYP2D7 structural haplotype represented, and what exact structural-copy AC/AN and unresolved fields can be reported before a separately governed, version-pinned star-definition review?
startingState.stopRule: Stop before a named-star, recurrence or not-observed claim if build, strand, copy order, breakpoint/insert identity, paralog-segment origin, phase, marker-definition version, event-level callability or accepted run provenance is missing. AoU is aggregate-only and cannot answer the structural-haplotype question.

before: Freeze the paper/source identity. The local 21-page asset is the final PLOS Genetics paper (DOI 10.1371/journal.pgen.1010176; SHA-256 63d06e373cf8833b84a762569586d1b735a6782babf4093ad28e902bce2249aa), while the repository index intentionally retains the bioRxiv DOI required by the current workflow identity check.

Pin GRCh38 and the locus map. In ascending reference-coordinate order the CoLoRGen analysis copies are CYP2D6 chr22:42126499-42130810, then CYP2D7 chr22:42139576-42144483; both transcripts are reverse-strand, so coordinate order and 5-prime-to-3-prime transcript order must not be conflated.

Record the paper's exact structural evidence without over-resolving it: HG01190 *5 deletion breakpoints 42123191 and 42135343 (12,152 bp); *68-associated duplicated source span printed in reverse order 42145873 to 42132193 (13,680 bp), normalized only for interval display to chr22:42132193-42145873. The main paper does not publish a nucleotide-resolved internal CYP2D6/CYP2D7 crossover coordinate.

Preserve sample architectures as ordered copy slots: NA12878 allele 1 [CYP2D6 *3, CYP2D7], allele 2 [CYP2D6 *4, *68 hybrid, CYP2D7]; HG01190 allele 1 [CYP2D6 *5 deletion, CYP2D7], allele 2 [CYP2D6 *4, *68 hybrid, CYP2D7]; GM19785 allele 1 [CYP2D6 *1, CYP2D7], allele 2 [CYP2D6 *2, *13 hybrid replacing the CYP2D7 slot].

Pin caller provenance: Guppy 5.0.7 high-accuracy basecalling/model r941_min_hac_g507; minimap/minimap2 2.18; Medaka Variant and Consensus 1.4.3; WhatsHap 1.1; CoLoRGen unversioned paper code; comparator NanoVar 1.4.1, Sniffles 1.0.12 and SVIM 1.4.2. Require at least 16X per allele/gene for reliable small variants and at least three breakpoint-spanning reads under the paper rule.

Load a reviewed external PharmVar snapshot and marker table. Treat the checked CoLoRGen hybrid JSON as an exon-membership template only: *68 has CYP2D6 exon 1 plus intron 9 and CYP2D7 exons 3-11; *68_dup has CYP2D6 exon 1 and CYP2D7 exons 3-11 plus intron 11; *13 has CYP2D6 exons 2-9 and CYP2D7 exons 1-2. JSON object order is not molecular segment order, and exon membership is not an exact breakpoint.
inside: Open the corrected provisional display chr22:42118682-42150000, not the manifest's chr22:42118682-42138682 window, which omits most of the paper/CoLoRGen CYP2D7 span. Verify build, cohort, release, database, chr22 run, scope and acceptance state.

Query all sequence/SV rows across the full locus, then reconstruct each HGSVC/HPRC chromosome copy from source records plus carrier phase. Do not treat vcf_strand 1/2 as a biological haplotype name; retain phase_set and the source GT-position semantics.

Construct an ordered copy ledger for every candidate: intact CYP2D6, deletion, duplication/insertion, hybrid, intact CYP2D7; for every hybrid list ordered CYP2D6- and CYP2D7-derived segments, exact transition intervals, orientation, junction sequence/hash, copy number and support depth.

Compare exact architecture before markers. A 12-14 kb deletion/duplication, exact-anchor event family, similar inserted length or paralog-rich ALT is only a candidate until both junctions, source span, orientation, segment order and sequence reconcile.

Only after architecture and phase reconcile, compare the phased marker ledger to a versioned external PharmVar definition. Report exact definition match, closest-definition-with-differences, ambiguous among definitions or unresolved; never silently choose the closest star label.

Compute a structural-copy denominator only from chromosome-locus copies for which the source can distinguish intact D6, intact D7, hybrid, deletion, ordered duplication and no-call states. Record AC, event-callable AN, no-calls, representation failures, participants and strata. A nearby record's AN, base depth or flat variant-row count is not this denominator.

Keep AoU as an aggregate record-level context branch only. It has no carriers, sample metadata or haplotype phase and therefore cannot support copy order, structural haplotypes or star-allele occurrence.
after: Return one bounded structural result: exact ordered structural haplotype observed; structure-comparable but internal crossover/sequence unresolved; same components in different order; nearby/length-similar event only; not observed among N fully reconstructable chromosome-locus copies; or data-blocked.

Export the locus map, ordered copy slots, breakpoint and insert hashes, segment-origin ledger, phased marker/no-call table, caller/model versions, event AC/AN/missingness, cohort/release/database/run/scope/status, source IDs/ALT indexes/filters, query timestamp and immutable receipt.

Hand the structural receipt to separately governed PharmVar/star-definition review. Keep activity score, metabolizer phenotype, drug-gene guideline selection and any prescribing interpretation external; unresolved remains a valid final state.

For the current live release, report data-blocked for a paper-*68-equivalent or any named-star prevalence: many large paralog-rich records exist, but the API does not expose copy-slot order, paralog segment origin, star-definition version or a structural-copy denominator.

branches.action: Report different architecture; flat component equality is not haplotype equivalence.

branches.action: Refuse the inference and route the exported molecular structure to independent curated pharmacogenomic review.

acceptanceTest.fixture: Seven GRCh38 fixtures: (A) resolved NA12878-like H1 [D6*3,D7], H2 [D6*4,*68-hybrid,D7] with exact junctions, ordered D6/D7 segments, phased markers and caller receipt; (B) identical flat variants/CN but reversed copy or segment order; (C) a 13.7 kb insertion with matching length but missing transition/sequence; (D) a closest-star marker profile with extra/conflicting markers and no pinned PharmVar version; (E) no exact event with high depth/record AN but no reconstructable-copy receipt; (F) no exact event with complete per-copy reconstruction/no-calls; and (G) the same aggregate rows in AoU.
acceptanceTest.actions: Open the corrected provisional region; attest build, strand, cohort, database, release, run, scope and status; reconstruct ordered HGSVC/HPRC copy slots; compare exact breakpoints/sequence/segment origin before markers; inspect phase_set and VCF-position semantics; apply a pinned external star definition; compute event AC/AN/no-calls; repeat the request in AoU; export and reload the receipt.
acceptanceTest.expected: Fixture A is an exact ordered molecular match and may receive only a versioned external-definition match; B is a different architecture; C is structure/transition unresolved; D remains ambiguous/unresolved; E is data-blocked rather than AC=0; F supports only 'not observed among N reconstructable chromosome-locus copies'; G never exposes carriers, phase, order or named-star occurrence. Reload preserves order, unresolved fields, caller versions, counts and provenance.
acceptanceTest.forbidden: No fixture may infer a star allele from length/overlap or flat SNVs, sort away CYP2D6/CYP2D7 order, call VCF strand maternal/paternal or biological haplotype, borrow nearby/event-row AN, turn base depth into structural callability, convert missing transition/marker data into reference, use AoU for haplotypes, or infer activity score, metabolizer phenotype, drug response, pathogenicity/benignity, diagnosis, dosing or care.

evidence.claim: The paper's GRCh38 target is chr22:42121165-42149371. The associated CoLoRGen configuration defines CYP2D6-203 chr22:42126499-42130810 and CYP2D7-207 chr22:42139576-42144483, both reverse-strand, inside that target.
evidence.citation: Rubben et al. 2022 PDF p. 9 Table 1; paper-linked CoLoRGen cyp2d6_hybrids.json and parameters.sh, checked commit eee82b87f994eb00bf2265d8960f615278da3848

evidence.claim: CoLoRGen basecalled with Guppy 5.0.7 high accuracy, mapped with minimap 2.18 to GRCh38, called/consensed with Medaka 1.4.3, phased SNVs/indels with WhatsHap 1.1, split reads by allele, required at least three breakpoint reads, built allele-adjusted references, and assigned the closest PharmVar star/sub-allele after reconstructing gene/hybrid fragments.
evidence.citation: Rubben et al. 2022 PDF pp. 6-8

evidence.claim: The paper established a 16X per-allele/per-gene lower limit for reliable small-variant calling; comparator versions were NanoVar 1.4.1, Sniffles 1.0.12 and SVIM 1.4.2.
evidence.citation: Rubben et al. 2022 PDF p. 8

evidence.claim: NA12878 was assigned *3/*4+*68. The *68 CYP2D6/CYP2D7 hybrid insertion had 74X depth and phased with the small variants absent from the older benchmark. The paper argues the NA12878 reference should be corrected to include *68 and additional SNVs/indels, while noting Get-RM had listed *68 only in brackets and Cyrius had statistically inferred it.
evidence.citation: Rubben et al. 2022 PDF pp. 11-14, Figs. 3-4

evidence.claim: For HG01190, 37 reads supported the 12,152 bp *5 deletion between GRCh38 positions 42123191 and 42135343; six reads supported a 13,680 bp duplication of the region printed in reverse order as 42145873 to 42132193. The final genotype was *5/*4+*68.
evidence.citation: Rubben et al. 2022 PDF pp. 14-15; S1 Text Table C

evidence.claim: GM19785 was assigned *1/*2+*13. The *13 hybrid replaced the CYP2D7 slot, so copy count alone did not reveal it; it was identified from small-variant/paralog sequence. The sequence between CYP2D6 and the hybrid remained unresolved because the hybrid introduced an extra gRNA2 cut and no read spanned the whole target.
evidence.citation: Rubben et al. 2022 PDF p. 15 and S5 Fig. description

evidence.claim: The checked CoLoRGen hybrid template describes *68 as CYP2D6 exon 1 plus intron 9 and CYP2D7 exons 3-11; *68_dup as CYP2D6 exon 1 and CYP2D7 exons 3-11 plus intron 11; and *13 as CYP2D6 exons 2-9 with CYP2D7 exons 1-2. These are exon-membership templates, not nucleotide breakpoint coordinates.
evidence.citation: Paper-linked CoLoRGen cyp2d6_hybrids.json at checked commit eee82b87f994eb00bf2265d8960f615278da3848

evidence.claim: The assay used 5 micrograms of DNA and one MinION flowcell per sample; low on-target fraction/depth, high cost, hybrid-created guide cuts, homopolymer errors, incomplete/outdated star definitions and only three reference cell lines limit transfer. Existing SV callers did not reliably resolve all locus structures.
evidence.citation: Rubben et al. 2022 PDF pp. 9-10 and 15-17; S1 Text Tables B-C

evidence.claim: A reusable structural haplotype must preserve ascending reference-coordinate copy order separately from reverse-strand transcript direction. Exact equivalence requires copy-slot order, both outer junctions, source span, orientation, nucleotide sequence/hash, ordered paralog segments and phased markers; matching length or component multiset is insufficient.
evidence.citation: Analyst reconstruction from the paper locus map, Figs. 2 and 4, and the CoLoRGen hybrid template; requires pharmacogene/SV review

evidence.claim: The internal *68/*13 crossover remains unresolved unless sequence-level transition coordinates are supplied. Exon membership, JSON object order or a star label must not be converted into an exact breakpoint.
evidence.citation: Analyst safety rule grounded in the paper's unresolved GM19785 sequence and CoLoRGen exon-membership-only JSON

evidence.claim: Current Ensembl GRCh38 lookup gives broader annotation spans CYP2D6 ENSG00000100197.25 chr22:42120962-42131727 and CYP2D7 ENSG00000205702.14 chr22:42140203-42149500, both strand -1. These support extending the display to 42150000 but do not replace the paper's transcript-copy spans.
