paper.title: Exonization of a deep intronic long interspersed nuclear element in Becker muscular dystrophy

locus: DMD intron 1 insertion site: paper GRCh37 NC_000023.10:g.33227460_33227461; composition-verified candidate GRCh38 NC_000023.11:g.33209343_33209344. The inserted product is 6,069 bp: a 6,051 bp chr8/KCNB2-intron-2 segment containing a 6,031 bp minus-strand L1HS, followed by C, followed by a direct 17 bp DMD target-derived non-tandem duplicate.

persona.role: Dystrophinopathy or mobile-element structural-variation researcher/laboratory scientist
persona.context: Research follow-up of an externally detected deep-intronic DMD insertion, asking first whether the same DNA architecture is represented in population long-read data and then handing the bounded DNA result to an independent RNA-splicing review

nonDiagnosticBoundary: This workflow can report whether a comparable DNA insertion architecture is represented in a population reference and whether chromosome copies were callable for that architecture. It cannot infer exonization from genomic overlap, reproduce the paper patient's muscle RNA result in a population participant, diagnose dystrophinopathy, classify pathogenicity or benignity, or transfer the paper phenotype, protein, segregation, or transcript evidence to a reference carrier.

startingState.trigger: An externally detected insertion or LINE-1 signal in DMD intron 1, or an unexplained exon-1-to-exon-2 splice product, requires structure-resolved population-reference comparison.
inputs: Original build, accession, transcript and endpoint convention; the paper uses GRCh37 accessions NC_000023.10/NC_000008.10 and DMD transcript NM_004006.2
Paper DNA target NC_000023.10:g.33227460_33227461 and both genomic breakpoint-PCR/Sanger junctions
Complete ordered insert notation NC_000008.10:g.73787774_73793824;C;NC_000023.10:g.33227444_33227460, with no inv/complement operator
Component lengths: 6,051 bp chr8 donor segment, one inserted C, and 17 bp direct DMD non-tandem duplicate, totaling 6,069 bp
Embedded L1HS interval chr8:73,787,793–73,793,823 (GRCh37), its strand/orientation, sequence completeness and annotation provenance
A build-remap receipt for target, donor, duplicated interval, orientation and composed altered product
RNA evidence as a separate external object: tissue, RT-PCR bands, cDNA Sanger sequence, splice-junction notation, transcript mixture and assay provenance
Cohort/release/run, non-PAR X ploidy model, MEI-architecture callability rule, callable/no-call X-copy counts and participant counts kept separate
startingState.question: Does the selected population release contain the same target, complete chr8/L1HS donor sequence, orientation, inserted C and 17 bp direct target-derived duplicate, a structurally different same-site insertion, only nearby/fragmented evidence, a callable non-observation, or a no-call—and after that DNA-only result, what external RNA evidence is still required to establish exonization?
startingState.stopRule: Stop exact matching if build, target convention, either junction, complete insert sequence, orientation, one-copy linkage or the 17 bp duplicate is unavailable. Stop a not-observed claim if representation-complete MEI callability and non-PAR X-copy denominators are unavailable. Never infer exonization, splice-site use, transcript abundance or protein effect from DNA overlap or population occurrence.

before: Freeze a DNA architecture signature before querying: interbase target, both retained flanks, complete ordered 6,069 bp inserted product, chr8 donor interval, L1HS interval/subfamily/strand, inserted C, direct 17 bp DMD duplicate, and both breakpoint validations. Do not reduce it to 'LINE-1 in DMD.'

Preserve the paper's terminology: insertion/non-tandem duplication. The 17 bp sequence is a direct target-derived repeat flanking the inserted material, but the paper does not call it a target-site duplication; record 'TSD-like, terminology gated' rather than silently relabeling it TSD.

Validate the complete GRCh37-to-GRCh38 composition. Candidate GRCh38 is NC_000023.11:g.33209343_33209344ins[NC_000008.11:g.72875539_72881589;C;NC_000023.11:g.33209327_33209343]. Retain the chain identity, sequence hashes, accessions and the fact that this is an analyst remap, not paper-provided GRCh38 notation.

Create a separate RNA-evidence object. The DNA query may nominate an architecture for follow-up, but only tissue-derived transcript evidence can establish the exon-1-to-exon-2 111 bp insertion and cryptic splice-junction use.
inside: Open the corrected GRCh38 target window chrX:33,204,343–33,214,343, not the generic index window, and verify cohort, accepted chrX primary run, database, reference build and modality availability.

Enumerate every exact-site and nearby INS, LINE_INS, other MEI subtype, DUP/complex-duplication and split representation. Preserve source_variant_id and ALT index, but do not infer a shared event from source-ID text, interval overlap or display family.

Apply tiered DNA matching. Exact comparable architecture requires the mapped target and both junctions, complete 6,051 bp chr8 donor sequence in accession-plus orientation, the embedded minus-strand L1HS, inserted C, direct 17 bp DMD duplicate, total structure/length and same-copy linkage. Same site with a different sequence/orientation/duplicate is a different insertion; a nearby LINE_INS is ordinary nearby evidence.

For any exact event, report AC against X chromosome copies callable for both junctions and complete 6,069 bp representation. Reconcile XX and XY copy counts, no-calls, representation failures and participants; row AN from another insertion, nearby SNV AN and base coverage are not the event denominator.

Display RNA exonization as unavailable in the population browser unless a separately admitted RNA modality exists. A DNA match must end with an explicit external RNA handoff, not an exonized/canonical-splicing label.
after: Export paper and remapped coordinates, accessions, endpoint convention, full component sequence hashes, L1HS annotation/strand, inserted C, 17 bp duplicate and terminology gate, all candidate records/ALTs, exact-versus-nearby classification, event AC/AN/no-calls, XX/XY reconciliation, release/run/database, filters, URL state, timestamp and rule version.

Hand the DNA receipt to an external RNA workflow requiring tissue and assay provenance, exon-1/exon-2 RT-PCR, cDNA Sanger or equivalent junction sequence, the 15 bp DMD + G + 95 bp L1HS-derived transcript structure, normal-versus-aberrant transcript observation and appropriate expert review.

Return only bounded population-reference wording. Preserve the paper's RNA, dystrophin and patient findings as external case evidence; do not attach them to population carriers or use population occurrence/non-occurrence as a clinical classification.

branches.condition: The original build, endpoint convention, full insert composition, orientation, one or both junctions, or 17 bp duplicate is missing
branches.action: Report DNA architecture data-blocked and list the missing fields; do not issue exact-match, same-site-equivalent or not-observed results.

branches.condition: An insertion is at the mapped target but donor sequence, orientation, inserted C, total structure or 17 bp duplicate differs
branches.action: Report same-site different insertion and preserve the field-level differences; do not call it the paper architecture.

branches.condition: Only a nearby LINE_INS/INS, one junction, a generic DMD overlap, L1-family similarity or unlinked fragments are represented
branches.action: Report nearby/partial candidate evidence and identify the missing target, junction, sequence, orientation, duplicate or linkage; stop exact-equivalence claims.

branches.condition: Target, both junctions, complete ordered insert, accession-plus orientation, embedded L1HS strand, inserted C, direct 17 bp duplicate and same-copy linkage all match
branches.action: Report comparable DNA architecture observed with architecture-callable AC/AN, no-calls and provenance, then hand off to external RNA review; do not report exonization.

branches.condition: No exact event is found and complete MEI representation plus per-copy non-PAR X event callability are independently established
branches.action: Report not observed in N architecture-callable X copies, with XX/XY, no-call and participant counts and bounded uncertainty; make no exonization or pathogenicity inference.

branches.condition: No exact row is returned but complete-event representation or X-copy callability is unavailable
branches.action: Report data-blocked, not AC=0, absent or rare.

branches.condition: A comparable DNA architecture is observed but no admitted tissue RNA evidence is available
branches.action: Report DNA architecture only and 'RNA exonization status unavailable'; create the explicit external RNA handoff.

branches.condition: External tissue RNA independently shows the exact exon-1-to-exon-2 aberrant junction under pinned assay provenance
branches.action: Attach the external functional receipt as a separate modality/evidence object. Do not claim that the population browser itself observed RNA exonization or transfer that result to another carrier.

story.given: the paper's GRCh37 DMD target and complete 6,069 bp insertion/non-tandem-duplication architecture, a composition-verified GRCh38 remap receipt, and RNA evidence represented separately
story.when: the researcher opens the corrected target window, matches target/junctions/full donor orientation/inserted C/17 bp duplicate on one X copy, audits architecture-specific callability, and then requests an external RNA handoff
story.then: the workflow returns exact comparable DNA architecture, same-site different insertion, nearby/partial candidate, not observed in N callable X copies, or data-blocked, followed separately by RNA exonization confirmed externally or RNA status unavailable—never exonization inferred from overlap

browserRegionNotice: Corrected 10 kb GRCh38 target window centered on the analyst-remapped interbase junction after chrX:33,209,343. The complete component sequences and target context are assembly-identical under the checked UCSC chain, but the paper itself supplies only GRCh37 notation; retain the remap receipt and do not treat navigation as proof of a matching event.

capabilities.step: Correct the generic DMD window and navigate to the candidate GRCh38 target
capabilities.evidence: The complete paper components map on plus-strand chains to chrX:33,209,343|33,209,344 and chr8:72,875,539–72,881,589 with identical component sequences; the corrected production region route returned HTTP 200. Current index source still stores unrelated chrX:32,168,643–32,268,643 and marks it unverified.

capabilities.step: Enumerate exact-site and nearby insertion representations with accepted chrX provenance
capabilities.evidence: The live API returned 109 HGSVC/HPRC and 386 AoU records in the corrected 10 kb window and accepted full-chromosome chrX primary provenance, but no record at the exact target. HGSVC/HPRC had one 214 bp LINE_INS 2,543 bp away; nearby small INS records were 715 bp away in HGSVC/HPRC and 570 bp away in AoU.

capabilities.step: Compare exact target, complete donor/L1HS sequence, orientation, inserted C and 17 bp duplicate
capabilities.evidence: LongReadVariant can expose ALT sequence, length, type and source identity, but has no explicit donor interval, MEI subfamily/strand, TSD/non-tandem-duplicate, junction completeness or same-copy architecture fields. There is no exact-site candidate to reconcile.

capabilities.step: Group fragmented or subtype-specific records into one reviewable MEI event
capabilities.evidence: Current source-event aggregation keys most insertions by exact interval and includes INS/ALU_INS/SVA_INS/NUMT, but omits LINE_INS from that insertion family. source_variant_id is explicitly a byte-exact record ID, not a guaranteed event ID.

capabilities.step: Search the full paper structure in one predicate
capabilities.evidence: Local search supports positions, ranges, IDs, alleles and only 3–64 bp sequence fragments; multiple terms are OR and sequence matching checks REF/ALT/motifs. It cannot require both junctions plus full donor, orientation, inserted C and duplicate as one linked architecture.

capabilities.step: Report architecture-specific callable non-PAR X denominators
capabilities.evidence: The exact event has no row. Nearby rows expose varying row-level AN, and exact-site coverage is base-depth percentage rather than sensitivity/representation for a 6,069 bp insertion. No per-copy event-callability or no-call receipt is exposed.

capabilities.step: Inspect a carrying chromosome copy
capabilities.evidence: HGSVC/HPRC provenance marks HAPLOTYPES unavailable for the accepted chrX run; AoU is summary-only. No exact architecture carrier exists to inspect.

capabilities.step: Observe or infer RNA exonization inside the population browser
capabilities.evidence: The primary API exposes predicted transcript consequences but no tissue RNA reads, RT-PCR bands, cDNA junction sequence, isoform abundance or admitted RNA-splicing modality. Genomic overlap and annotations are not observed exonization.

capabilities.step: Open a curated ref-141 detailed workflow page
capabilities.evidence: Current clean source commit 7c8c7b97 contains 20 workflow records and no ref 141. On 2026-08-11 the deployed workflow slug, literature index and /papers/141.pdf returned HTTP 404, while the corrected and generic region routes returned HTTP 200.

capabilities.step: Use population matching to diagnose, classify, or transfer the paper RNA result
capabilities.evidence: The paper's exonization evidence came from the patient's muscle-derived RNA and cDNA Sanger sequence. Population DNA occurrence or non-occurrence cannot establish that functional result in another person.

acceptanceTest.fixture: At the corrected GRCh38 DMD target provide: (A) one complete 6,069 bp exact architecture with both junctions, the 6,051 bp chr8 donor in accession-plus orientation, embedded minus-strand L1HS, inserted C and direct 17 bp DMD duplicate; (B) a same-site LINE-1 with different donor/orientation/TSD; (C) the live-like 214 bp LINE_INS 2,543 bp away; (D) one-junction and unlinked fragment records; (E) callable XX/XY reference X copies, explicit no-calls and a representation-complete no-event state; and (F) for A, separate external RNA fixtures consisting of exact 111 bp exon-1-to-exon-2 junction evidence, negative/other-splice evidence and no RNA assay.
acceptanceTest.actions: Attempt the generic index link and require a relevance warning; open the corrected receipted window; inspect provenance and every exact/nearby MEI ALT; compare complete DNA structure and linkage; audit event AC/AN, XX/XY copies and no-calls; request exonization before and after attaching each external RNA fixture; export and reload the receipt.
acceptanceTest.expected: The generic window is rejected as event-irrelevant and the corrected window opens provisionally. A alone is exact comparable DNA architecture; B is same-site different insertion; C is ordinary nearby MEI evidence; D is partial/data-blocked. E reports not observed only with complete event callability. Before RNA handoff A is 'RNA status unavailable,' never exonized; the exact external RNA fixture alone adds a separate exonization-confirmed functional receipt, while negative/absent RNA remains separate. Reload reproduces components, classifications, denominators, provenance and RNA-modality boundary.
acceptanceTest.forbidden: The result must not call generic DMD overlap, a nearby LINE_INS, L1-family similarity, one junction or an unlinked fragment exact; relabel the 17 bp repeat as TSD without preserving the paper's non-tandem-duplication terminology gate; use nearby row AN or base coverage as 6,069 bp event callability; convert missingness to zero; infer exonization from DNA overlap, VEP consequence or carrier status; attach the paper patient's RNA/protein/phenotype to a population carrier; or diagnose/classify pathogenicity or benignity.

evidence.claim: Standard MLPA and short-read neuromuscular-panel testing were negative; muscle-derived DMD mRNA analysis and genomic long-read whole-DMD sequencing were pursued as separate assays.
evidence.citation: PDF p. 2, Standard genetic testing and DMD mRNA analysis; PDF pp. 3–4, Genomic short- and long-read whole DMD gene sequencing

evidence.claim: Nanopore PromethION whole-DMD sequencing had mean depth 306× and mean read length 3,942 bp. Ninety-two reads (mean 4,362 bp) indicated a roughly 6 kb chr8-derived insertion in DMD intron 1, and both genomic breakpoint regions were PCR/Sanger confirmed.
evidence.citation: PDF pp. 3–4 and Fig. 2A–E

evidence.claim: The paper's exact GRCh37 DNA notation is NC_000023.10:g.33227460_33227461ins[NC_000008.10:g.73787774_73793824;C;NC_000023.10:g.33227444_33227460]. It describes a 6,051 bp KCNB2-intron-2 donor segment, one C and a 17 bp DMD-intron-1 non-tandem duplicate, totaling 6,069 inserted bases.
evidence.citation: PDF p. 4, genomic SV paragraph and Fig. 2F–G

evidence.claim: Most of the donor, GRCh37 chr8:73,787,793–73,793,823, was annotated L1HS/LINE-1. The paper calls the target-derived 17 bp component a non-tandem duplication and does not explicitly call it a target-site duplication.
evidence.citation: PDF p. 4 and Fig. 2F–G/caption

evidence.claim: Muscle RT-PCR showed both a longer aberrant band and a normal-sized band. cDNA Sanger sequencing identified a 111 bp insertion between DMD exons 1 and 2: 15 bp of DMD intron 1, one G and 95 bp homologous to KCNB2 intron 2/L1HS.
evidence.citation: PDF p. 2 and Fig. 1J–M

evidence.claim: The aberrant transcript is NM_004006.2:r.[=,31_32ins[NM_004006.2:r.31+1941_31+1955;g;NM_004770.2:r.580-54346_580-54440]]. The paper reports a cryptic LINE-1 donor GAG|GTACCG and DMD-intron acceptor ATCACCTTTTAG|AA, predicts p.[=,Tyr11*], and discusses nonsense-mediated decay.
evidence.citation: PDF pp. 2, 4–5 and Fig. 2H–I

evidence.claim: UCSC hg19ToHg38 chain SHA-256 5c0598e500ceb5a78c73086929e8ef993aec309bcafb595139b53d440b125a1d maps the target on plus strand from chrX:33,227,460|33,227,461 to chrX:33,209,343|33,209,344; the 17 bp duplicate maps to chrX:33,209,327–33,209,343 and the 6,051 bp donor to chr8:72,875,539–72,881,589.
evidence.citation: Read-only UCSC chain reconciliation, 2026-08-11

evidence.claim: The full 6,051 bp donor is byte-identical across assemblies (SHA-256 677dc633ad120f6cc782eec8ab5a8560daf6c721f69719c3aa339a63e1275504); the 17 bp duplicate TCTGCAGATGAAATTCT is identical (SHA-256 b5d3048b124f40c00ba17bcfbe3e57411d6ebe9dfd8ec6aff6c998b9883f18f2); a checked 120 bp target context is identical (SHA-256 56f527e1227f6ad6a06a4f5a92babd149c35441435bd1eccc218b35bb21a466e). This supports the candidate GRCh38 composed HGVS but remains an analyst remap.
evidence.citation: Read-only UCSC sequence API comparison, 2026-08-11

evidence.claim: UCSC hg19 RepeatMasker records the embedded 6,031 bp L1HS at chr8:73,787,793–73,793,823 on the minus strand. Because the HGVS donor has no inv/complement operator, it is copied in accession-plus orientation and retains that embedded minus-strand L1HS; DMD itself is minus-strand, so the element is sense-oriented relative to DMD transcription.
evidence.citation: Analyst reconciliation of paper HGVS/Fig. 2 with UCSC hg19 rmsk record (L1HS, strand '-', genoStart 73787792, genoEnd 73793823), 2026-08-11

evidence.claim: The original 17 bp target sequence remains immediately upstream of the junction and a direct copy occurs after the chr8 segment plus C, making it TSD-like in structure. Because the authors explicitly use 'non-tandem duplication' and never 'TSD,' a repository record must preserve that term and gate mechanistic TSD relabeling for MEI review.
evidence.citation: Analyst product reconstruction from paper HGVS and Fig. 2G; requires MEI-domain review

evidence.claim: Exact population matching must precede and remain logically separate from RNA review. Even a sequence-identical genomic event proves neither tissue expression nor cryptic splice-site use; exonization requires an admitted external RNA junction/isoform receipt.
evidence.citation: Analyst workflow and safety boundary grounded in the paper's separate DNA and muscle-RNA assays; requires workflow/clinical review

evidence.claim: The current ref-141 index source uses unverified generic chrX:32,168,643–32,268,643, which ends 940,700 bp before the remapped target. Both that generic route and corrected chrX:33,204,343–33,214,343 route returned HTTP 200; routability does not make the generic window relevant.
evidence.citation: Current longReadLiteratureExamples.json and read-only deployed route checks, 2026-08-11

evidence.claim: In the corrected 10 kb window the live API returned 109 HGSVC/HPRC records (84 SNV, 9 INS, 8 TRV, 7 DEL, 1 LINE_INS) and 386 AoU records (145 SNV, 9 INS, 223 TRV, 9 DEL). paper.title: Long-read sequencing identified a causal structural variant in an exome-negative case and enabled preimplantation genetic diagnosis

locus: G6PC1 (paper: G6PC), GRCh37 deleted bases chr17:41,049,879–41,057,003 (7,125 bp; AluJr/AluSx) and c.326G>A (p.Cys109Tyr); independently mapped GRCh38 deleted bases chr17:42,897,862–42,904,986 and, for NM_000151.3/.4, chr17:42,904,026G>A.

persona.role: Rare-disease structural-variant researcher or molecular laboratory scientist
persona.context: Research comparison after external assays have resolved one G6PC1 deletion and one point allele; the browser is used only to ask whether exact events and a supportable phase state occur in a named population-reference release

nonDiagnosticBoundary: This workflow can report exact population-reference occurrence, joint carriage and reference-participant copy phase only when event identity, deletion-aware genotypes and compatible phase evidence support it. It cannot establish the paper patient's phase, perform or guide PGT, diagnose GSD-Ia, classify an allele, infer penetrance, or transfer a reference participant's phase to a patient.

startingState.trigger: External testing reports the final Sanger-refined 7,125 bp G6PC1 deletion and c.326G>A (p.Cys109Tyr), while population occurrence and any reference-participant trans configuration remain unknown.
inputs: Original reference accession/build and endpoint convention; the paper used GRCh37 and finalized deleted bases chr17:41,049,879–41,057,003
Deletion junction or both retained flanks, deleted sequence, AluJr/AluSx context, source event/ALT identity, caller, genotype, and orthogonal validation
Point-variant transcript and version, c.326G>A / p.Cys109Tyr notation, genomic normalization, genotype, and validation; the paper does not print a transcript accession or genomic point coordinate
A reviewed GRCh37-to-GRCh38 event-remap receipt; candidate equivalent deleted bases are chr17:42,897,862–42,904,986 and the NM_000151.3/.4 point allele is chr17:42,904,026G>A

For phase: same reference sample, deterministic opposite-copy assignments for both exact events, compatible phase-set or chromosome-wide source-phase evidence, and deletion-aware genotype/copy-number handling
Release/database/run/source identity, exact-event callable chromosome-copy denominators, no-call and representation-mismatch counts, and query timestamp
Patient/family segregation, phenotype, PGT and diagnosis evidence retained outside the population-browser result
startingState.question: Does the selected release contain the exact normalized Alu-mediated deletion and exact c.326G>A allele, do they co-occur in any reference participant, and are they demonstrably on opposite chromosome copies under deletion-aware phase evidence?
startingState.stopRule: Stop exact matching if build, endpoint convention, junction/retained flanks, transcript normalization or source-event identity is missing. Stop trans claims if either exact event is absent, sample identity differs, copy assignment is ambiguous, phase sets are missing/incompatible, or the genotype model ignores that the point coordinate lies inside the deleted interval. Stop absence claims without event-specific callable AN and explicit missingness. Never infer patient phase, PGT suitability or diagnosis.

before: Freeze the paper's final Sanger-refined event separately from the initial noisy long-read call: final GRCh37 chr17:41,049,879–41,057,003del7125; initial long-read estimate chr17:41,049,904–41,057,049del7146 with four supporting reads and 20–50 bp breakpoint discordance.

Retain c.326G>A (p.Cys109Tyr) as the paper notation. If NM_000151.3 or NM_000151.4 is selected, record the external normalization to GRCh37 chr17:41,056,043G>A and GRCh38 chr17:42,904,026G>A; do not imply that the paper specified that transcript.

Validate the complete deletion, not only two lifted points. Preserve source/target accessions, inclusive deleted-base convention, full deleted-sequence and retained-flank hashes, Alu context, chain/tool identity and the reconstructed junction. Retain the original GRCh37 event beside the GRCh38 query.

Declare exact deletion equivalence as sequence-compatible retained flanks/junction, the same 7,125 deleted bases after documented normalization, deletion type, and one source event. A similar-size G6PC1 or Alu/Alu deletion, one shared breakpoint, gene overlap or a deletion family display is not exact.

Declare phase tiers before querying: separate occurrence; same-participant co-carriage; exact opposite-copy phase with compatible PS/source phase; or unresolved. The point base lies within the deleted interval, so a same-copy point ALT is an inconsistency unless a separately resolved complex copy-number architecture explains it.

Define the denominator as chromosome copies callable for the complete deletion event and point allele plus participants eligible for a joint phase test. Nominal 292 participants, 584 chromosomes, endpoint depth and nearby-row AN are context, not substitutes.
inside: Open chr17:42,897,618–42,917,618, confirm GRCh38, HGSVC/HPRC, accepted source/database/run and HAPLOTYPES/COVERAGE availability, and display that the region is an analyst-verified remap of a GRCh37 paper event.

Enumerate every deletion, split/normalized deletion representation and SNV ALT. Preserve source_variant_id and alt_index; reconcile normalization-equivalent deletion rows only with junction/flank evidence and never infer event identity from overlap or a source-ID prefix.

Apply the exact deletion predicate to GRCh38 deleted bases 42,897,862–42,904,986 (or an equivalent anchored representation) and the exact point predicate to 42,904,026G>A under the selected NM_000151 transcript. Report exact, partial, overlap-only, representation-mismatch, not-returned or not-callable states separately for each.

Only after both exact events are found, join carriers by the same sample. Distinguish same-participant co-carriage from trans. Require deterministic opposite VCF-copy assignments and the same compatible phase block or an explicit chromosome-wide source-phase receipt; copy 1/2 is not maternal/paternal.

Run a deletion-aware consistency check because 42,904,026 is among the deleted bases. Reject a claim that the SNV ALT occupies the deletion-bearing copy unless a validated duplication/complex architecture restores that base; expose possible hemizygous-SNV or genotype-model artifacts rather than repeating the paper's initial apparent homozygous WES call.

For each exact event and the joint state, show AC, callable AN, no-call/unassessed copies, carrier participants, ancestry strata, deterministic-versus-ambiguous phase counts, source/event/ALT identity and complete provenance. If an exact row is absent, do not borrow AN from a nearby row or convert local depth to event callability.
after: Export original and remapped event definitions, transcript normalization, junction/flank and sequence hashes, all candidate rows/ALTs, exact-match rules, carrier/copy/PS evidence, deletion-aware consistency outcome, AC/AN/no-calls, release/database/run/query and every triggered stop rule.

Return the bounded population-reference receipt for external molecular review. Patient-specific segregation, direct phase confirmation, phenotype, diagnosis, reproductive counseling and PGT remain outside gnomAD and outside this workflow.

branches.condition: The source build, endpoint convention, final junction/retained flanks, point transcript normalization or source-event identity is missing
branches.action: Report unresolved/data-blocked and list the missing evidence; allow visibly non-equivalent overlap exploration only.

branches.condition: An exact normalized deletion is observed but the exact point allele is not observed or not callable
branches.action: Report deletion occurrence only with its own AC/AN; do not report a joint state or trans phase.

branches.condition: Both exact events occur in the same reference participant but one copy assignment or phase relation is missing or incompatible
branches.action: Report same-participant co-carriage with phase unresolved; do not call cis, trans, maternal or paternal.

branches.condition: Both exact events occur in one reference participant on deterministic opposite copies with compatible continuous PS or explicit chromosome-wide source-phase evidence
branches.action: Report a trans configuration for that named reference participant only, with the deletion-aware consistency check and phase receipt; do not transfer it to the paper patient.

branches.condition: The point ALT is assigned to the deletion-bearing copy without a separately validated duplication or complex copy-number architecture
branches.action: Report a representation/genotype inconsistency and stop phase interpretation; investigate hemizygosity, allele indexing, normalization and copy number.

branches.condition: Only a similar-size deletion, one matching breakpoint, G6PC1 overlap, Alu/Alu mechanism or unlinked compatible records are represented
branches.action: Report partial/overlap-only or representation mismatch; do not transfer the candidate row's frequency or phase to the paper event.

branches.condition: No exact joint state is observed and both exact events plus their joint phase are representation-completely callable
branches.action: Report not observed in N jointly evaluable participants/copies with no-call and phase-missing counts; make no pathogenicity or diagnosis claim.

branches.condition: No exact row is returned but event callability, deletion-aware genotyping, representation reconciliation or phase eligibility is incomplete
branches.action: Report data blocked, not AC=0, absent, private or unphased.

branches.condition: A user asks the browser to establish the patient's phase, classify the alleles, diagnose GSD-Ia, select an embryo or guide PGT
branches.action: Refuse the inference and identify the required external patient, family, assay, clinical and reproductive-specialist evidence.

story.given: an externally validated GRCh37 7,125 bp G6PC1 AluJr/AluSx deletion plus c.326G>A (p.Cys109Tyr), a reviewed GRCh38 event/transcript remap, and patient/family evidence kept outside the browser

acceptanceTest.fixture: GRCh38 fixtures containing: (A) the exact deletion of bases 42,897,862–42,904,986 represented with a left VCF anchor and linked to retained-flank/junction hashes; (B) an Alu-homology-shifted but junction-equivalent representation of A; (C) a similar 7.1 kb G6PC1/Alu deletion with different retained flanks; (D) exact 42,904,026G>A; (E) participant REF001 with A on copy A and D on copy B under one compatible phase receipt; (F) REF002 carrying both exact events with missing/incompatible PS; (G) an impossible same-copy deletion-plus-D assignment; and (H) explicit event-callable, point-callable, jointly phase-evaluable and no-call copies. Keep paper-patient segregation and PGT metadata in a separate inaccessible fixture.
acceptanceTest.actions: Load the reviewed GRCh37-to-GRCh38 remap; open the 20 kb region; enumerate all source rows/ALTs; canonicalize A/B by junction and retained flanks; keep C overlap-only; match D by transcript/genomic identity; join same-sample carriers; require opposite copies plus compatible PS; run the deletion-aware consistency check; compute event and joint denominators; attempt patient-phase/diagnosis/PGT inferences; export and reload the receipt.
acceptanceTest.expected: A/B collapse to one exact deletion event without double counting; C remains non-equivalent; D is exact; REF001 is labeled trans for REF001 only; REF002 is co-carried/phase unresolved; G fails closed as a copy-number/genotype inconsistency; occurrence and non-observation use exact-event and joint callable counts with no-calls; the reloaded receipt reconstructs source/remap, event normalization, carrier/copy/PS edges, denominators, provenance and stop rules exactly.
acceptanceTest.forbidden: The result must not match by gene, size, Alu mechanism, one breakpoint or overlap alone; treat source_variant_id as an event ID; equate same-participant carriage with trans; call copy 1/2 maternal/paternal; permit the point ALT on the deleted copy without a validated complex CN architecture; borrow nearby AN or depth as event callability; convert missingness to zero; transfer reference phase to the patient; classify either allele; diagnose GSD-Ia; or guide PGT/embryo selection.

evidence.claim: Four long reads supported an initial GRCh37 call chr17:g.41049904_41057049del7146, with slightly discordant breakpoints. evidence.claim: The final deletion removes the 5′ regulatory sequence, exon 1, intron 1, exon 2 and part of intron 2. Its 5′ breakpoint is in AluJr and 3′ breakpoint in AluSx; Fig. 3 shows the joined retained flanks and supports an Alu/Alu recombination mechanism.

evidence.claim: WES reported c.326G>A (p.C109Y) as apparently homozygous, but Sanger found the mother heterozygous and the father negative in blood; paternal sperm sequencing for the point allele was inconclusive. evidence.claim: qPCR showed the proband and father carried the heterozygous exon-1/exon-2 deletion while the mother did not; breakpoint PCR produced a 418 bp deletion product in father and proband. evidence.claim: WES exon mean depths were 123, 74, 119, 190 and 259, yet variable exon coverage and intronic breakpoints masked the deletion. The authors state qPCR after WES could detect exon loss but could not identify exact breakpoints; low-coverage ONT breakpoints required Sanger refinement.

evidence.claim: The point coordinate lies inside the 7,125 bp deleted span, 960 bp before its distal deleted base. Therefore a deletion-bearing chromosome cannot also carry that point base in a simple diploid deletion model; exact trans testing must be deletion-aware and a same-copy call is an integrity warning unless a complex CN architecture is proven.

paper.title: Multi-Omic Investigations of a 17–19 Translocation Links MINK1 Disruption to Autism, Epilepsy and Osteoporosis

archetypes: A6 — Balanced and complex structural variation
locus: A de novo cytogenetically balanced reciprocal t(17;19)(p13;p11). The paper's discovery alignment and Figure 1D coordinates are GRCh37/hg19: the two derivative junctions bound chr17:4,778,779–4,778,819 and chr19:27,731,719–27,740,627. The chr17 interval disrupts MINK1 between exons 1 and 2. Read-only chain/reference checks give candidate GRCh38 chr17:4,875,484–4,875,524 and chr19:27,249,719 for only the mappable chr19 endpoint; GRCh37 chr19:27,731,719 does not chain-map, so no exact GRCh38 chr19 interval is publication-ready without a full breakpoint-junction sequence remap.

persona.role: Rare-disease structural-variation researcher or laboratory scientist
persona.context: Research follow-up of a cytogenetically balanced interchromosomal translocation where the repeated population-reference question is exact molecular recurrence, not generic overlap, expression prediction, diagnosis, or causal classification

nonDiagnosticBoundary: This workflow can compare a fully sequence-resolved reciprocal two-junction architecture with represented population-reference events and report whether every required junction was callable. It cannot diagnose a patient, infer phenotype or penetrance in HGSVC/HPRC, transfer patient NESC expression to a population carrier, prove MINK1 haploinsufficiency, or call the translocation causal, pathogenic, benign, or suitable for counseling.

startingState.trigger: A cytogenetic or external long-read result suggests t(17;19)(p13;p11), MINK1 disruption, or a breakend near either paper interval, and the researcher wants to know whether the same reciprocal molecular architecture is represented in the population release.
inputs: Original build and coordinate convention; Nanopore discovery reads were aligned to GRCh37 and the Figure 1D labels are treated as one-based GRCh37/hg19 coordinates

der(17) junction: chr17:4,778,819 joined to chr19:27,731,719 in Figure 1D, with an apparent 26 nt insertion in GRCh37 that maps to chr19 centromeric reference sequence in GRCh38 and becomes a blunt join
der(19) junction: chr19:27,740,627 joined to chr17:4,778,779 in Figure 1D, with two non-reference insertions of 17 nt and 5 nt separated by 8 nt in both GRCh37 and GRCh38 alignments
The bounded GRCh37 breakpoint intervals chr17:4,778,779–4,778,819 and chr19:27,731,719–27,740,627, plus complete retained flanks, junction sequences, orientations and PCR/read support
An event-aware GRCh37-to-GRCh38 remap receipt for both derivative products, including source/target accessions, BLAT or equivalent version, sequence hashes and endpoint convention

Cohort/release/database/run, one two-chromosome query identity, representation-complete BND/CTX reconciliation, per-junction and linked-event AC/AN, callable/no-call counts and centromeric callability rule
Patient NESC RNA-seq and qPCR evidence retained as external paper context, with patient/control/tissue/replicate identity and no join to population participants
startingState.question: Does the population release contain the same pair of reciprocal chr17/chr19 junctions, including derivative orientation and insertion sequence architecture, and were both junctions callable strongly enough to support an observed, not-observed, partial, or data-blocked result?
startingState.stopRule: Stop exact matching when the build, endpoint convention, either derivative junction, orientation, inserted sequence, reciprocal linkage, or GRCh38 event remap is missing. Stop a not-observed claim when either chromosome or representation family is not event-callable. Keep expression external and never treat one nearby BND/CTX, MINK1 overlap, local coverage, or row AC=0 as the balanced event.

before: Freeze paper truth as two derivative products, not one interval: der(17) chr17:4,778,819↔chr19:27,731,719 and der(19) chr19:27,740,627↔chr17:4,778,779 on GRCh37/hg19, with direction, retained sequence and PCR/read evidence.

Retain the paper's base-level qualification of 'balanced': cytogenetically reciprocal and copy-neutral at that resolution, but not a simple two-coordinate swap because the derivative junctions use 40 bp and 8,908 bp breakpoint intervals and der(19) contains 17 nt and 5 nt insertions separated by 8 nt.

Validate complete altered-junction sequences against pinned GRCh37 and GRCh38 accessions. A coordinate-only chain result is provisional: both chr17 endpoints and only chr19:27,740,627 map cleanly, while chr19:27,731,719 does not chain-map.

Define exact equivalence before searching: both reciprocal derivative junctions, compatible retained flanks, partner chromosome, orientation, insertion sequence/canonicalization and one-event linkage must agree. One breakend, an interval overlap, a MINK1-disrupting record, or two unlinked local records is candidate evidence only.

Create a synchronized two-chromosome query state around the validated GRCh38 chr17 and chr19 junctions. Block a one-window publication because current workflow state can carry only one browserRegion and the chr19 interval is not fully remapped.
inside: Verify GRCh38, HGSVC/HPRC, accepted full-chromosome primary runs and ancillary availability independently on chr17 and chr19, but retain one analysis/query receipt across both views.

Enumerate BND, CTX, OTH, CPX, INV, INS, DEL, DUP and split representations at both loci. Preserve source_variant_id and ALT index, but do not infer mate identity from a source ID, shared type, overlap, or display grouping.

Apply tiered matching: generic breakend overlap; one compatible derivative junction; two unlinked compatible junctions; and exact reciprocal linked architecture. Only the last tier is an exact comparable event.

Gate centromeric callability separately from ordinary depth. Require representation-complete mapping and callable evidence for both sides of both derivative junctions; mean depth or percent-over-threshold at one coordinate is not an event-negative denominator.

Report component-junction AC/AN and no-calls separately from the linked-event count. A linked-event denominator may include only participants whose two derivative junctions and linking representation are callable; do not synthesize event AN from independent chr17 and chr19 row AN values.

Display the paper's RNA-seq/qPCR result only in an external patient-evidence panel: patient-derived NESCs versus three unrelated healthy controls, three replicates per individual, RNA-seq log2 fold change −0.92 with p=1.1×10^−11, and qPCR validation. Never calculate or imply expression for a population carrier.
after: Export original and remapped coordinates, endpoint convention, both derivative junction sequences and hashes, inserted-sequence canonicalization, all candidate records/ALT indexes, partner/orientation/linkage evidence, centromeric callability, exact-versus-partial classification, per-junction AC/AN, linked-event callable/no-call counts, release/database/run, both query windows, timestamp and browser state.

Hand the bounded architecture result back for patient-specific transcript, expression, segregation, functional and clinical interpretation outside the browser. Preserve the NESC/qPCR evidence and the authors' MINK1 hypothesis as single-patient external evidence, not a population-browser observable or causal label.

branches.condition: The original build, endpoint convention, complete BPJ sequences or event-aware GRCh38 remap is missing
branches.action: Report remap/data-blocked and list the missing derivative evidence; do not navigate from a coordinate-only chr17 window as if it represented the complete event.

branches.condition: A record overlaps MINK1 or one paper breakpoint but has no validated chr19 partner, reciprocal mate, orientation or junction sequence
branches.action: Report generic breakend or gene-overlap candidate only; do not call exact recurrence.

branches.condition: Both loci contain compatible records but the two derivative products are not linked to one source event/participant
branches.action: Report two unlinked candidates and keep the reciprocal architecture unresolved.

branches.condition: Both reciprocal derivative junctions, partner chromosomes, orientations, retained flanks and insertion architecture match under one event identity
branches.action: Report an exact comparable reciprocal architecture with per-junction and linked-event counts, callability and provenance; make no expression, phenotype or causal claim.

branches.condition: Both reciprocal joins match but copy-number evidence shows gain/loss beyond the explicitly normalized small junction sequence
branches.action: Report a sequence-related unbalanced or complex architecture, not the paper's cytogenetically balanced architecture.

branches.condition: No exact linked event is observed and every required representation and both derivative junctions are callable for N participant-genomes
branches.action: Report not observed in N event-callable participant-genomes, with per-junction chromosome-copy AC/AN, no-calls and a conditional upper reference-frequency statement.

branches.condition: No exact linked event is returned but the centromeric join, mate linkage, representation family or denominator is incomplete
branches.action: Report data-blocked, not AC=0 and not absent.

branches.condition: A population event is observed and the user requests MINK1 expression, phenotype, pathogenicity or diagnosis
branches.action: Keep the population architecture result separate and hand off to external patient-specific molecular and clinical review.

story.given: a GRCh37 t(17;19) result represented by both paper derivative junctions, their bounded chr17/chr19 intervals, retained flanks, insertion architecture and an external patient-NESC expression result
story.when: the researcher validates both altered-junction mappings to GRCh38, opens synchronized accepted chr17 and chr19 views, reconciles every BND/CTX/split representation into one reciprocal event, and audits centromeric event callability
story.then: the browser returns exact reciprocal architecture, one-junction/generic overlap, unlinked candidate pair, architecture-distinct complex event, not observed in N event-callable participant-genomes, or data-blocked, with complete provenance and with expression remaining external patient evidence

browserRegionBlockedReason: No one-region link can represent a reciprocal chr17/chr19 event, current workflow state has only one browserRegion, and the chr19 GRCh37 endpoint 27,731,719 does not coordinate-chain-map to GRCh38. Candidate chr17 GRCh38 4,875,484–4,875,524 is useful only as one synchronized component; publication requires an event-aware remap of both complete derivative junctions and a paired-region receipt.

capabilities.step: Navigate to the MINK1-side candidate window and verify accepted chr17 provenance
capabilities.evidence: On 2026-08-11 the candidate chr17 route and API returned HTTP 200 with accepted GRCh38 full-chromosome primary and haplotype provenance. This proves one-locus serviceability, not the reciprocal event.

capabilities.step: Validate exact GRCh37-to-GRCh38 breakpoint-junction mappings
capabilities.evidence: Read-only UCSC chain/reference checks map chr17:4,778,779–4,778,819 to candidate GRCh38 chr17:4,875,484–4,875,524 and map chr19:27,740,627 to chr19:27,249,719 with identical 201 bp context. chr19:27,731,719 has no chain result; the paper says its apparent GRCh37 26 nt insertion is chr19 reference in GRCh38, so full altered-junction sequence alignment is mandatory.

capabilities.step: Keep chr17 and chr19 windows synchronized as one linked-event query and share/export that state
capabilities.evidence: Current LiteratureWorkflow has one browserRegion or a blocked state, region URLs carry one interval, and neither the LongReadVariant GraphQL contract nor the UI defines a paired-chromosome event/mate receipt.

capabilities.step: Find generic local breakend/translocation candidates
capabilities.evidence: The UI normalizes BND and CTX into Other/BND/CTX and local search can filter those types, but the API exposes only one chrom/pos/end plus REF/ALT/source identity and frequencies; it has no explicit partner chromosome, mate/event ID, derivative orientation or junction field.

capabilities.step: Distinguish the exact balanced reciprocal architecture from generic overlap
capabilities.evidence: Source-event display grouping is chromosome-local and interval-keyed, and source_variant_id is explicitly not a guaranteed event ID. Exact recurrence needs two derivative joins, partner/orientation/insertion sequence and one-event linkage that the current contract cannot express.

capabilities.step: Establish representation-complete centromeric callability
capabilities.evidence: Live chr19 coverage in the 27.22–27.27 Mb candidate neighborhood has 20,875 consecutive zero-mean bins followed by high-depth bins; only one paper chr19 endpoint chain-maps. Coverage percentages are not paired-junction callability, so neither safe absence nor a linked-event AN can be computed.

capabilities.step: Conclude exact occurrence or safe absence in HGSVC/HPRC
capabilities.evidence: The live chr17 candidate window had 1,016 records and no BND/CTX/INV/CPX or >=1 kb structural record; the chr19 candidate window had 1,884 records, including ten local >=1 kb INS/DEL/DUP records but no BND/CTX. The API cannot prove reciprocal representation completeness or linkage, so this is data-blocked rather than not observed.

capabilities.step: Use patient NESC RNA-seq/qPCR as population-carrier evidence
capabilities.evidence: The expression result is from one patient's iPSC-derived NESCs versus three unrelated healthy controls. No HGSVC/HPRC expression layer, patient identity join or validated phenotype layer exists; expression must remain external.

capabilities.step: Open a curated MINK1 detailed-workflow page
capabilities.evidence: Production returned HTTP 404 for this slug. Current source commit 7c8c7b97 contains 20 detailed records through Batch 2 and no ref-98 record.

capabilities.step: Infer MINK1 haploinsufficiency, phenotype or clinical classification from a population event
capabilities.evidence: The paper is a single-patient study; allele-specific expression was impossible, no aberrant MINK1 transcript was detected, and the causal interpretation is explicitly a hypothesis/candidate-gene argument requiring further study.

acceptanceTest.fixture: GRCh38 fixtures containing: (A) the exact der(17) and der(19) junction sequences as one reciprocal event, including normalized GRCh37/GRCh38 representation of the der(17) 26 nt segment and the der(19) 17 nt + 8 nt + 5 nt architecture; (B) one MINK1-side BND with no chr19 mate; (C) compatible chr17 and chr19 records in different participants/events; (D) both joins linked but with additional copy gain/loss; (E) generic local BND/CTX overlap with different partners/orientations; and (F) a representation-complete no-event set with explicit callable and no-call participant-genomes at every required junction. Keep patient NESC RNA-seq/qPCR in a separate external-evidence fixture.
acceptanceTest.actions: Attempt a one-window MINK1 link and require it to fail closed; load a pinned two-junction remap receipt; open and share synchronized chr17/chr19 views; enumerate every ALT and BND/CTX/split representation; match partner/orientation/junction sequence and linkage; audit centromeric callability, per-junction AC/AN and linked-event callable/no-call participant counts; attempt to attach the paper's expression result to a population carrier; export and reload the analysis receipt.
acceptanceTest.expected: A is one exact reciprocal architecture despite build-specific normalization. B is one-junction partial, C is an unlinked candidate pair, D is architecture-related but unbalanced/complex, E is generic overlap only, and F may report not observed only with complete two-junction representation and event callability. The patient expression panel stays external and unjoined. Reloading reconstructs both windows, both derivative sequences, mappings, component identities, classifications, denominators and provenance exactly.
acceptanceTest.forbidden: The result must not call a MINK1 overlap, one BND, two unlinked BNDs, a source-ID prefix, local depth, or a cytogenetic label an exact balanced event; convert a missing mate or centromeric no-call to reference/zero; synthesize linked-event AN from independent row AN; treat technical/within-individual RNA replicates as independent people; assign reduced expression or phenotype to a population carrier; or label the architecture causal, pathogenic, benign, diagnostic, penetrant or suitable for counseling.

evidence.claim: The male patient had a de novo 46,XY,t(17;19)(p13;p11) described as a balanced reciprocal translocation; the report is one patient, not a cohort recurrence or penetrance study.
evidence.citation: PDF p. 2, Clinical Findings; p. 7, Conclusions

evidence.claim: Nanopore PromethION lrGS was the only tested technology that resolved the breakpoint junctions. The discovery data were about 3× coverage, aligned to GRCh37 with Minimap2, called with Sniffles at minimum three-read support, and BPJs were validated by breakpoint PCR; srGS, linked reads and optical mapping did not resolve the event.
evidence.citation: PDF pp. 2–3, Genomic Analyses and Fig. 1; pp. 5–6, Discussion and Genome Analysis methods

evidence.claim: Figure 1D labels the der(17) join as chr17:4,778,819 with chr19:27,731,719 and the der(19) join as chr19:27,740,627 with chr17:4,778,779. Because discovery aligned to GRCh37, these define GRCh37/hg19 breakpoint intervals chr17:4,778,779–4,778,819 and chr19:27,731,719–27,740,627.
evidence.citation: PDF p. 3, Fig. 1D; p. 6, Genome Analysis methods

evidence.claim: The der(17) breakpoint disrupts MINK1 between exons 1 and 2; the reciprocal der(19) breakpoint lies inside the chromosome 19 centromere.
evidence.citation: PDF abstract and p. 3, Genomic Analyses/Fig. 1B–D

evidence.claim: When BPJ sequences were aligned to GRCh37 and GRCh38, the der(17) apparent 26 nt random insertion in GRCh37 mapped to chr19 centromeric reference sequence in GRCh38 and the join became blunt. The der(19) retained two random insertions of 17 nt and 5 nt separated by 8 nt in both builds.
evidence.citation: PDF pp. 3–5, Genomic Analyses, Fig. 1D and Discussion

evidence.claim: RNA-seq of patient-derived NESCs versus three unrelated healthy controls found 539 differentially expressed genes, including MINK1 at p=1.1×10^−11 and log2 fold change −0.92; qPCR significantly validated downregulation. Each individual had three replicates with 44 million 150 bp paired reads per replicate.
evidence.citation: PDF p. 4, RNA-Seq of Neural Stem Cells and Fig. 2A; p. 6, Neural Stem Cell Cultivation and Transcriptome Sequencing

evidence.claim: The paper found no other differentially expressed gene within 1 Mb of the translocation breakpoints. GTEx showed healthy-tissue median MINK1 expression of 142.6 TPM in cerebellum and 89.25 TPM in cortex.
evidence.citation: PDF p. 4, RNA-Seq of Neural Stem Cells and Fig. 2B

evidence.claim: Allele-specific MINK1 expression could not be tested because there were no informative heterozygous SNVs, and no aberrant MINK1 transcripts were detected. The authors interpreted this as affected-allele nonsense-mediated decay, but direct allele assignment was unavailable.
evidence.citation: PDF p. 4, RNA-Seq of Neural Stem Cells

evidence.claim: The authors call MINK1 a candidate gene and hypothesize haploinsufficiency, while stating that it remains unknown whether all or only some clinical features share one etiology; they also refrain from assigning a formation mechanism because centromeric reference shortcomings prevent complete BPJ characterization.
evidence.citation: PDF p. 5, Discussion; p. 7, Conclusions

evidence.claim: 'Balanced' is a cytogenetic/reciprocal classification, not proof of nucleotide-perfect copy neutrality. Exact comparison must retain both derivative junctions and their build-dependent insertions rather than reducing the event to one BND or two nominal breakpoint positions.
evidence.citation: Analyst reconstruction from PDF Fig. 1D and BPJ discussion; requires paper-truth/workflow review

evidence.claim: UCSC hg19ToHg38 chain SHA-256 5c0598e500ceb5a78c73086929e8ef993aec309bcafb595139b53d440b125a1d maps the chr17 interval to candidate GRCh38 chr17:4,875,484–4,875,524 and chr19:27,740,627 to candidate chr19:27,249,719 with identical 201 bp contexts. chr19:27,731,719 does not chain-map, so an exact GRCh38 interval cannot be published from independent coordinate liftover.
evidence.citation: Read-only UCSC chain/API reference-context check, 2026-08-11; details in cited evidence markdown

evidence.claim: A fully comparable event requires two derivative junctions with partner, orientation, retained-flank and insertion-sequence compatibility plus one-event/participant linkage. Generic BND overlap, MINK1 disruption alone, or two unlinked local records are lower evidence tiers.
evidence.citation: Analyst reconstruction from paper architecture and current GraphQL/source-event semantics; requires workflow/data-semantics review

evidence.claim: RNA-seq log2 fold change −0.92 corresponds to about 0.529× control expression (about 47% lower); this is close to, but not literally greater than, a 50% reduction. The abstract's >50% language and qPCR validation should be preserved separately rather than collapsed into one exact effect estimate.
evidence.citation: Analyst calculation from PDF abstract and p. 4 RNA-seq result; requires paper-truth review

evidence.claim: The expression evidence is tissue/model- and participant-specific: one patient's iPSC-derived NESCs versus three unrelated controls. Three replicates per individual improve assay precision but do not create twelve independent people, and the lack of allele-specific markers prevents direct assignment of reduced expression to the disrupted allele.
evidence.citation: Analyst uncertainty boundary from PDF pp. 4 and 6; requires data-semantics/safety review

evidence.claim: For this interchromosomal event, retain per-junction chromosome-copy AC/AN and separately count participant-genomes callable for both linked derivative junctions. Independent chr17 and chr19 row AN values cannot be merged into a reciprocal-event denominator.
evidence.citation: Analyst denominator contract; requires data-semantics review

evidence.claim: On 2026-08-11 the accepted GRCh38 chr17 candidate window returned 1,016 rows (520 SNV, 293 TRV, 102 INS, 95 DEL, 6 DUP) and no BND/CTX/INV/CPX or >=1 kb structural row. This is a local record observation, not an exact-event negative result.
evidence.citation: Read-only production GraphQL query against gnomad-lr-api-00018-xoz, 2026-08-11

evidence.claim: The GRCh38 chr19 27.22–27.27 Mb candidate neighborhood returned 1,884 rows, including ten local >=1 kb INS/DEL/DUP rows but no BND/CTX. Mean coverage was zero across 20,875 consecutive positions (27,220,000–27,240,874) and high at the cleanly mapped endpoint chr19:27,249,719; this heterogeneity plus incomplete remap blocks centromeric event callability.
evidence.citation: Read-only production GraphQL variant and lr_coverage queries against gnomad-lr-api-00018-xoz, 2026-08-11

evidence.claim: Production provenance reports accepted full-chromosome HGSVC/HPRC primary and haplotype sources for chr17 and chr19 in database gnomad_lr_y1_scratch_demo_full_genome_20260803, with runs y1-full-prototype-hgsvc-hprc-chr17-20260728-r1 and y1-full-prototype-hgsvc-hprc-chr19-20260728-r1; independent region routes return HTTP 200.
evidence.citation: Read-only production provenance and route checks, 2026-08-11

evidence.claim: Current source commit 7c8c7b97 exposes local chrom/pos/end/REF/ALT/type/source IDs and frequencies, displays BND/CTX as Other/BND/CTX, and groups source events by chromosome-local exact interval. It exposes no partner chromosome, MATEID/EVENT, derivative orientation, junction sequence or paired-region receipt; source_variant_id is not guaranteed event identity.
evidence.citation: Current source: long-read-variant.graphql, longReadVariantTypes.ts and sourceEventAggregation.ts, 2026-08-11

evidence.claim: Current source contains 20 detailed workflow records through Batch 2 and no ref 98; production gnomad-lr-browser-00012-suv returns HTTP 404 for /long-read-literature-examples/paper/mink1-balanced-translocation.
evidence.citation: Current record inventory and read-only production route check, 2026-08-11

capabilityBasis: Read-only Batch-3 manifest, complete nine-page PDF (SHA-256 0118c4a205be75275e09f4ae678707f5873a679e24800487e97e266c488ea19f), shared workflow schema, implemented record shape/current records, current source commit 7c8c7b97490641838de9585d0e100c9eef830c57, UCSC chain/reference context and production browser/API checks on 2026-08-11. Deployed revisions were gnomad-lr-api-00018-xoz and gnomad-lr-browser-00012-suv. Independent route success, local row absence and ordinary depth do not establish reciprocal junction equivalence, centromeric event callability, expression, phenotype or safe absence.

paper.title: Integration of transcriptomics and long-read genomics prioritizes structural variants in rare disease

locus: Genome-wide UDN rare-SV workflow; strongest concrete LRS example is two FAM177A1 deletions affecting the 5′ UTR–CDS and 3′ CDS–UTR in trans. The analysis used GRCh38 patch 13, but the local paper gives no exact breakpoints, lengths, event IDs, or coordinate-level FAM177A1 notation; unmapped/no CTA.

persona.role: Rare-disease genomics researcher or molecular laboratory scientist
persona.context: Research prioritization after long-read SV discovery has produced hundreds of rare candidates and matched-tissue RNA-seq is available or planned outside the population browser

nonDiagnosticBoundary: This workflow can report whether one fully specified SV is exactly represented, only overlaps a population event, is not observed among event-callable chromosome copies, or is data blocked, with AC/AN, missingness, ancestry strata, and provenance. It cannot reproduce Watershed-SV, host patient RNA-seq, rank a genome, infer an expression effect, classify pathogenicity/benignity, diagnose a participant, or treat non-observation in 292 reference participants as pathogenic evidence.

startingState.trigger: An external long-read pipeline has produced a candidate rare SV or a genome-wide candidate list for downstream expression-aware prioritization.
inputs: For each candidate: source reference accession/build, chromosome, normalized breakpoints and endpoint convention, SV type, REF/ALT or inserted sequence when resolved, orientation, length, constituent records, caller/merge identity, genotype, phase/linkage evidence, and QC/callability status
A predeclared exact-equivalence rule appropriate to the SV class and a separate candidate-overlap rule; the paper's SVAFotate 0.5 overlap setting is not an exact-event rule
Population cohort/release/database/run/caller/source identity and a representation-complete event-callability rule
Callable chromosome-copy AN, exact-event AC, no-call/unassessed/representation-mismatch counts, participant count, ploidy, and ancestry strata
An immutable export receipt carrying the normalized query, all returned records, match tier, denominator, missingness, provenance, timestamp, and software/rule versions

External matched-tissue RNA-seq, tissue/control cohort, normalization/covariate model, expression z-scores, Watershed-SV/model version, HPO inputs, and independent validation evidence; none is supplied by the browser
Paper comparator context: 571 technology-matched control long-read genomes, UDN n=68, MAF < 0.01, and a same-workflow Jasmine population merge
Selected paper example: two FAM177A1 deletions in trans with Watershed-SV posteriors >0.9 and fibroblast under-expression, but no exact event coordinates in the local paper
startingState.question: For each fully specified external SV, is the same normalized event observed in the selected long-read population release, is only a non-equivalent overlap observed, or is a qualified non-observation possible after explicit callability and missingness accounting, before transcriptomic prioritization proceeds externally?
startingState.stopRule: Do not emit a region CTA or query the selected FAM177A1 example until exact event coordinates and build-normalized boundaries are available. For any candidate, stop before rare/not-observed claims if exact equivalence, representation reconciliation, event-specific callable AN, or missingness is unavailable; stop before functional or clinical interpretation because transcriptomics and patient evidence are external.

before: Freeze the source candidate and provenance. Keep one object per biological event even if it has several VCF records; retain all breakpoints, sequences, orientations, phase links, caller support, and unresolved fields.

Normalize to a pinned reference accession and declare exact equivalence before population search. For deletions this normally requires type and both sequence-compatible boundaries; insertions require anchor plus complete inserted sequence/structure when available; inversions and complex events require all linked junctions, orientation, and components.

Define overlap separately as a candidate-retrieval operation, with its reciprocal-overlap/breakpoint-distance rule and version. Never allow generic gene, interval, or 50% overlap to satisfy exact equivalence.

For the paper exemplar, retain FAM177A1, two deletion regions (5′ UTR–CDS and 3′ CDS–UTR), in-trans phase, posterior >0.9, and fibroblast under-expression as paper facts, but keep browserRegion null because exact breakpoints, lengths, IDs, and coordinate notation are absent.

Record panel limitations in advance: HGSVC/HPRC has 292 participants and at most 584 callable autosomal chromosome copies before missingness, smaller than the paper's 571-control panel and its merged UDN/reference frequency cohort. Require ancestry-specific denominators rather than treating 292 as one homogeneous panel.
inside: After a candidate has exact build-normalized coordinates, open the smallest safe region and attest reference build, cohort, release, accepted run, source caller/representation, and query scope.

Enumerate every exact and overlapping source record/ALT. Reconcile normalization-equivalent records without double counting, but preserve shifted, split, multi-allelic, insertion, BND, and complex representations until event identity is proven.

Apply the exact predicate first and the overlap predicate second. Report mutually exclusive tiers: exact represented event; normalization-equivalent exact event; overlap-only candidate; representation mismatch; event-callable not observed; or data blocked.

For an exact represented event, show event AC and callable AN, AF, no-call/unassessed copies, participant count, ploidy, ancestry strata, source IDs/ALT indexes, matching rule, release/run/database, and query timestamp. A row-level AN is acceptable only if it is proven to be the callable denominator for the complete biological event.

For no exact event, issue 'not observed in N callable chromosome copies' only when every representation and breakpoint required by the exact predicate is callable. Otherwise report data blocked; nearby-record AN, aggregate coverage, 292 participants, or 584 nominal copies cannot fill the denominator.

Do not label AF < 0.01 as case-specific pathogenic evidence. With at most 584 nominal autosomal copies, one observed copy is about 0.0017 before missingness, and ancestry-specific strata are much smaller; display uncertainty and do not claim the paper's filtering power has been reproduced.

Export one immutable population-frequency receipt per candidate. The receipt must preserve both exact and overlap results, constituent records, denominator and missingness accounting, panel strata, complete provenance, filters, rule versions, query payload, timestamp, and a hash.
after: Join the exported population receipt to transcriptomics outside the browser. Use matched blood or fibroblast RNA-seq, tissue-matched controls, RNA QC, batch/RIN/sex/hidden-factor correction, and a pinned expression-outlier/model pipeline.
Treat expression outlier, HPO, CADD-SV, regulatory annotation, segregation, and orthogonal validation as independent evidence classes. Population rarity is one filter, not the functional conclusion.

Return candidates for expert research review with all negative and data-blocked branches visible. Preserve the paper's FAM177A1 interpretation as motivating evidence, not a diagnosis or a transferable classification.

branches.condition: The paper/example or external candidate lacks exact build-normalized event coordinates, boundaries, or representation
branches.action: Keep the workflow genome-wide/unmapped with no browser CTA; list the missing fields and do not substitute a gene-centered region.

branches.condition: A normalization-equivalent event satisfies the full exact predicate
branches.action: Report exact population-reference occurrence once, with constituent representations, event AC/callable AN, missingness, strata, and provenance; do not infer function or clinical significance.

branches.condition: Only interval, gene, or one-breakpoint overlap is observed, or event linkage/sequence/orientation differs
branches.action: Report overlap-only candidate or representation mismatch and preserve the exact-versus-overlap rule; do not transfer the overlapping row's AF to the source event.

branches.condition: No exact event is returned and every required representation and breakpoint is event-callable
branches.action: Report 'not observed in N callable chromosome copies' with no-call counts, strata, release scope, and uncertainty; do not call the event private or pathogenic.

branches.condition: No exact event is returned but event-specific callability, representation reconciliation, or missingness is incomplete
branches.action: Report data blocked, not AC=0, absent, private, or MAF < 0.01.

branches.condition: Exact-event AF is at or above 0.01 in the selected release
branches.action: Report that the candidate does not pass this release-specific paper-inspired rarity filter, with uncertainty and strata; do not call it benign or exclude disease relevance.

branches.condition: Exact-event AF estimate is below 0.01 with adequate callable AN
branches.action: Report that it passes a release-specific population rarity filter and export the receipt for external transcriptomic review; do not call it functional, causal, or diagnostic.

branches.condition: Matched-tissue RNA-seq or a valid external expression comparator is unavailable
branches.action: Stop after the population receipt and label expression-aware prioritization unavailable; do not infer an outlier from genomic annotation alone.

branches.condition: External transcriptomics identifies a candidate gene expression outlier and a pinned model prioritizes the gene–SV pair
branches.action: Return a research-prioritization result for orthogonal validation, segregation, and expert review; keep the population observation, transcriptomic signal, and clinical interpretation separate.

story.given: a genome-wide external long-read SV list with pinned GRCh38 event definitions, QC and phase evidence, plus a selected population release and optional matched-tissue RNA-seq
story.when: the researcher queries each event using separate exact and overlap predicates, conditions AC on event-callable AN and explicit missingness, exports a provenance-complete population receipt, and only then joins that receipt to tissue-matched expression-outlier evidence outside the browser
story.then: each candidate is labeled exact represented, overlap-only/representation-mismatched, not observed in N callable copies, or data blocked; the external analysis may prioritize but not diagnose, and the coordinate-incomplete FAM177A1 paper example remains a no-CTA motivating example

browserRegionBlockedReason: The paper is a genome-wide workflow and its strongest concrete LRS example, the two in-trans FAM177A1 deletions, has no exact breakpoints, lengths, event IDs, or coordinate-level notation in the local 55-page PDF. Although the calling pipeline used GRCh38 patch 13, a gene label/build alone is not an event query. Emit no browser CTA until a machine-readable event record or supplementary table supplies exact coordinates and passes normalization review.

capabilities.step: Represent a genome-wide/unmapped literature workflow without a misleading region CTA
capabilities.evidence: The current LiteratureWorkflow type accepts browserRegion=null only with browserRegionBlockedReason, and literatureWorkflowBrowserPath returns null. Four of 20 current records already use this fail-closed pattern.

capabilities.step: Upload or evaluate a genome-wide list of hundreds of external SV candidates as one analysis
capabilities.evidence: Current LR navigation and search are region/record oriented; the literature workflow model stores one optional region and has no genome-wide candidate-list intake, batch matcher, or per-genome prioritization workbench.

capabilities.step: Retrieve exact identifiers, positions, REF/ALT, and generic overlaps for one mapped candidate
capabilities.evidence: Current search supports exact identifier/VCF terms and range overlap, but comma/newline terms are OR. It cannot express all-breakpoint/event-linkage predicates for an arbitrary SV list.

capabilities.step: Keep exact-event equivalence separate from generic interval overlap
capabilities.evidence: Source-event aggregation deliberately refuses overlap as identity and groups by normalized family plus exact anchor/interval, which is a safe baseline, but source_variant_id is not a guaranteed event ID and the GraphQL contract lacks mate, orientation, linked components, and event-callability fields.

capabilities.step: Display per-record cohort and ancestry AC/AN/AF with source release/run fields
capabilities.evidence: LongReadVariant exposes global and population AC/AN/AF plus cohort, data source, source release, and source run ID. These values remain per record/ALT unless event reconciliation proves otherwise.

capabilities.step: Distinguish event-callable non-observation from missing/no-call representation
capabilities.evidence: The API has no event-specific callable/no-call counts when no matching record exists and no complete-event callability contract for split or complex SVs. Nominal 292 participants, nearby row AN, and aggregate coverage are not substitutes.

capabilities.step: Reproduce the paper's 571-control same-technology rarity filter with HGSVC/HPRC N=292
capabilities.evidence: The current HGSVC/HPRC panel has 292 participants (at most 584 nominal autosomal copies before no-calls), roughly half the paper's control-genome count, and cannot reproduce its same-pipeline 571-control plus UDN population merge or its ancestry power.

capabilities.step: Export an immutable exact/overlap frequency receipt with AC/AN, missingness, strata, rule, and full provenance
capabilities.evidence: The haplotype CSV exports LR AF, groups/carriers, selected population AFs and annotations, but omits AC, AN, no-call/missing counts, source release/run, query/rule identity, and a receipt hash.

capabilities.step: Join population results to blood/fibroblast expression outliers or run Watershed-SV
capabilities.evidence: Current LR variant and workflow records have no transcriptomic samples, expression z-scores, GTEx normalization, Watershed-SV posterior, HPO join, or external-evidence receipt.

capabilities.step: Use rarity or expression prioritization to diagnose, classify pathogenicity, or infer participant phenotype
