acceptanceTest.fixture: A pinned GRCh38 external candidate set containing: (A) one exact deletion represented once; (B) the same biological deletion in a normalization-equivalent shifted record that must not be double counted; (C) a reciprocal-overlap event with different breakpoints; (D) a fully event-callable locus with no exact event; (E) a locus with one required breakpoint or representation uncallable; and (F) the paper's coordinate-incomplete FAM177A1 two-deletion example. Supply HGSVC/HPRC counts totaling no more than 292 participants/584 nominal autosomal copies, explicit callable and no-call copies, uneven ancestry strata, accepted release/run provenance, and a separate external RNA fixture with tissue, controls, z-scores, model version and posteriors.
acceptanceTest.actions: Attempt to navigate fixture F; query A–E with separately declared exact and overlap rules; expand all source ALTs/components; reconcile A/B; inspect global and stratum AC/AN, missingness, participant counts and provenance; request MAF < 0.01 and non-observation statements; export and reload the population receipt; then join the receipt to the external RNA fixture and attempt a diagnostic conclusion.
acceptanceTest.expected: F remains unmapped and emits no CTA. A/B collapse to one exact event and one AC accounting unit while preserving both representations. C is overlap-only and its AF is not transferred to the source event. D says not observed in N event-callable copies with uncertainty. E says data blocked, never zero. Every output labels N=292 and the smaller ancestry denominators, and the export reloads identical rules, records, AC/AN, no-calls, release/run/query state and hash. The RNA join remains external and yields research prioritization only.
acceptanceTest.forbidden: The workflow must not invent FAM177A1 coordinates, substitute a gene-centered CTA, equate 50% overlap with exact identity, double count normalization-equivalent records, use 292 participants or 584 nominal copies as callable AN without evidence, convert missingness to reference, call an unobserved event private/pathogenic, claim parity with the paper's 571-control filtering, import expression or phenotype into population participants, or label any candidate causal, benign, pathogenic, diagnostic, or suitable for clinical action.

evidence.claim: The study sequenced 68 UDN individuals (57 affected and 11 unaffected family members) after negative or inconclusive short-read testing; median aligned coverage was 18× (range 7.1–33×), median N50 19.2 kb, and reads aligned to GRCh38.
evidence.citation: Local PDF pp. 2, 5–6, Abstract, cohort results and Fig. 1

evidence.claim: LRS SVs were aligned to GRCh38 patch 13 (GCF_000001405.39), called with Sniffles2, cuteSV and SVIM, merged with Jasmine v1.1.5, required support from at least two callers, and used Iris insertion refinement.
evidence.citation: Local PDF pp. 28–30, Methods: LRS Structural Variant Calling

evidence.claim: For long-read frequency estimation, the authors used a technology-matched ADRC/SAMS nanopore control collection reported as n=571, ran an identical SV-calling workflow, merged controls with UDN using Jasmine, and estimated AF from merged allele counts; rare was MAF < 0.01.
evidence.citation: Local PDF pp. 10–11 and 31, Long-read population references and Allele Frequency Estimation

evidence.claim: The paper's control counts are internally inconsistent: prose/abstract use 571, Fig. 1 says 579, Fig. 2 approximately 600, and Methods says ADRC contains 598 while also reporting 667 total merged genomes. The dossier preserves the requested 571 headline but does not silently reconcile these labels.
evidence.citation: Local PDF pp. 2, 6, 8, 10–11 and 31

evidence.claim: The merged LRS analysis reported 32.6% of variants below MAF 0.01 and a median 716 rare SVs >50 bp per genome; short-read population references would have left over 17,000 candidates, while PARAGRAPH genotyping in 1000G left 3,198, 4.4-fold more than the technology-matched reference.
evidence.citation: Local PDF pp. 10–11, Fig. 2c–d and Long-read population references

evidence.claim: The paper separately reports median LRS burdens of about 546 rare deletions, 490 rare insertions, 11 rare duplications and 2 rare inversions in the broader 30 bp-plus analysis. These subtype medians must not be arithmetically substituted for the separately defined 716 count of SVs >50 bp.
evidence.citation: Local PDF p. 10, Long-read population references; pp. 6–7 size definitions

evidence.claim: Sixty of 68 LRS individuals had RNA-seq, including 42 blood and 27 fibroblast samples. UDN and tissue-matched GTEx were jointly normalized with RIN, sex, batch and expression PCs, yielding a median 139 blood expression outliers per individual.
evidence.citation: Local PDF pp. 12–13, Transcriptome data identifies functional effects; pp. 37–38, outlier methods

evidence.claim: After removal of global expression outliers, the enrichment analysis used 33 individuals with LRS and blood z-scores. Rare SVs within 10 kb of outlier genes were enriched (LOR 0.63, adjusted p=4.8×10^-6); 100 kb analyses evaluated coding, noncoding and regulatory annotations, while 519 putatively non-regulatory rare SVs were not enriched.
evidence.citation: Local PDF pp. 12–16 and 38–40

evidence.claim: Watershed-SV was trained on GTEx v8 short-read SVs and expression outliers, modeled 10 kb and 100 kb gene windows, and outperformed matched WGS-only baselines. The paper therefore did not train the current models on the UDN long-read SV landscape.
evidence.citation: Local PDF pp. 16–19 and 27

evidence.claim: In UDN, 19,277 gene–SV pairs were tested and 886 (4.6%) had posterior at least 0.6; the abstract reports a median eight high-confidence functional SVs per genome. Watershed-SV, CADD-SV, expression and HPO filters produced complementary candidate sets rather than a diagnostic classifier.
evidence.citation: Local PDF pp. 2 and 20–22, Abstract and Watershed-SV prioritizes LRS SVs

evidence.claim: The strongest concrete LRS SV example comprises two deletions in siblings, one affecting the FAM177A1 5′ UTR–CDS region and one the 3′ CDS–UTR region. Both had Watershed-SV posterior >0.9, fibroblast FAM177A1 under-expression, and long-read phase evidence placing them in trans.
evidence.citation: Local PDF pp. 22–26, Fig. 5e–f and case text

evidence.claim: The local paper does not print exact FAM177A1 deletion coordinates, lengths, event IDs, or a coordinate-level event notation. Its Data Access section says harmonized UDN VCFs are in controlled-access dbGaP and top hits are in supplementary table S7, but no machine-readable event table is present in the local PDF.
evidence.citation: Local PDF pp. 22–26 and 47; complete local-text coordinate search

evidence.claim: Study limitations include low-depth approximately 15–18× nanopore data, alignment-based LRS sensitivity limits for some inversions/duplications and deletions above 10 kb, need for larger ancestry-diverse LRS panels and disease-relevant transcriptomes, and Watershed-SV training on SRS GTEx rather than LRS. Future work was proposed for splicing, methylation, proteomics and pedigree transmission.
evidence.citation: Local PDF pp. 7, 26–27, Discussion

evidence.claim: The document is a March 26, 2024 medRxiv preprint explicitly marked not certified by peer review and not for guiding clinical practice.
evidence.citation: Local PDF header and p. 1

evidence.claim: FAM177A1 is the strongest concrete example because it is an LRS-discovered pair of SVs with high posteriors, matched fibroblast under-expression and in-trans phase. It remains a text-only exemplar because gene label plus analysis build is not an exact event locus.
evidence.citation: Analyst selection from paper examples; exact-event and no-CTA gate

evidence.claim: A safe browser contribution is deliberately narrower than the paper: for one already mapped candidate, distinguish exact event from overlap, report occurrence only against event-callable copies, export provenance, then stop before external transcriptomics.
evidence.citation: Analyst reconstruction from paper workflow and current population-browser scope

evidence.claim: For an autosomal event, HGSVC/HPRC N=292 supplies at most 584 nominal chromosome copies before missingness. A single observed copy has nominal AF about 0.0017, but small/uneven ancestry strata, representation failure and no-calls make MAF <0.01 estimates unstable and prevent parity with the paper's larger same-caller merge.
evidence.citation: Analyst denominator calculation and panel limitation; requires data-semantics review

evidence.claim: A zero count may be described only as not observed in N event-callable copies; it is neither proof of population absence nor evidence of pathogenicity. Participant count, nearby variant AN and aggregate coverage are not an event denominator.
evidence.citation: Analyst missingness and safety contract

evidence.claim: The paper's 0.5 overlap option belongs to SVAFotate retrieval against short-read reference catalogs. A population workflow must version overlap as a candidate tier and define exact equivalence separately by both boundaries, sequence/orientation and linkage appropriate to SV class.
evidence.citation: Analyst reconstruction from PDF p. 30–31 SVAFotate methods and event semantics

evidence.claim: The external expression handoff must preserve tissue, controls, RNA QC, covariates, model version, z-score/posterior and candidate-gene relation; importing only a 'high-confidence' label would erase the independent functional-evidence boundary.
evidence.citation: Analyst reproducibility contract based on PDF pp. 12–19 and 37–47

evidence.claim: Current source commit 7c8c7b97490641838de9585d0e100c9eef830c57 contains 20 detailed workflow records and no ref-14 record. The type explicitly supports browserRegion=null plus a blocked reason and returns no browser path for such a record.

evidence.citation: Current graphql-api/src/graphql/types/long-read-variant.graphql, read-only check 2026-08-11

Search range matching is overlap-based and multiple terms are OR, so complete-event matching is underdeveloped.

paper.title: Defining the heterogeneity of unbalanced structural variation underlying breast cancer susceptibility by nanopore genome sequencing

locus: BRCA1/NBR2/LOC101929767 · corrected architecture overview chr17:43,073,282–43,163,674 (GRCh38); the paper’s 1.08 Mb BRCA1 founder-marker core is not fully specified and exceeds this view

persona.role: Structural-variation researcher or molecular genetics laboratory scientist
persona.context: Research comparison after an external assay has identified a BRCA1 exon 1-2 deletion or exon 13 duplication; the browser supplies population-reference architecture and descriptive local haplotype context only.

nonDiagnosticBoundary: Do not diagnose hereditary cancer, assign pathogenicity or benignity, infer penetrance or individual risk, equate exon overlap with recurrence, call descriptive marker similarity proof of identity by descent, treat ancestry labels as biological causes, or turn absence among 292 reference participants into pathogenic evidence. Population-reference evidence cannot diagnose or classify hereditary cancer and does not establish common ancestry.

startingState.trigger: An externally resolved or partially resolved BRCA1 CNV appears recurrent by exon dosage, and the researcher needs to determine whether it has the same linked breakpoints and, separately, whether exact-event carriers have a descriptively similar phased local-marker pattern.
inputs: GRCh38/NC_000017.11 event notation with both boundaries, type, orientation, and coordinate convention
External assay/caller, sample, family, validation, uncertainty, and original clinical exon-level label
Concrete paper event set: three distinct BRCA1 exon 1-2 deletions plus the ins6kbEx13 tandem duplication
Predeclared architecture-match rule and a separate, non-causal marker-similarity rule
Cohort/release/run identity and event-specific callability requirements
Reference/build basis: GRCh38, chromosome accession NC_000017.11; supplementary methods state reads were aligned to GRCh38

Architecture observation unit: Parallel, non-interchangeable units: one exact linked deletion or tandem-duplication event per callable chromosome copy; and one marker-eligible exact-event chromosome copy for descriptive founder similarity.

Architecture callability: An architecture copy is callable only when the accepted source/caller can detect both exact boundaries, type/orientation, and required junction/event linkage, with explicit no-call/representation status. A marker comparison is eligible only when the exact event and every declared marker are callable and linked on the same chromosome copy under a reviewed phase basis across the declared interval. Record AN, local coverage, or deterministic GT placement at unrelated variants is insufficient.

Required counts: Participants queried and maximum possible autosomal chromosome copies Exact P1, P2, P3, and ins6kbEx13 AC and separate event AN Different-architecture, candidate-overlap, partial/unlinked, representation-mismatch, and no-call counts Exact-event carriers eligible for marker comparison Per carrier/template concordant, discordant, missing, and unphased marker counts and covered span Marker-comparison unavailable count by reason Cohort-wide and every displayed stratum AC/AN for each eligible architecture class

Required provenance: reference genome and NC_000017.11 accession source VCF URI, size, checksum, and generation cohort and participant-roster identity database, release, run_id, chromosome scope, and accepted status source_variant_id and alt_index for every constituent event/junction/orientation and phase receipt marker-template version, interval, phase method, and similarity rule query timestamp and receipt hash matching class/rule, UI filters, and ancestry-label source
startingState.question: Does a callable HGSVC/HPRC chromosome copy contain one of the exact paper BRCA1 architectures, and among exact-event carriers is the predeclared local-marker pattern descriptively similar, different, or unavailable?
startingState.stopRule: Stop if any of the following is missing: GRCh38 build and both event boundaries Tandem orientation for the duplication or both deletion boundaries for a deletion A source-event/junction receipt that distinguishes exact architecture from overlap A pinned local-marker interval/list, phase-block receipt, and missing-marker count before founder similarity is reported An event-specific callable denominator before not-observed wording Any missing boundary, absent junction/event linkage, uncertain tandem orientation, representation mismatch, no-call, ambiguous unphased heterozygote, missing marker, broken/unknown phase basis, absent BRCA1 template, or stratum AN=0 is unavailable/data-blocked for that class, not a reference call and not zero.

before: Record the original clinical exon label but normalize each candidate to GRCh38 with both boundaries, orientation, exact type, junction evidence, and uncertainty; keep the four paper architectures separate.
P1 exact rule: both normalized retained-flank/deleted-interval boundaries must form one deletion event; exon 1–2 overlap alone is different architecture.
P2 exact rule: both boundaries, including the distal boundary beyond the generic index window, must match one linked deletion; P1, P3, and generic BRCA1 deletions are not matches.
P3 exact rule: the NBR2-side and BRCA1 intron-2 boundaries must form one 6,649 bp deletion; shared exon dosage is insufficient.

ins6kbEx13 exact rule: both boundaries, the 6,126 bp interval, tandem orientation, and junction/event linkage must match after representation normalization; a point-anchored or differently sized duplication is not exact.
inside: Open chr17:43073282-43163674 in HGSVC/HPRC and verify GRCh38 plus accepted primary/haplotype provenance before inspecting records. Use the corrected region for the four exact architectures; gate the generic 100 kb index window as truncated because it omits the P2 distal boundary.

Reconcile source representations and classify each chromosome copy by exact P1, P2, P3, exact tandem ins6kbEx13, different BRCA1 architecture, candidate overlap, partial representation, or data-blocked. Display matched and missing constituents. A different 17 kb tandem duplication, a 126 bp insertion, or an exon-overlapping deletion never counts as exact recurrence.

Only among exact ins6kbEx13 carriers, compare a pre-reviewed local SNV template on the same chromosome copy and phase block; report descriptive concordance, discordance, missingness, and span without inferring a founder origin. Never substitute nearby variants, the CHEK2 rs986514763 marker, broad ancestry, or visual clustering for the missing BRCA1 template and phase receipt.

Marker comparison unit: marker-eligible exact-event chromosome copy. Compare only predeclared callable markers linked to the exact event under an explicit phase receipt; report concordant, discordant, missing, and unphased counts plus span. No founder yes/no threshold is supplied by the paper.

For each exact architecture and marker-comparison class, report its own callable chromosome-copy denominator, partial/no-call/phase-unavailable counts, global and stratum AC/AN, and source/release/run; describe ancestry labels as sampled metadata only. Never substitute nearby record AN, AN=584, local coverage, or the paper's 19 as an event denominator. Never pool broad reported-ancestry groups into causal founder evidence.

Stratify by Source-provided ancestry group with AC/AN and missingness Cohort/release/run and caller/technology Paper reported ancestry kept separate from browser sample metadata Index versus carrier-testing ascertainment only for the paper cohort, never inferred for HGSVC/HPRC.

Missingness rule: Any missing boundary, absent junction/event linkage, uncertain tandem orientation, representation mismatch, no-call, ambiguous unphased heterozygote, missing marker, broken/unknown phase basis, absent BRCA1 template, or stratum AN=0 is unavailable/data-blocked for that class, not a reference call and not zero.

Uncertainty rule: Only after the relevant exact-event denominator is complete: for AC=0, report the declared exact-binomial method or rule-of-three upper bound. Descriptive marker similarity must report counts/uncertainty and has no paper-derived founder threshold. Current checks do not justify 0/584 for any exact paper event.
The 100,000 bp UI maximum is not biological: the corrected 90,393 bp architecture overview fits, but the paper’s 1.08 Mb founder haplotype does not.
There is no numeric founder-similarity threshold; visual clustering, ancestry labels, or the CHEK2-specific rs986514763 marker cannot substitute for a predeclared BRCA1 comparison.
after: Export paper templates, corrected region, source constituents, exact/overlap labels, marker/phase receipt, denominators, missingness, provenance, P/I/B ledger, and required non-diagnostic wording for structural-variation and statistical-genetics review. Reloading the export must recreate classifications and cautions without screenshots or manuscript prose.

Required export fields: paper DOI/PMID and original/normalized event notation all four event templates, eight boundaries, type, orientation, and coordinate convention corrected region URL and generic-window truncation warning source_variant_ids, ALT indices, types, intervals, junction/mate/event status, and filters exact, different-architecture, overlap, partial, representation-mismatch, and data-blocked labels sample/chromosome-copy identity and phase-set/read linkage status marker template/version, interval, concordant/discordant/missing counts, similarity measure, and uncertainty event AC/AN, marker-eligible denominator, partial/no-call/unphased counts, and stratum AC/AN source VCF URI/generation, database, release, run_id, accepted status, and query timestamp ancestry/sampling caveats, P/I/B classes, reviewer state, filters, and forbidden interpretation
Handoff roles: Structural-variation analyst Statistical geneticist/phasing reviewer BRCA1 disease-area scientist Callset/data-semantics owner Clinical genetics safety reviewer.

acceptanceTest.actions: Load chr17:43073282-43163674 under one accepted HGSVC/HPRC chr17 state. Match both boundaries, type, orientation, and event linkage against all four templates. Inspect chromosome-copy carriers and phase-set/read evidence. For exact ins6kbEx13 only, apply the pinned marker template and inspect concordant, discordant, missing, and unphased markers. Inspect class-specific AC/AN, strata, no-calls, provenance, and export/reload the receipt.
acceptanceTest.expected: A, B, and C form three separate exact deletion groups despite shared exon dosage. D is exact tandem-duplication architecture and receives a descriptive marker result with uncertainty, never a causal founder verdict. E is exact architecture with marker/founder comparison unavailable. F is different architecture/candidate overlap, never exact recurrence. G is partial/data-blocked, never zero. The CHEK2 rs986514763 marker is never used in the BRCA1 template. AN=584, nearby record AN, or the paper's 19 carriers is never substituted for event-level callability. evidence.claim: The study sequenced 19 previously identified carriers from 18 families with deletions or duplications in BRCA1, BRCA2, CHEK2, or PALB2. The 19 carriers represented 14 distinct SVs from 510 bp to 108 kb; this is an ascertained known-positive cohort, not a prevalence sample.
evidence.citation: Dixon et al. 2023 main PDF pp. 1-2 (journal pp. 602-603), Results and Table 1

evidence.claim: Median genome coverage was 21.6X (13.1-36.5X), median read N50 was 14.5 kb (6.57-23.5 kb), all known SVs had at least three supporting reads, and one breakpoint remained imprecise because of low coverage and low-complexity sequence.
evidence.citation: Dixon et al. 2023 main PDF p. 2 (journal p. 603); Supplementary Table S2

evidence.claim: Three clinically similar BRCA1 exon 1-2 deletions were molecularly distinct on GRCh38: P1 NC_000017.11:g.43118925_43156395del (37,471 bp inclusive), P2 g.43122618_43158674del (36,057 bp inclusive), and P3 g.43121293_43127941del (6,649 bp inclusive).
evidence.citation: Dixon et al. 2023 main PDF Table 1 and Fig. 1, pp. 2-3 (journal pp. 603-604); Supplementary Tables S1-S2

evidence.claim: P1 and P2 had telomeric breakpoints in intron 1 of the partial BRCA1 pseudogene LOC101929767 and were approximately 36-37 kb; P3 had a telomeric breakpoint in NBR2 intron 1 and was 6.649 kb. Shared exon loss therefore did not imply shared exact architecture.
evidence.citation: Dixon et al. 2023 main PDF pp. 2-3, Fig. 1 and legend (journal pp. 603-604)

evidence.claim: The British BRCA1 ins6kbEx13 founder event was an exact 6,126 bp tandem duplication, NC_000017.11:g.43078282_43084407dup, found in three unrelated participants P17-P19. Table 1 reports their ancestry collectively as Britain and Unknown.
evidence.citation: Dixon et al. 2023 main PDF p. 2 and Table 1; Supplementary Tables S1-S2 and Fig. S2

evidence.claim: All three ins6kbEx13 carriers were missed by the available agnostic SV-calling step despite 13, 22, and 4 supporting reads, respectively; manual review and local assembly/read evidence were used. Thus even a known recurrent duplication was not representation-complete under the paper's caller path.
evidence.citation: Dixon et al. 2023 Discussion, main PDF p. 4 (journal p. 605); Supplementary Methods and Table S2 rows P17-P19

evidence.claim: Founder-haplotype inference integrated read-based phasing with SHAPEIT4 reference-guided phasing from a 1000 Genomes Phase 3 panel of 2,504 individuals, then assigned reads with WhatsHap. Joint SNVs required at least 15X in all study samples and variants with missing genotypes were excluded.
evidence.citation: Dixon et al. 2023 main PDF p. 2; Supplementary Methods pp. 1-2

evidence.claim: Among 13 genomes with at least 20X average coverage, read information alone phased 77-92% of heterozygous SNVs; longer reads were associated with larger haplotype blocks (Spearman correlation 0.78). These are study performance observations, not a guarantee for every locus or browser record.
evidence.citation: Dixon et al. 2023 main PDF p. 2 (journal p. 603); Supplementary Fig. S1

evidence.claim: SNVs extending beyond the BRCA1 duplication defined a shared core haplotype of 1.08 Mb. The supplied article and supplement do not enumerate the BRCA1 marker IDs, exact core boundaries, distance metric, or statistical threshold; Supplementary Fig. S2 shows one representative carrier locally.
evidence.citation: Dixon et al. 2023 main PDF p. 2 (journal p. 603); Supplementary Fig. S2 and caption

evidence.claim: The paper's explicitly identified rare marker belongs to the separate CHEK2 del5395 analysis: NC_000022.11:g.28801711G>T (rs986514763), about 100 kb upstream, within a 1.26 Mb core. It must not be reused as a BRCA1 marker.
evidence.citation: Dixon et al. 2023 main PDF p. 2; Supplementary Fig. S3 and caption

evidence.claim: The authors caution that reference-guided phasing accuracy depends on reference-panel composition and size and that many populations are underrepresented. The study table uses broad reported-ancestry labels, including Britain, South East Asia, and Unknown.
evidence.citation: Dixon et al. 2023 main PDF Table 1 and Discussion p. 4 (journal p. 605)

evidence.claim: The faithful browser workflow clusters exact linked breakpoint architecture first. P1, P2, P3, and ins6kbEx13 are four separate architecture groups even though the first three share an exon-level clinical label.
evidence.citation: Analyst reconstruction from P3-P6; requires structural-variation review

evidence.claim: A corrected 90,393 bp overview, chr17:43073282-43163674, includes 5 kb flanks around all eight boundaries in the concrete four-event set. The generic chr17:43057270-43157270 window excludes the P2 distal boundary by 1,404 bp and must not be called an exact event view.
evidence.citation: Analyst coordinate arithmetic from P3 and P5; requires product review

evidence.claim: Founder comparison is a second-stage descriptive operation only among exact-event carriers. It must report marker interval/list, compared and missing markers, phase-block continuity, similarity measure, and uncertainty; without the paper's BRCA1 marker definition it is unavailable, not negative.
evidence.citation: Analyst reconstruction from P7-P11; requires statistical-genetics review

evidence.claim: Independent 201 bp boundary-context requests from NCBI NC_000017.11 and Ensembl GRCh38 agreed exactly at all eight paper boundaries, supporting direct GRCh38 routing without liftover. This does not independently validate patient junction sequence.
evidence.citation: Read-only NCBI EFetch and Ensembl REST checks, 2026-08-11; hashes in companion evidence markdown

evidence.claim: The deployed corrected and generic region routes returned HTTP 200, while the BRCA1 workflow-detail route and deployed /papers/106.pdf returned 404. Current source commit 7c8c7b974 has 20 workflow records but none for ref 106. Route 200 proves navigation only.
evidence.citation: Read-only deployed route and source-record checks, 2026-08-11

evidence.claim: The live API returned 2,002 allele rows from 1,454 source IDs in chr17:43073282-43163674 under accepted chr17 Y1 primary/haplotype run y1-full-prototype-hgsvc-hprc-chr17-20260728-r1. No row began or ended at any of the eight paper boundaries.

evidence.claim: The checked live window contained a different 17,096 bp tandem-duplication-labeled record at chr17:43074533 (AC=1, AN=2) and a common 126 bp duplication-labeled insertion at chr17:43128198 (AC=185, AN=584). Neither is the exact 6,126 bp founder duplication or one of the three exact deletions.

evidence.claim: The live 90,393 bp haplotype response exposed 584 chromosome-copy rows and 1,514 deterministically placeable variants. Its aggregate phase summary contained 64,135 carrier rows: 31,475 phased, 23,424 unphased homozygous-alt, and 9,236 ambiguous unphased rows. The 17 kb tandem-duplication candidate was absent from that payload, but the aggregate receipt does not attribute the omission to that record specifically.

evidence.claim: Current source excludes unphased heterozygous/partial ALT calls from deterministic haplotype placement, preserves optional per-record PS values, and caps Y1 Haplotype View at 100 kb. It has no 1.08 Mb founder-template or cross-tile phase receipt.
evidence.citation: graphql-api/src/queries/long_read_y1_haplotypes.ts:4-13, 62-70, 162-201; browser/src/LongReadVariantPage/LongReadUnifiedView.tsx:313, 388-411; source commit 7c8c7b974

evidence.claim: The generation-pinned chr17 HGSVC/HPRC VCF header declares allele_type, END, SVTYPE, GT, and PS but no EVENT, MATEID, or CHR2. Raw INFO is stored only in summaries; canonical alleles/GraphQL expose no junction/mate object or event-callable/no-call denominator. Frontend grouping uses exact family/anchor rules and explicitly treats overlap as insufficient.
